stories.summary: BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput slapped the in-charge of the government agricultural seed store in Mahoba on Wednesday. He told him, "You have met Akhilesh Yadav. Why do you want to sacrifice poor people? Whom were you sending the seeds to? Why don't you say? Get a garland of shoes brought for them and take them out in a procession dressed in a lehenga and chunri. They will not listen otherwise." Brijbhushan, the MLA from the Charkhari Assembly seat, had arrived following a complaint about the black marketing of chickpea seeds. When he saw around 100 sacks of chickpea seeds loaded onto a pickup at the site, he lost his temper. When the store in-charge, Sonu Yadav, failed to give a proper answer to his questions, the MLA slapped him three times in succession. A video of the incident has also emerged. As soon as the Agriculture Department and police teams learnt of the matter, they reached the spot. The pickup and the sacks of chickpea seeds were seized. Acting on a complaint filed by the Agriculture Department, police detained three people, including the store in-charge. The seeds seized from the pickup are said to be worth ₹4 lakh to ₹5 lakh. The incident took place in Charkhari, 20 km from the district headquarters. See two photos... Arrived with supporters following a complaint of black marketing According to the police, MLA Brijbhushan Rajput arrived with his supporters at the government agricultural seed store in Charkhari following a complaint of black-marketing of government seed. It is alleged that, in the presence of warehouse in-charge Sonu Yadav, seed meant to be distributed free of cost to farmers was being loaded into a pickup and taken away. After receiving information about the incident, acting District Agriculture Officer BC Vishwakarma reached the spot with police personnel on the instructions of the Deputy Agriculture Director. Read in detail what the video shows In the 2.37-minute video that has emerged in the case, the MLA can be heard saying, "We have become troubled because of you people. All the farmers are troubled because of this act of yours." He then called the Deputy Agriculture Director. He told the officer, "You people have no idea about anything. You neither asked us nor gave any order." He said, "He himself is saying that neither the DD nor the DO ordered us. He is not even saying whether the seeds were ordered by the in-charge of another centre. He is making up a fabricated story." After this, he grabbed the warehouse in-charge by the collar and said, "You have divine powers; you know everything." MLA says, ‘If these people do not understand, we will worship the sticks.’ MLA Brijbhushan Rajput said, "Our divisional president, Pushpendra Yadav, saw a pickup vehicle being loaded at the Agriculture Department's seed warehouse. On making inquiries, it was found that, despite the warehouse being closed, the warehouse in-charge was having bags of chickpea seeds loaded into the vehicle to take them away for sale." I was informed about this. I then reached the spot. When I took cognisance of the matter, it was found that the bags were being taken away without permission. When questioned, the warehouse in-charge attempted to mislead us. He said they were being taken to another warehouse. We then spoke to the centre in-charge in Kulpahar, who said that he was lying. We then asked the district agriculture officer whether he had ordered the bags to be taken away, but he also denied it, saying he had not issued any such order. The accused will now face a case and be sent to jail. They will lose their jobs. He alleged that warehouse in-charge Sonu Yadav was involved in black marketing. A peon and a pickup driver have also been caught in the case. More people may be involved. No one can carry out such a major operation alone. I warn them that if they do not mend their ways, they will also be beaten with sticks. Charkhari Kotwali in-charge Rahul Mishra said: Based on the complaint, a case has been registered against Sonu Yadav, the warehouse in-charge, and Radheshyam Sahu, a Class IV employee. stories.title: ‘Girl called my brother, then killed him’:Family alleges she pursued him even after marriage; bodies of lovers found hanging from a tree in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: "My brother was murdered and his body was hung from a tree. He worked in Lucknow. The girl called him and summoned him. Some boys were with her too. They threatened my brother, saying that if he went, he would still be trapped, and if he did not go, he would be trapped anyway. The last time he spoke, he said he would return shortly. After that, he was kidnapped and murdered, and his body was hung from a tree." This was said by the elder brother of the young man whose body was found hanging from a tree in Lakhimpur on Monday (19 October). The body of his girlfriend was also found hanging from another tree with the help of a dupatta, around 100 metres away. The young woman was five years older than the man. She had married the village head's son but was not going to her marital home. Her husband said that she had quarrelled with him and assaulted him ever since their marriage. According to villagers, the two had been having an affair for three years. The family had arranged the young woman's marriage elsewhere. The incident took place in the area under Padhua police station, 47 km from the district headquarters. The Daily Bhaskar team spoke to the young woman's maternal and marital families and the young man's relatives. Affair began at sister's marital home Ram Khilawan's family lives in Bechelal Purwa. His wife is Ram Devi, and they have seven children. His two daughters, Lajwanti and Lalita, are married. Lalita married Mukesh from Pachasa village, 10 km away. His third daughter, Rama (23), often visited her elder sister's home. Jitendra (18) lives in Pachasa village. His father, Shridhar, is a farmer. The family also includes his mother, Sunita, and elder brother, Dharmendra. Dharmendra and Jitendra worked in Lucknow. Around three years ago, Rama and Jitendra began an affair as she visited her sister's home. Fifteen months ago, the family arranged Rama's marriage Rama and Jitendra used to speak on the phone, but their families were unaware of it. Rama often visited her elder sister's home. Around fifteen months ago, her father, Ram Khilawan, married her to Kamal Kishore (25) from Danduri village. Rama was not ready for the marriage. Kamal Kishore's mother, Meena Devi, is the village head. His father, Chunni Lal, looks after the village head's duties. Kamal's three sisters are married. The family also has a younger brother and a younger sister. The girl would not stay at her in-laws' home Rama stayed at her in-laws' home for the first few days of the marriage, then returned to her maternal home. The family tried several times to send her back to her in-laws, but she kept returning. She had been living at her maternal home for the past two months and was unwilling to return to her in-laws. Rama suddenly went missing from home on Sunday (18 October) morning. Meanwhile, Jitendra also left Lucknow at night carrying some money. He had told his brother that he would return shortly. The family searched for both of them throughout the night. The next morning, the bodies of Rama and Jitendra were found hanging from two separate trees around 100 metres apart. Jitendra's body was hanging from a noose made from his trousers, while Rama had used her dupatta to make a noose. When villagers saw the bodies in the morning, they informed both families. The police conducted post-mortems on the bodies. The reports confirmed that they died by hanging. Now read what the deceased man's brother said... Jitendra's elder brother, Dharmendra, said, "We both worked in Lucknow. At night, Jitendra received a phone call from a girl. Some boys were with her. They threatened him, saying that he would be implicated whether he went there or stayed away. Out of fear, Jitendra left with some money. When we asked him, he said he was going to Madhia and would return shortly." "He was kidnapped on the way. At around 11 p.m. that night, the girl's father came to our house. He threatened us, saying that there would be serious consequences if we did not find the girl and bring her back. My father told him that they would find his daughter and bring her back in the morning." "By the time we reached the spot in the morning, the body had already been taken down. No video recording was made while the body was being taken down either. My brother was murdered and his body was hung up. We want justice." Father says police did not listen to them Jitendra's father, Shridhar, said that his son had left Lucknow at 8:30 p.m. He was kidnapped on the way. The girl's father came to me at night and said that I should return the girl so that the honour of both families could be saved. I told him that we would find the girl and return her in the morning. At 6 a.m., we received a call saying that my son had hanged himself. When we reached the spot, the body had already been taken down from the tree and packed. When we asked to see the body, only the face was shown to us, after which it was packed again. My son did not die by suicide. If that had been the case, both of them would have been found hanging from the same tree by a rope or dupatta. Shridhar has alleged that people from Rama's in-laws' family may have arranged his son's murder. He said that his son had never told him anything about the girl. Shridhar alleges that the police are not acting on his complaint. The other side has paid the police. He is not satisfied with the police action and wants justice for his son. Husband said-My wife had assaulted me several times Rama's husband, Kamal Kishore, said that just days after their marriage, his wife had gone to her parental home. She did not treat him well. He went several times to bring Rama back, but she was unwilling to return with him. Even after he complained to the police, she refused to go to her in-laws' home. Rama often quarrelled and said that her family had forced her into the marriage. She said she had become trapped by getting married. Kamal alleged that Rama had assaulted him several times. Father-in-law said-daughter-in-law did not want to live with her son Rama's father-in-law, Chunnilal, said that his daughter-in-law had stayed at her in-laws' home for barely one and a half months. She used to argue and fight with his son. After the incident, he learnt that his daughter-in-law was having an affair with someone. Responding to the allegation that Jitendra had been murdered, Chunnilal said that he himself had cancer and had undergone an operation six months earlier. Girl's father says daughter never told him about an affair Rama's father, Ram Khilawan, said that his daughter had been living at her maternal home. She left the house at 5:30 a.m. without informing anyone. The family searched for her throughout the day and night, but found no information. The following morning, the village head informed them that Rama and Jitendra's bodies had been found hanging from a tree. Jitendra belonged to the Harijan community, while we are Lodhi farmers. If there had been no affair between them, why would they have hanged themselves together? Our daughter never told us anything about it at home. If she had told us earlier, we would have tried to find a solution. However, getting her married to Jitendra was difficult because they belonged to different communities. Station House Officer Mohit Pundir said The post-mortem report found hanging to be the cause of death. The two were having an affair and died by suicide. So far, no complaint has been received from either side.

stories.title: Students selling blood to fund their education:NEET aspirant in UP says, ‘Blood will keep regenerating, but I won’t get another chance to study’
stories.summary: Students are being forced to sell their blood to pay for their education. Coming from poor families, they struggle to afford expensive NEET and SSC coaching, hostel accommodation and mess fees. To raise money, some students sell their blood twice a month, while others do so as many as four times. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar’s hidden camera, these students described their helplessness. “My father is a farmer, but we do not own enough land to cover all the household expenses through farming. So, we manage our education expenses ourselves. Sometimes, we even send the money we earn by selling our blood to our village,” they said. Students in several Uttar Pradesh cities have reportedly started selling their blood to cope with financial hardship while pursuing their studies. After receiving information about the practice, Dainik Bhaskar chose Prayagraj for its investigation, as thousands of students come to the city to prepare for NEET and SSC examinations. Reporters went undercover, posing as relatives of patients, to approach students. Here is the full investigation report. Unable to pay hostel fees for two months, student turns to blood bank Dainik Bhaskar’s undercover reporters visited the Allahabad Medical Association (AMA) Blood Bank at Rajapur Crossing in Prayagraj, described as the city’s largest blood bank. They spotted several students outside and told them they needed blood. During the conversation, one student said he was preparing for the SSC examination while living in Prayagraj. He was the only son in his family. His father was a farmer, his mother had died, and his two younger sisters lived in the village, where they continued their studies and managed household responsibilities. “Farming earns us just enough to get by. I had to sell my blood because I had not been able to pay my hostel fees for two months. I kept thinking that if I lost my place to stay, how would I continue my studies? That is what brought me to the blood bank,” he said. Reporter: We need three units of blood, but we cannot find donors. Student: I need money. I can donate blood for a payment. Reporter: How much will it cost? Student: Give me ₹8,000, and I will donate blood for you. Reporter: You are studying. Why have you had to sell your blood? Student: My father is a farmer, and coaching fees are very high. The money I get from home is not enough to cover all my expenses. Reporter: Why are you selling blood? You could teach coaching classes or give tuition instead. Student: My blood will be replenished, but if I do not study, I will remain unemployed. Reporter: How much of your expenses can you cover by selling blood? Does it cause any problems? Student: It does for a few days, but covering my expenses is more important. Otherwise, I will have to return to my village. ‘My father is Ill, and I have to send money home’ During the investigation, reporters met Anand, another student preparing for the SSC examination. He had come to the blood bank to pay his coaching fees. Just 10 days earlier, he had sold his blood to pay his mess bill, although he had gone to a different blood bank that time. Anand said he was enduring these hardships in the hope of becoming a government officer one day, which he believed would help him overcome his family’s financial difficulties. Reporter: You have come to donate blood… Student: Yes, but I donated blood 10 days ago at another blood bank. Anyway, I will donate here. Reporter: How much will you have to be paid? Student: You will have to pay ₹8,000. I cannot do it for any less. Reporter: You are a student. Why are you selling your blood? Student: I need the money. I sold my blood earlier to pay my coaching fees, and now I have to pay my mess bill. Reporter: How can you donate blood twice in 10 days? What if you face health problems? Student: I will not have any problems. I am doing this to cover my education expenses. Reporter: Doesn't the blood bank staff catch you? Student: First, we donate blood and collect the slip. Then we take the patient's demand letter and collect the blood. We have to do something to manage our expenses. NEET aspirant says his father went into debt to send him to Prayagraj Outside the blood bank, we met another student preparing for NEET named Vivek. He said no one sells blood willingly. “My father has high hopes for me. To send me to Prayagraj for my studies, he mortgaged two bighas of farmland. He fell into debt, but I still could not clear the exam. Now I have only one attempt left,” Vivek said. Reporter: You have come to donate blood… Student: Yes, I need to pay my coaching fees before Diwali. Reporter: Don't you get money from home? Student: My father is a farmer and cannot even cover the household expenses. If I get money by selling my blood, I will be able to pay the fees. Reporter: Did you come here because an agent called you? Student: Yes, he called me, but he deducts a portion of the money. I get a better amount when I deal directly. Reporter: Do you have no other option besides selling blood? Student: If my family were financially better off, I would not face this problem. But we are struggling, so I donate blood whenever an emergency arises. Many students arrange money this way We met another student, Ashish, who was also preparing for NEET and had come to the blood bank to sell his blood. He was waiting outside the premises for a patient when we approached him. Ashish said many students who come to Prayagraj from other places to pursue their studies arrange money this way. Although their accommodation and food expenses are relatively manageable, coaching fees are expensive. Speaking about his family, he said, “When my father sent me here, he believed I would return as a doctor. How many times can I tell him about every small expense, and for how long? So, I arrange the money this way.” Reporter: Have you donated blood before? Student: Yes, we are taking NEET coaching here at PW. Reporter: Why do you donate blood? Student: We are taking coaching, and we do not get financial support from home, so we have to do this. Reporter: Aren’t you asking for too much money? Student: It is not too much money. This is a student’s blood; an addict sells it for less. After speaking to four students, three things became clear: Brokers exploit students’ financial distress The investigation revealed that while students are selling their blood out of financial desperation, a larger network of brokers is also operating. Brokers active around blood banks remain in contact with students who are ready to donate blood at a single phone call. Students said different hostel groups exist, and many of them receive calls from agents who arrange deals with patients and then summon students to donate blood. Posing as a student, Dainik Bhaskar’s undercover reporter struck a deal with one such broker, Sonu. He was found outside the Allahabad Medical Association Blood Bank in Prayagraj. Reporter: Sir, I need one unit of blood. How much will I get? Sonu: We will pay you ₹4,000. Reporter: My friends who study with me were saying I should ask for ₹8,000. You are offering too little. Sonu: Arranging blood directly is risky; you could get caught. Blood bank staff keep an eye on things. We make arrangements in such a way that students do not face any trouble. That is why we take a cut from the money received. Reporter: I am a student, not a drug addict. Please increase the amount a little. I am facing a lot of financial difficulties these days. Sonu: The amount will not increase. Everyone gets the same. We have to cover all the risks. After repeated requests, the agent agreed to pay ₹5,000 but still told the student to pay the processing fee. The conversation then continued. Reporter: I donated blood 20 days ago as well. There won't be any problems, will there? Sonu: You won't face any problems. How can students wait that long? They donate blood twice a month. If you need money, you have to do it. Reporter: If the blood bank staff recognise me, will they catch me and take action? Sonu: We arrange blood through different blood banks, so students are never caught. If there is a problem in Prayagraj, we get the work done in neighbouring districts. During the deal, Sonu and his associate Rajesh claimed that they arranged more than 12 units of blood in a day. They said they could provide hospital stamps, fake doctors, prescriptions and demand letters. They claimed these arrangements were intended to protect donors and said they kept fake hospital demand letters ready in advance. During the investigation, the students captured on hidden camera are being published with their faces blurred and names changed because they want to secure their future. The cost of education is driving Students to Sell Their Blood According to students, coaching institutes such as Aakash Institute, Allen Career Institute and Narayana charge annual fees ranging from ₹1.20 lakh to ₹1.80 lakh, usually in a single payment. A hostel room costs between ₹3,500 and ₹5,000 a month. Students must also pay for study materials and food. The government offers free coaching through the Abhyudaya scheme, but admission is subject to eligibility criteria that not all students can meet. Selling blood is a crime and can lead to imprisonment and fines In India, selling blood or donating it in exchange for money is illegal. In 1996, the Supreme Court imposed a complete ban on the commercial sale and purchase of blood in the country under the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Only voluntary blood donation is permitted. What punishment and fines can be imposed? Understand the health risks of donating blood too frequently Brajesh Kumar, Assistant Commissioner in Prayagraj’s Food and Drug Administration Department, said medical science has established standards for blood donation by men and women. The government has also issued guidelines that every blood bank must follow. He warned that repeatedly donating blood while concealing personal information could be life-threatening.

stories.title: SP aims to wrest Ayodhya temple issue from BJP:Akhilesh to visit Ram Lalla after worship at Kedarnath; reaches out to Sanatan voters ahead of 2027 elections
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav will visit Ayodhya to offer prayers at the Ram temple ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Before that, he will worship Lord Shiva at the Kedareshwar Temple in Etawah. Both religious visits are scheduled for November, after Diwali. Are these visits driven by Sanatan faith or political gains? To understand the context, it is necessary to look back at the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. In February 2024, a Shaligram stone brought from Nepal arrived at the Samajwadi Party (SP) office in Lucknow. Akhilesh Yadav and his wife, Dimple Yadav, performed prayers according to Vedic rituals. The stone was later taken to Etawah and installed in the sanctum sanctorum of the Kedareshwar Temple. Subsequently, the SP’s vote share increased by 15.64 percentage points in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. After winning five seats each in 2014 and 2019, the party’s tally rose sharply to 37 seats in 2024. Akhilesh now appears to recognise that relying solely on the PDA coalition of Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and minorities may not be enough to win elections. He also needs the support of upper-caste voters. This is one reason religious imagery has become more prominent in his politics. At times, he is seen seeking blessings from Shankaracharyas and saints; at others, he organises Brahmin conventions. Pictures of him wearing yellow clothes and holding a trident, damru and chakra have also emerged. Read the report on the SP’s changing political strategy ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections… Akhilesh seeks to expand SP’s support base beyond MY and PDA The Samajwadi Party’s politics remained centred on the MY (Muslim-Yadav) equation for a long time. The 2024 Lok Sabha elections gave the party an opportunity to broaden its support base. For the first time, it received support from extremely backward classes as well as Dalits. Now, ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, Akhilesh Yadav wants to extend this support base to upper-caste communities. His focus is on Brahmins, who account for around 12% of Uttar Pradesh’s population. Brahmins have been among the BJP’s core voter groups in the past four elections. Akhilesh also wants to counter the perception that the SP is opposed to Sanatan traditions. This is one reason his conduct has reflected elements of soft Hindutva since 2024. The party is likely to feature more Brahmin leaders, saints and religious events in its activities. The party has announced Tej Narayan Pandey, popularly known as Pawan Pandey, as its candidate from Ayodhya. Akhilesh announced his candidature at a Brahmin convention. When it came to appointing the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, he chose Mata Prasad Pandey, a Brahmin leader from eastern Uttar Pradesh. On 5 August, the party organised events aimed at the intellectual community to mark the birth anniversary of Janeshwar Mishra. Akhilesh wants to convey that the PDA coalition has room not only for social justice but also for upper-caste communities, particularly Brahmins. Referring to the friendship between Lord Krishna and Sudama, he has also spoken about social equality and respect. Why Akhilesh wants to shed the image of being opposed to Sanatan traditions Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says the BJP, which the Samajwadi Party (SP) is competing against in Uttar Pradesh, has built its politics around Hindutva. Its success relies on social polarisation, while development has also been used to expand its support base. This is why the SP is having to change its longstanding image. Muslims continue to stand firmly with the party, but Akhilesh Yadav does not want to be seen as someone who focuses exclusively on Muslim interests. Akhilesh’s real test will be on three fronts Akhilesh to inaugurate Kedareshwar Temple in bid to shed anti-Sanatan image Akhilesh Yadav began efforts to shed the perception that he is opposed to Sanatan traditions after the Samajwadi Party’s victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. One of the most prominent examples was his taking a holy dip during the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj, while his INDIA bloc allies, including Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and other prominent leaders, largely stayed away from the event. When the controversy over the alleged insult to a Shankaracharya emerged, Akhilesh quickly responded. He spoke to the Shankaracharya and expressed his support for standing up for his dignity. Later, his wife, Dimple Yadav, met Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand, followed by Akhilesh himself. Whenever the Shankaracharya visited Lucknow, Akhilesh was seen seeking his blessings. Now, ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Akhilesh is preparing for a grand inauguration of the Kedareshwar Mahadev Temple in Etawah. After the inauguration, he also plans to visit the Ram temple in Ayodhya to offer prayers. Akhilesh visited Ayodhya on 8 October this month and attended a Shrimad Bhagwat Katha organised at the residence of SP leader Pawan Pandey. During the visit, he said he would go to the Ram temple only after the Kedareshwar Dham in Etawah was completed. “A vow is not taken repeatedly,” he said. Political observers describe Akhilesh’s approach as ‘neo-socialism’ Senior journalist Sharat Pradhan says the BJP has made the Ram temple a major issue in its politics. This has created a challenge for the Samajwadi Party (SP): how to retain the support of backward classes, Dalits and minorities while responding to accusations that it distances itself from Hinduism. According to Pradhan, the SP has continued to raise questions over issues such as alleged irregularities in donations for the Ram temple to challenge the BJP’s Hindutva politics on its own ground. At the same time, the party is trying to reassure Hindu voters that it is not opposed to Sanatan Dharma through religious symbolism, including temple construction, meetings with saints, wearing yellow clothes and reciting the Hanuman Chalisa. Akhilesh Yadav’s promise to build a Vishwakarma temple, schemes related to cattle, meetings with Dalit saints, and statements such as “Socialism itself is Ram Rajya” and “What is Sanatan is also socialism” are seen as part of this effort. However, challenging the BJP’s Hindutva politics and winning over its supporters are two different things. Religious activities may change Akhilesh’s public image, but their electoral impact will depend on how voters perceive them. The key question is whether voters see these steps as a genuine expression of religious faith or as a political exercise ahead of the elections. Is there a religious belief linking Shiva worship to darshan of Lord Ram? To understand Akhilesh Yadav’s resolve, it is important to examine the religious tradition associated with the relationship between Lord Shiva and Lord Ram. In the Ramcharitmanas, Lord Ram says: “Shiv drohi mam daas kahaava, So nar mohi sapnehu nahi bhaava.” This means that a person who bears enmity towards Lord Shiva cannot be considered a devotee of Lord Ram. Religious beliefs regard the worship of Lord Ram and Lord Shiva as symbols of mutual reverence and harmony. According to tradition, Lord Ram worshipped Shiva before setting out for Lanka and installed a Shivling at Rameswaram. How the Installation of Nandi Led to the Construction of a Temple The Kedareshwar Mahadev Temple, built in Sheetalpur village in Etawah district opposite the Lion Safari, is reminiscent of the Kedarnath Temple in Uttarakhand at first glance. Spread across around 11 acres, the project began with a massive statue of Nandi carved from black granite. According to Madhu Botta, an architect from Andhra Pradesh and a company director involved in the temple’s construction, he met Akhilesh Yadav in Delhi in 2009. During his engineering studies in Mysuru, Akhilesh had been impressed by the Nandi statue at the Chamundeshwari Temple. He wanted a similarly massive Nandi statue to be installed in Etawah. The Nandi statue was brought to Etawah in 2017. After seeing it, Akhilesh proposed building a grand Shiva temple at the site. Land for the temple was purchased in 2018, and the foundation-laying ceremony took place on 7 March 2021. The temple reflects architectural traditions from both North and South India. Its sanctum sanctorum draws inspiration from the Kedarnath Temple in Uttarakhand, while the complex incorporates distinctive granite and traditional stone-joining techniques associated with South Indian Dravidian architecture.

stories.title: Car runs over five people in Firozabad, killing four:Two girls among the victims, who were on their way to immerse Tesu idols
stories.summary: A speeding car hit villagers heading to immerse Tesu-Jhenjhi in Firozabad on Sunday night. Two girls died on the spot, while two other people succumbed to their injuries during treatment at the district hospital in Shikohabad. Three people were seriously injured in the accident. They have been referred to the Trauma Centre in Firozabad for treatment. The accident took place in the Nasirpur police station area. Sirsa Ganj MLA Sarvesh Yadav is present at the scene following the accident. Sirsa Ganj CO Chanchal Tyagi, Shikohabad CO Jabvinder Gupta, Shikohabad Inspector Anuj Kumar, Nasirpur Inspector Jasveer Singh, Sirsa Ganj Inspector Anil Kumar and Makkhanpur Inspector Chaman Sharma, along with other officials, are present at the scene. See pictures related to the accident... What are Tesu and Jhenjhi? • Tesu is a symbolic doll made from three bamboo sticks. It is dressed like a groom, with a lamp placed in the middle. • Jhenjhi (Jhanjhi) is a small clay pot or doll, decorated like a beautiful bride, with a lamp placed inside or around it for illumination. Mythological legend- • This tradition is believed to be associated with the era of the Mahabharata and the story of the warrior Barbarik (Khatu Shyam Ji). • According to popular belief, Barbarik was supposed to marry Jhenjhi, but their marriage remained incomplete because he donated his head during the war. In accordance with a boon granted by Lord Krishna, Tesu and Jhenjhi are symbolically married on Sharad Purnima in the Kali Yuga.

stories.title: Owaisi thanks Akhilesh for calling him Ravana:Asks why he failed to stop Muzaffarnagar riots despite having 32 Muslim MLAs
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi addressed a public meeting in Shamli on Sunday. He launched a scathing attack on Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Owaisi said, "Do we look like Ravana to you? Akhilesh indirectly shot an arrow at us. Thank you, Akhilesh Yadav. I have succeeded in my objective. I wanted to make poison spew from your tongue. I wanted it to become clear from your tongue how much you hate someone who keeps a beard and wears a cap. For you, every self-respecting Muslim is an enemy. In your eyes, every Muslim who wears a cap on his head and has a beard on his face looks like Ravana." Owaisi said, "I feel Akhilesh is not merely speaking in the BJP's language; Abu Jahl's spirit has now entered your body. Try speaking about someone else. Will you call Modi Ravana? If you call Modi Ravana, the River Front will be opened. The entire highway that was built-that file will be opened." Read Owaisi's three key points 'Three generations sacrificed their youth for the Akhilesh family' Targeting Akhilesh Yadav, Owaisi said that not one or two, but three generations had sacrificed their youth for the Akhilesh family. "We strengthened their political palaces by laying carpets for them. By voting for them repeatedly, we shattered the dreams of our young generations." 'What could SP's 32 Muslim MLAs do during the Muzaffarnagar riots?' Referring to the Muzaffarnagar riots, Owaisi criticised Akhilesh Yadav. He said, "We voted for him, so tell me, people of Muzaffarnagar and Kairana, is it not true that when Akhilesh was chief minister, you, we and the whole world saw with our own eyes how the Muzaffarnagar incident took place on this very land?" 50,000 people were displaced from their homes. Girls were attacked and children were orphaned. Those who had lived in their villages and on that land for 100 years were rendered homeless. Whose government was it? It was the Samajwadi Party government. Who was the chief minister? Akhilesh Yadav was the chief minister. “Those who are speaking today ask what will happen if five or 10 of Owaisi's MLAs win. I want to ask you: your party had 32 Muslim MLAs. Could you stop the Muzaffarnagar incident? You could not, because you are not the leader of Muslims. You were, and will remain, a slave of the Samajwadi Party.” Questions raised over MLA Nahid Hasan and MP Iqra Hasan At the public meeting, Owaisi targeted local MLA Nahid Hasan. Referring to the mob-lynching incidents in Shamli and the Thanabhawan area, he questioned what steps had been taken to ensure justice for the victims. He said public representatives had a responsibility to remain among the people and give priority to raising the problems of their constituencies. Owaisi also questioned Kairana MP Iqra Hasan. He said public representatives should answer questions on issues affecting the people and clarify their role in incidents occurring in the area. Raised issues of hospitals, street lights and the Jal Jeevan Mission Owaisi raised the issue of inadequate healthcare facilities in Kairana. He said people had to travel to cities such as Shamli, Meerut and Panipat for better treatment. He questioned who was responsible for improving hospital facilities in the area. In addition, he questioned the street light project and the work carried out under the Jal Jeevan Mission. Owaisi alleged that despite projects worth several crores, people were not receiving the expected facilities in many places. At the meeting, Owaisi also prominently raised the problems faced by sugarcane farmers. Referring to the farmers' outstanding payments, he demanded that the government ensure timely payment. He also backed the demand to raise the price of sugarcane to ₹600 per quintal. Owaisi said his party stood with the farmers in their fight for their rights. Expresses desire to field engineer Irfan as candidate During his speech, Owaisi made an important statement about Kairana politics. He said that the Majlis wanted engineer Irfan to be made the party's candidate from Kairana. He also appealed to those present to support engineer Irfan. Owaisi said that a candidate should work among the people for five years, rather than appearing only during elections. Targets Opposition over politics in Bihar and Seemanchal Owaisi targeted the RJD and Congress, referring to his party's performance in Bihar's Seemanchal region. He claimed that his party had sought seats to join the opposition alliance, but its demand was not accepted. He said that in politics, forming a government is not the only priority; it is also important to elect representatives who can strongly raise the issues of people's rights, the Constitution and the poor.

stories.title: DM, commissioners will be held responsible for voter list errors:UP bars computer operators from entering forms and orders checks on past entries
stories.summary: The Election Commission has taken a strict decision after irregularities were found in the voter lists in Pilibhit and Azamgarh. Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa said on Sunday that district magistrates and commissioners would be held responsible if discrepancies were found in the voter list. The data entered in Uttar Pradesh since the completion of the SIR will be checked. The CEO said, "The mistakes must not be repeated. If this happens, the responsibility of the Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) and computer assistants will be fixed." In addition, computer assistants have been barred from entering voter-list-related forms. The forms entered by computer assistants since the end date of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) on 10 April will be checked. The aim is to prevent the wrong names from being added to the voter list, the names of eligible voters from being removed and other irregularities. Computer assistants will not enter forms Instructions have also been issued to change the process of digitally recording applications received in physical form. These forms will no longer be entered by computer assistants. All such forms will be digitised by booth-level officers (BLOs) through the BLO app. The Election Commission believes that clear accountability must be established from the receipt of an application to its entry into the digital record. Instructions have therefore been issued to assign the responsibility for digitising physical forms directly to BLOs. They have also been instructed to preserve all applications received in physical form safely, so that they can be verified when required. The original documents must remain available during the investigation of any complaint. Divisional commissioners will also be held accountable Divisional commissioners will serve as roll observers to monitor the process of preparing the voter lists. They have been directed to closely supervise voter-list-related work in the districts of their respective divisions. If irregularities are found in any district and negligence in supervision is established, action will be taken against the officials concerned. District Election Officers have also been asked to regularly monitor the work of the officers under them and ensure that investigations into complaints related to the electoral roll are completed on time. The purpose of this arrangement is to ensure that any irregularity in the electoral roll is not considered limited only to lower-level employees. Instead, the role of the officers responsible for supervision should also be examined. Report sought from 4 districts on duplicate voters The Chief Electoral Officer also expressed displeasure over delays in taking action on complaints related to the electoral roll. The District Election Officers of Bulandshahr, Sitapur, Ghaziabad and Aligarh had not sent reports on the complaints on time. Expressing displeasure over this, Rinwa asked all concerned officers to send their reports at the earliest. The officers were told not to ignore complaints emerging through social media or other channels. They were instructed to investigate them and prepare reports based on the facts. Action must be taken within the stipulated time. Officials will not share their ERONET passwords To strengthen security and accountability in the digital management of electoral rolls, officials have been instructed not to share their ERONET login IDs and passwords with anyone else. All officials have also been directed to change their passwords immediately under the password policy.

stories.title: Legal adviser runs after woman professor with shoe:Registrar threatens to kill her in Prayagraj, says, ‘I will get you fired’
stories.summary: A case has come to light in Prayagraj in which a woman professor has accused a university registrar and legal adviser of verbal abuse and death threats. The allegations have been levelled against Registrar SS Mishra and Legal Adviser Sarvesh Mishra. Assistant Professor Dr Vandana Mishra said, “I was misbehaved with on 11 September. The legal adviser tried to hit me after taking off his shoe. I was threatened with dismissal from my job and the destruction of my career.” An FIR was registered on Sunday, 44 days after the alleged incident. The case falls under the jurisdiction of Sarai Inayat police station. Read the full story Dr Vandana Mishra has been working as an assistant professor at Nehru Gram Bharati Deemed University since 2019 and also heads the Department of Special Education. She said that on 11 September, between approximately 2.30pm and 5pm, she visited the office of Pro Vice-Chancellor Prof. Suresh Chandra Tiwari for departmental work related to admissions to the D.Ed Special Education (HI) course. The university’s legal adviser, Sarvesh Mishra, was also present. According to Dr Vandana, Sarvesh Mishra called Acting Registrar SS Mishra and asked him to come to the office after seeing her. She told the Pro Vice-Chancellor that the application and the necessary formalities had not been completed on time in 2025. As a result, the approval process for the D.Ed Special (HI) and M.Ed Special (HI) courses could not be completed. She said that if the relevant file and documents were made available, the application process for the next academic session could be completed. Registrar allegedly threatened to end professor’s career In her complaint, Dr Vandana Mishra alleged that Executive Registrar SS Mishra behaved inappropriately towards her, verbally abused her and threatened to kill her. She said he told her that he was the registrar and would take such written action against her that her career would be finished. She further alleged that Legal Adviser Sarvesh Mishra also began abusing her. He then took off his shoe and approached her while shouting. Frightened, she began crying. As the situation escalated, four to five employees who were outside the Pro Vice-Chancellor’s office rushed in and forcibly took Sarvesh Mishra outside. According to Dr Vandana, Sarvesh threatened to kill her and made objectionable remarks about her character. Legal adviser continued threats outside the office Dr Vandana alleged that Sarvesh Mishra continued abusing her after leaving the office. He reportedly threatened to make it difficult for her to continue working at the university and warned that he would do something so terrible to her that no one else had ever done anything like it. She also alleged that during this time, SS Mishra kept laughing at her and stared at her for around five minutes. Professor emailed VC and Pro-VC, approached Women’s Commission According to Dr Vandana Mishra, she emailed a written complaint to the Vice-Chancellor and Pro-Vice-Chancellor on 11 September, immediately after the incident. She also approached the Women’s Commission on 12 September. In addition, she sought action through the Chief Minister’s helpline, 1076, and the Police Commissioner. Vikrant Tiwari, who was the outpost in-charge at the time, investigated the complaint, but the matter did not progress further. Dr Vandana said she had to make repeated visits to get an FIR registered, despite having filed a complaint. Professor alleges pressure to sign compromise letter Dr Vandana alleged that the university later called her and asked her to appear before an inquiry committee. She claimed that she was blamed for the incident and pressured to sign a compromise letter. She has been on medical leave since the incident. She submitted another complaint at Sarai Inayat police station on 10 October. When no action followed, she visited the police station again two days ago, after which the FIR was registered. Demand to preserve CCTV footage Dr Vandana has asked the police to conduct an impartial investigation into the case and preserve the evidence related to the incident. She said CCTV footage from the Pro Vice-Chancellor's office and the corridor from 2:30 p.m. to 5 p.m. on 11 September should be preserved. ADCP Ganganagar Pushkar Verma said an FIR had been registered on the complaint of the victimised assistant professor. Further action will be taken based on the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Uttarakhand police arrest actress Urmila Sanawar in Saharanpur:Suresh Rathore’s daughter accuses her of demanding ₹5 crore
stories.summary: Haridwar Police have arrested Urmila Sanawar, who came under scrutiny over a viral audio recording naming the alleged VIP in the Ankita Bhandari murder case. Police detained her from her home in Govind Nagar, Saharanpur, on 25 October. According to police, a case had been registered at Ranipur police station on a complaint by the daughter of former MLA Suresh Rathore, alleging blackmail, a demand for ₹5 crore and threats to kill her. Police arrested Urmila within 12 hours of taking action. The mobile phone allegedly used in the incident was also recovered from her. Urmila's arrest came at a time when the Dehradun CBI court was scheduled to hear the matter again on 26 October regarding her narco and polygraph tests. After appearing in court on 23 October, Urmila had said she had been asked to consider giving her consent for the narco test. According to Haridwar police, Urmila has been arrested in connection with a case registered against her and will be produced in court today. As the police took her to court, Urmila said, "This is how revolutionaries leave." Case filed at Ranipur police station on daughter's complaint According to the police, a woman from Tehri Displaced Colony filed a complaint at Ranipur Kotwali on the night of 24 October. The complainant is the daughter of former MLA Suresh Rathore. Urmila allegedly made obscene and defamatory comments on social media, tarnishing her and her family's reputation. The complaint also alleged that Urmila made a WhatsApp call demanding that the property of Ravidas Dham be transferred to her name and that ₹5 crore be paid. She was also accused of threatening to kill the complainant if these demands were not met. Based on the complaint, the police registered case crime number 387/26. The case was registered under Sections 308(5)(7), 79, 356(3) and 356(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and Sections 4/10 of the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986. The police arrested her in the case today. What happened in court on 23 October? Earlier, the CBI had issued notices to Urmila Sanawar and former BJP MLA Suresh Rathore in connection with its investigation into a viral audio mentioning the name of an alleged VIP. Both appeared before the CBI court in Dehradun on 23 October. The court heard arguments regarding Urmila's narco and polygraph tests. After the hearing, Urmila said she had been asked to appear in court again on 26 October. She was also asked to consider whether she consented to the narco test. What had been said about the narco test? Urmila had claimed that if her narco test was conducted properly and in front of live cameras, several secrets linked to the Ankita Bhandari murder case and other cases could come to light. She had said that she would not back down. Meanwhile, former MLA Suresh Rathore had said that he would fully cooperate with the CBI investigation and was y to undergo a narco test. Controversy over the VIP's name in viral audio Alleged audio and video recordings of conversations between Suresh Rathore and Urmila Sanawar went viral in December 2025. They contained claims about the alleged VIP linked to the Ankita Bhandari murder case. The names of former BJP leaders were also mentioned in these claims. However, the identity of the alleged VIP and the authenticity of the viral audio are matters under investigation. Dushyant Kumar Gautam had rejected the allegations against him and described them as a conspiracy to damage his image. The CBI is investigating the facts related to the case.

stories.title: Murder accused stages his own death by burning a goat:Uses AI to create funeral pyre image, lives as a monk in Mau for 18 months before arrest
stories.summary: In Mau, an accused staged his own death to avoid punishment in a murder case. According to the police, Raju alias Rajkumar Rajbhar, who had studied only up to Class 10, had a goat's carcass burned to make it appear that he was dead. He then used artificial intelligence (AI) to have a fake photograph created showing him lying on his own funeral pyre. His family even performed his thirteenth-day death ceremony. The accused obtained forged death certificates from the cremation ground and the municipal corporation and submitted them to the court. He then went into hiding. For nearly one and a half years, he evaded the police while disguised as a holy man. However, the police arrested him from Khwajahanpur village at around 9 a.m. on Sunday. Raju had been wanted in connection with the 2016 murder of Yogesh Singh. The case was being heard in court. According to the police, he feared that the court might sentence him to life imprisonment. To avoid this, he conspired to have himself declared dead. See 2 pictures... Now, read the full story The case falls under the Kotwali Nagar police station area. The accused was identified as 38-year-old Raju alias Rajkumar Rajbhar, a resident of Khwajajahanpur. His father, Ramnath, has died. Raju, his wife, their four children and his elderly mother make up the family. According to the police, accused Raju lived disguised as a holy man and would occasionally return home at night to meet his wife. He worked as a mason. However, he was also skilled in online trading. He took money from people by promising to increase their funds and invested it in the stock market. Money dispute: Brick kiln owner was murdered According to the police, Rajkumar and his friend Sudarshan Rajbhar had bought bricks from kiln owner Yogesh Singh. A dispute later arose over the payment. Yogesh Singh was shot dead near the Munshipura railway line on 19 December 2016. On a complaint filed by Yogesh Singh's nephew, Avinash Singh, a case was registered against Rajkumar Rajbhar and his friend Sudarshan Rajbhar at Kotwali Nagar. The trial in the murder case was under way. During this period, the accused hatched a conspiracy to show himself as dead in order to evade legal action. On 30 May 2025, he had himself declared dead in Ghazipur. For this, an image of a body lying on a funeral pyre was created using AI. A goat's carcass was burned to make people believe he had died Additional Superintendent of Police Anoop Kumar said that Raju, aged around 38, had earlier worked in Mumbai. He later became involved in share market trading and the cryptocurrency business. According to the police, the accused was allegedly rendered unconscious and taken to hospital. His photographs were then altered to make it appear as though he had been taken to the cremation ground for his last rites. A goat's carcass was allegedly burned there so that people would believe he had died. After this, documents including certificates related to the cremation and death were prepared. The accused also had an invitation card printed for the thirteenth-day ceremony on 11 June. It is alleged that a death certificate was also obtained from the Mau Municipal Council on the basis of forged documents. After submitting these documents in court, the accused absconded. Wife performed the thirteenth-day ceremony, investigation into ₹10 lakh insurance According to the police, the accused Rajkumar's wife was informed of his death. The family then performed the thirteenth-day ceremony. The police have also learnt that the wife received insurance money of around ₹10 lakh. Police are now investigating the circumstances under which the insurance payment was made and whether a death certificate was used. So far, no irregularity related to the insurance has been confirmed. Role of two homeopathic doctors under investigation According to the police, several people had invested money in Rajkumar's trading business. Two homeopathic doctors were among them. According to the accused's alleged statement, the doctors had advised him to pretend to be dead. Police are also investigating whether, besides avoiding punishment, the motive behind having himself declared dead was to avoid returning the investors' money. The role of both doctors is still under investigation. They will be questioned. Had been changing locations for 18 months According to the Additional Superintendent of Police, the Civil Lines police team was searching for the accused. He had been continuously changing his hideouts for 18 months. The police received information that he was in Khwajajahanpur village. They then raided the location and arrested him. The police are now investigating the preparation of the alleged fake death certificate, tampering with photographs and the role of others involved in the entire case. Action will be taken against anyone found to be involved in the investigation.

stories.title: Bank manager’s wife found dead in hotel room:Married in Jhansi four months ago, father accuses son-in-law of murder
stories.summary: The body of a bank manager's wife was found at a hotel in Jhansi. She had got married just four months earlier. She had come to her parents' home on 10 October to take the junior engineer exam. Her husband arrived two days later. The couple stayed at a hotel on Saturday night. On Sunday afternoon, the husband took his wife to hospital with the help of hotel staff while she was covered in blood. Doctors there declared Muskaan, 27, dead. Her father said, "My son-in-law Nilesh took my daughter with him by lying to her. He said they were going to her maternal aunt's house, but took her to a hotel. There are serious injury marks on my daughter's head. My son-in-law killed her by holding her mouth and smashing her head against the wall." After the incident, the police reached the hotel and conducted an investigation. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The cause of death will become clear only after the report is received. For now, the police have taken her husband, Nilesh, into custody. Now, here is the full story... Ramjilal Simoliya, a resident of Premnagar, said, "My daughter Muskaan married Nilesh, a resident of Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh, on 29 June. We held her wedding with great ceremony at Hotel JS Grand. Muskaan had her JE exam on 28 October. I thought she could sit the exam and stay with me for a few days." We did not know that Nilesh would suddenly arrive at night and take Muskaan away early the next morning. Nilesh arrived at around 11:30 p.m. on the night of 23 October. The next day, he lied to me and took Muskaan with him. He said he was going to his maternal aunt's home in Ganesh Vihar Colony. I told him to go ahead. He had lied to us. We did not know where he had taken her. Nilesh called today and asked us to come to Rudra Hotel. There is no Rudra Hotel here. When we looked for it, we found out that it was Rishabh Hotel. When we checked their bill at Rishabh Hotel, we found that instead of taking Muskaan to his maternal aunt's home, he had taken her to the hotel. The hotel bill was for 23 to 24 October. Father-in-law said-Son-in-law told us to come to the nursing home Nilesh called me again. He told me to come to Kapoor Nursing Home. We reached Kapoor Nursing Home, but he was not there either. After that, Nilesh called us and said again that we should come to the medical college, so we went there. He then told us to come to the civil hospital. When we reached the civil hospital, we found Muskaan dead there. Nilesh is saying that Muskaan had fallen. But I suspect that he may have grabbed my Muskaan by the face and slammed her head against the wall. She suffered an injury to her head. Father-in-law says son-in-law had relationships with other women Ramjilal Simaulia said Nilesh had earlier worked in a private job. He had joined Madhya Pradesh Gramin Bank as a society manager just 15 days ago. His son-in-law had relationships with other women. He already had a wife who lives in Indore. We learnt about this after our daughter's marriage. He repeatedly told my daughter, "My first wife is better. You do not have what she has." SP City Preeti Singh said CCTV footage showed the husband and wife heading towards a room with a hotel staff member. Muskan can then be seen falling. The father's allegations are being investigated. A post-mortem has been conducted.

stories.title: Transgender people create ruckus outside Jhansi SSP’s office:Strip off clothes, block road, kick constable and slap passer-by
stories.summary: Transgender persons staged a major protest with their associates in front of the SSP's office in Jhansi. Angry over the lack of action in a case, they removed their clothes and stripped naked. They put up barricades, blocked the road and climbed onto vehicles. The transgender persons did not stop there and kicked a uniformed constable. He ran away to save his life. During the blockade, they slapped and kicked several passers-by. The police tried to reason with them, but they continued protesting. A large police force then arrived, detained the transgender persons and took them to the police station. The incident took place on Saturday evening. On Sunday, the police arrested four transgender persons and a woman. A case has been registered against all of them at Nawabad police station. According to the police, a dispute over the division of areas has been going on between two groups of transgender persons. The two groups fought on 21 October. Both groups went to Nawabad police station to lodge complaints. There, transgender person Abhishek alias Anshika drank phenyl to put pressure on the other side. On 24 October, Anshika staged a protest with associates. See two pictures... Now read the full matter in detail... Mamata Devi, who lives in Mahaveeran Colony in Premnagar, said, "I have two sons. My elder son, Abhishek Vanshkar (20), came into contact with a transgender person while he was studying. He began living with them and also dropped out of his studies. In January 2025, the transgender person arranged for Abhishek to undergo gender reassignment. His name was changed from Abhishek to Anshika." The dispute was over soliciting ‘badhai’ "I filed a complaint against this, but nothing happened. My son Abhishek was now asking the guru of the transgender group for an area in which to solicit 'badhai'. However, the guru was not allocating areas. This was the reason for the ongoing dispute. On 21 October, my son went to Kochhabhanwar with his transgender companions Naintara, Rasiyan and Pooja to solicit ‘badhai’. Another transgender faction led by Babli arrived there, and a fight broke out"," Mamata said. Other group accused of issuing threats Several complaints were lodged over this issue, but no action was taken. On Saturday afternoon, transgender person Anshika, also known as Abhishek, reached the SSP's office along with her mother Mamta, Pooja, Naintara, Rasiyan and others. She alleged that the police were not listening to her and that the other group was threatening to kill her. Dispute over division of areas SP City Preeti Singh said that Anshika had earlier worked with Babli Mausi, the head of the transgender community. She used to visit areas without informing Babli Mausi and demand more money. Following a complaint, Babli Mausi removed her from her group. Since then, tension has persisted between Babli Mausi and Anshika's transgender followers over the division of their areas. They have been counselled several times after complaints were received, but they are unwilling to listen. The two groups fought on 21 October. Both sides reached Nawabad police station to file complaints. There, they began accusing each other. Anshika, a transgender person, attempted to drink phenyl to pressure the police into registering a false case against Babli Mausi, also a transgender person. The police then took her to the district hospital in their vehicle and admitted her. Three people were arrested for disturbing the peace after creating a commotion. Staged a naked protest by climbing onto vehicles The City SP further said, "On Saturday evening, four transgender people and one associate blocked the police lines gate by putting up a barrier. They misbehaved with passers-by travelling through the area and staged a naked protest. When police personnel tried to stop them, they jostled with and misbehaved with the officers. They stood on the bonnets of some vehicles and staged a naked protest." The police repeatedly tried to stop them, but they continued to become aggressive. Following this, Anshika alias Abhishek Kinnar, Pooja Kinnar, Nayantara Kinnar, Russian Kinnar and Anshika's mother Mamta were arrested. Sub-Inspector Ramkaran registered a case against all of them at Nawabad police station.

stories.title: Unnao woman killed and dumped in Lucknow:Injuries to face, strangled; names of 4 youths found written on paper in bag
stories.summary: A 25-year-old woman from Unnao was killed and dumped beneath Kisan Path in Lucknow. She had injuries on her face and marks suggesting strangulation. A bag was found nearby, containing her Aadhaar card, PAN card and a piece of paper. The names of four young men were written on the paper. Police reached the spot at around 9.30 p.m. on Saturday after being informed that a body was lying there. She was identified from her Aadhaar card as Aashiya alias Tina, daughter of Qamaruddin, a resident of Safipur in Unnao. A murder case has been registered against unidentified people following a complaint by the woman's sister. The incident took place in Saidpur village in Dubagga. See 3 pictures... The names of four young men are written on the paper A sheet of paper was found in the bag recovered from the woman. The names of four young men are written on it. In addition, a four-digit number is also written on the paper. However, the police have not yet disclosed the four names. The number may be related to a vehicle. However, no state- or district-related number or shortcode is written before the number. Meanwhile, as news spread that a body had been found in the bushes, people gathered at the spot. DCP West Jitendra Srivastava also reached the scene. She had a love marriage seven years ago; her family arranged another marriage two years later Asia was the youngest of four sisters and two brothers. Her older sisters are Parveen, Nasreen and Shaheen, while her brothers are Naz Mohammad and Shan Mohammad. Neither of the two brothers has married yet. Asia's family members said that Asia, also known as Nargis and Tina, had been married twice. Seven years ago, she eloped and had a love marriage with an SC youth from the same village. She was living with him in Delhi. They also had a daughter, Urooj Fatima, who was four years old. Two years later, Asia returned home from Delhi. Her father, Qamaruddin, then married her to Nasir, also known as Auwa, the son of Kallu, who lived in Rupau Godwa village in Nawabganj. However, Asia stayed there only on the night of the marriage. She returned to her parental home the next day and never went back. Her husband Nasir came several times to take her back, but she refused to go. Qamaruddin then turned Asia out of the house. She left with her daughter, Urooj Fatima. She subsequently began living in a rented house in Safipur. Asia would sometimes also go to the home of her sister Nasreen, who lived in Nawabganj. Police suspect murder based on the way the body was dumped ACP Shakeel Ahmed said, “The woman was wearing a burqa. An Aadhaar card and a PAN card were found in her bag during the investigation. The woman was identified using them. The body appears to be 5-6 hours old. The way the body was dumped suggests that the woman was murdered. The cause of death will be revealed by the post-mortem report.”

stories.title: UP to observe a holiday on 26 October:Yogi announces closure for Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti
stories.summary: There will be a public holiday in Uttar Pradesh on Monday, 26 October, on the occasion of Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti. The Yogi government issued the government order at 3 p.m. on Sunday. The Yogi government issued an official order at 3 PM on Sunday. Government offices and schools will remain closed; however, banks will stay open. In 2017, the Yogi government had cancelled 15 public holidays commemorating the birth anniversaries of eminent personalities, which included the holiday for Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti. At the time, the government stated that schools and government offices would instead host events on these days to share information about these figures. Later, following demands from the Valmiki community and various organizations, the government reversed its decision and restored the public holiday for Valmiki Jayanti. Last year as well, a holiday was declared on Valmiki Jayanti. Government to celebrate Valmiki Jayanti across 75 districts; Yogi to visit Bithoor Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti will be celebrated across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on October 26. Illumination ceremonies (deepdan), Ramayana recitations, devotional singing (bhajan), and cultural programs will take place at temples and major sites associated with the Ramayana. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will visit Bithoor in Kanpur to attend the Ramayana recitation and prayers at the Valmiki Ashram. According to tradition, the epic Ramayana was composed at this ashram, and it is where Goddess Sita found shelter and gave birth to Lord Ram’s sons, Lav and Kush. The Chief Minister will also gift development projects worth over ₹411 crore to the residents of Bilhaur and Bithoor assembly constituencies.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan says Akhilesh should have met Azam first:"I would have offered Congress just 25 seats; Owaisi is an excellent leader"
stories.summary: Former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh arrived in Etawah on Sunday afternoon. He took a jibe at Akhilesh Yadav's meeting with Azam Khan, saying, "Akhilesh Yadav should have met Azam Khan earlier." On the Samajwadi Party-Congress seat-sharing arrangement, he said, "If the decision on seat sharing had been in my hands, I would not have given Congress more than 25 seats." He said that all political parties in Uttar Pradesh are busy preparing for the 2027 Assembly elections. The contest in the upcoming election will be interesting. Called Owaisi a leader, took aim at Farooq Abdullah Brĳ Bhushan said, "AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi is a good leader. Farooq Abdullah's love for Pakistan, meanwhile, comes to the fore from time to time." Describing Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK) as part of India, he said that POK belonged to India and would remain a part of India. Only Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government will merge POK with India. Pakistan does not have the strength to fight India. Congress always stages protests on holidays Brij Bhushan also reacted to the Congress's proposed rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on 1 November. He said, "It is the festival of Diwali. Will the sky fall if it is held two or four days later? These people stage protests on the day that is a holiday." Meritorious students honoured At 1 p.m. on Sunday, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh arrived at the Etawah Police Lines in a private helicopter. From there, he attended a Dussehra Milan organised by the Kshatriya Swabhiman Manch as the chief guest. At the event, he spoke about the history and current circumstances of the Kshatriya community. He also honoured meritorious students. He said, "The history of the Kshatriya community has been glorious" Brij Bhushan Singh mentioned Lord Ram, Lord Krishna, King Harishchandra, Maharana Pratap and Prithviraj Chauhan. He said that the history of the Kshatriya community has been glorious. Its roots are linked to Ayodhya. Anyone who writes the history of the Kshatriyas also becomes immortal. In the past, the community had swords and royal families, but circumstances changed over time. The community should prepare itself according to changing circumstances Brij Bhushan Singh referred to Mewar's historic heritage. He said that the tradition of self-respect had continued there even during the rule of the Mughals and the British. Mewar is still respected today. Referring to the international situation, he cited Israel, the United States and Iran as examples. He said that failing to adapt to changing times was one of society's major shortcomings. Society should prepare itself according to changing circumstances.

stories.title: Only son dies by suicide after shooting himself:Video captures him telling his father to keep the money; his mother had also died by setting herself on fire
stories.summary: A 19-year-old BA student died by suicide in Jhansi on Sunday. He shot himself with his father's licensed pistol. Neighbours reached the spot after hearing the gunshot. When they found the door locked, they called the student's father. At the time, the father and the student's stepmother had gone to the fields. They both returned home and took the student to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The student was his father's only child. His father is retired from the post of village development officer. He had married twice. The incident occurred at 10 a.m. Police found a video on the student's mobile phone that he had recorded before taking his own life. In the video, he said: "I have caused my father a lot of distress. I would continue to cause him distress as long as I lived. Now I am going to my mother. Keep your money with you. I am ending my life today." Read the full story... Father Munnalal married twice; Luv's mother had also died by suicide The incident took place in the Gursarai police station area. Munnalal Patel, a resident of Singar village, had retired as a Village Development Officer 10 years ago. He now farms in the village. Munnalal had married twice. His first wife, Hemlata, did not have any children, so he married Sangeeta Patel. They had a son, whom they named Luv Patel. In September 2009, Sangeeta died by setting herself on fire. Since then, Love had been living with his father. Munna Lal said that at around 8 a.m. on Sunday, he had gone to the fields with his wife, Hemlata. Their son, Luv, was alone at home. According to Munna Lal, the neighbours called at around 10 a.m. They told him that they had heard the sound of a gunshot coming from his house. Lav was lying on the floor, pistol found nearby Munna Lal said he rushed home. When he opened the door of the room, Luv was lying on the floor. A pistol was lying right next to him. He took Lav to the health centre in Gursarai, where doctors declared him dead. After receiving information about the incident, the police and forensic team reached the spot. The police questioned the family members, while the forensic team collected evidence from the scene. During the investigation, a video that Luv had recorded before the incident was found on his mobile phone. Luv's father told the police that his son often remained stressed. As a result, his health would also frequently be poor. He could not sleep at night, so he often took sleeping pills. What did Luv say in the video? In the video, Luv mentioned the hardships he had faced from his parents. Pointing towards his mother's photograph, he said that he was going to her. He also said that his friends, family or any relative was not to blame for the incident. CO Garotha Piyush Kumar Pandey said that the young man locked the room from inside and shot himself with his father's licensed pistol. His father has been questioned. The reason why the young man took this step is not yet clear. A video recorded before the incident was found on his mobile phone. The body has been sent for post-mortem examination.

stories.title: Cyclone Alert 2026: बंगाल की खाड़ी में उठ रहा तूफान, यूपी में मौसम का यू-टर्न; लखनऊ में बारिश को लेकर बड़ा अपडेट
stories.summary: Cyclone Alert: बंगाल की खाड़ी में बना कम दबाव का क्षेत्र अब गहरे दबाव और फिर चक्रवाती तूफान में बदलने की ओर बढ़ रहा है। भारत मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (आईएमडी) के 25 अक्टूबर 2026 को सुबह 8:30 बजे जारी बुलेटिन के अनुसार, यह मौसमी सिस्टम 28 अक्टूबर की सुबह तक बेहद गंभीर चक्रवाती तूफान का रूप ले सकता है। इसके आंध्र प्रदेश के तट के पास पहुंचने और 28 अक्टूबर की सुबह से पूर्वाह्न के बीच बापटला और विशाखापत्तनम के बीच तट पार करने की आशंका जताई गई है। इस दौरान समुद्र तटीय इलाकों में तेज हवाओं के साथ भारी से अत्यधिक भारी बारिश का खतरा रहेगा। वहीं, इस मौसमी गतिविधि के बीच उत्तर प्रदेश में भी मौसम बदलने के संकेत हैं। लखनऊ सहित पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश के जिलों में 28 अक्टूबर से गरज-चमक और तेज हवाओं की संभावना है, जबकि 29 अक्टूबर से बारिश की गतिविधियां बढ़ सकती हैं। हालांकि, लखनऊ में 28 अक्टूबर को भारी बारिश की आधिकारिक चेतावनी नहीं है।

stories.title: Bulldozer action on lawyers' chambers in Lucknow sparks protest:Lawyers sit on the ground as officials try to convince them; heavy police force deployed
stories.summary: Bulldozers will be used to remove illegal structures built by lawyers around the district court in Kaisarbagh, Lucknow. The Municipal Corporation has identified 211 illegal structures and marked them with red crosses. Officials have reached the site with bulldozers, along with the police and administration teams, to carry out the demolition drive. Before the action, officials had also reviewed 14 objections filed against the notices. The High Court has rejected the lawyers' appeal. Earlier, 72 illegal chambers were demolished in two phases between May and August. The latest drive was planned for October 11 but was postponed because the objections were still being addressed and the court case was pending. Lawyers protest, demand space for displaced chambers Lawyers staged a protest and demanded that space be provided for chambers that had been removed. About a year ago, the Municipal Corporation surveyed illegal chambers at the old High Court complex, the district sessions court, the registration office in Kaisarbagh, and roads in front of and behind the District Magistrate's office. The survey was conducted as part of a public interest case pending in the High Court. Around 241 chambers were identified at that time. So far, only 72 chambers have been demolished, and some have been rebuilt. During the demolition drive on August 30, questions were raised because the joint team of the Municipal Corporation and police had acted only against the 72 chambers involved in the court case. Officials say all illegal structures will be removed No action had been taken against other chambers built along the road from the Civil Court, past Balrampur Hospital, towards the Residency. Last month, the High Court took a strict stand and ordered the removal of the remaining illegal chambers. Municipal Corporation Zonal Officer Om Prakash Singh said all illegal structures built over drains, open drains, footpaths and roads outside the court complex would be removed in line with the High Court's order. Notices have already been issued to those concerned.

stories.title: Black magic ritual with PM Modi’s photo in Mau:Lemon, coconut and vermilion found with picture at Ghosi cremation ground; four detained
stories.summary: A picture of Prime Minister Narendra Modi was found alongside items used in occult rituals near the cremation site at Muktidham in Mau. On Saturday, police detained four people after filing an FIR against unidentified persons. Superintendent of Police Sarvesh Kumar Mishra said the investigation was being conducted with the help of CCTV footage and surveillance. On Friday, coconuts, lemons, red thread and vermilion were found alongside the Prime Minister's picture near the cremation site at Muktidham in the Duhri Ghat police station area. All the items found with the picture are used in witchcraft. Lemons pierced with needles had been placed over the picture, while coconuts tied with kalawa and vermilion had been placed at its four corners. After seeing the video and photographs, BJP district president Ramashray Maurya objected to the incident. In a complaint to the police, he demanded that the administration identify those involved and take strict action against them. FIR registered under the BNS and IT Act Police at Doharighat police station have registered a case against unidentified accused under Section 353(2) of the BNS and Section 67 of the IT Act. Police are examining CCTV footage from the scene and the surrounding area. They are also using surveillance to identify those connected with the photograph and video. Four suspects questioned; police looking into the motive SP Sarvesh Kumar Mishra said four suspects had been taken into custody during the investigation. They are being questioned. The police team has found some important clues, and the entire case will be solved soon.
