stories.title: Bulldozer action at SP event in Ghaziabad:Stage and tents demolished, organiser detained for 6 hours; bicycles were to be distributed to 1,000 girl students
stories.summary: Police and the municipal council stopped the Samajwadi Party's cycle distribution programme in Ghaziabad. The stage was demolished with a bulldozer and the tent was brought down late on Friday night. The equipment was loaded into vehicles and taken away. Before the action, police detained the organiser, SP leader Anuj Pradhan, for six hours. The matter concerns the Ankur Vihar police station area of Loni, around 22 kilometres from the district headquarters. Bicycles were scheduled to be distributed to 1,000 female students at the programme proposed for Sunday. Police are currently deployed at the venue, and no one is being allowed to enter. Meanwhile, Loni Municipal Council also imposed a fine of ₹10,86,930 on the organiser. Municipal officials said permission had not been obtained for the programme. SP leader Anuj Pradhan said, "The programme would have benefited the daughters, but a Ravana is sitting as a public representative on the soil of Loni. He called his masters and said, 'Go and take it away.' The police kept me detained for six hours." Here is the full story... A PDA felicitation ceremony and a programme to distribute bicycles to 1,000 poor female students had been scheduled for Sunday by Anuj Pradhan, a Samajwadi Party leader from Garhi Kattaia village in Loni. A large pandal and stage had been set up in the village for the event. According to his family, on Saturday, a day before the programme, the police had called organiser Anuj Pradhan to the Circle Officer's office in the Ankur Vihar area for a discussion. Anuj Pradhan reached the Circle Officer's office at around 6 p.m. According to Anuj, the police detained him for six hours. Meanwhile, a bulldozer was used to demolish the stage and tent set up at the programme venue. The belongings were then loaded into a vehicle and taken away. Permission had been obtained from the municipality for the programme Anuj Pradhan said he had duly obtained permission for the programme. However, his political opponents spread rumours that permission had not been granted to distribute bicycles. He claimed that he also showed the police the documents related to the permission, but the officials did not listen to him and stopped the programme. SP leader says decision to distribute bicycles was taken after seeing girls walking According to Anuj Pradhan, he saw some girls walking around three kilometres to another village to attend school. After this, he and his family decided to give bicycles to the students. After collecting documents from Loni's 55 municipal wards and gram panchayats, a bicycle distribution programme was scheduled for 25 October. Bicycles were gathered at the farmhouse for the event, and a pandal was also set up. He further said that he would give bicycles to women and girls at any cost. Even if he had to lose his life for it, he would not change his decision. He was willing to go to jail, but he would not be afraid. CO says: It is a municipal council matter; let them deal with it DCP Rural Surendranath Tiwari said- "This is a matter related to the municipal council. Only the municipal council can provide information on whether the programme had permission. The municipal council halted the programme. The police neither halted the programme nor detained any organiser."

stories.title: ₹50 lakh Fortuner stolen from BJP leader:Thief arrives limping, opens gate and drives away in 50 seconds
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, a young man fled with a BJP leader's Fortuner worth ₹50 lakh. Pretending to limp, he approached the car, lay down near the gate for three seconds, then opened the car door, got inside and drove away in just 50 seconds. CCTV footage of the theft has also emerged. It shows the thief wearing a turban and carrying a bag. The car owner has lodged a police complaint and also expressed suspicion of his driver, while the thief seen in the CCTV footage has not been identified. The incident took place at 10:30 pm on Thursday in the Cantonment police station area. The BJP leader lodged the complaint at 1:46 am on Saturday. Police are investigating the case based on the complaint. See 3 pictures... Car parked near hotel Businessman Piyush Jaiswal is the district vice-president of the BJP's OBC Morcha. Piyush Jaiswal said he parked his Fortuner near Hotel Royal Stay Inn in the Rajapur area at around 10:30 pm on 22 October. When he arrived to collect the car at around 11 am on 23 October, it was missing. The car could not be traced even after searching the surrounding area and questioning people. He then lodged a complaint with the police. CCTV footage from the area was checked, which showed a young man driving the car away. He is seen carrying a bag and wearing a turban. Pretending to limp on one leg, he approaches the car. He then unlocks it, gets inside and drives away within a few seconds. New driver under suspicion Piyush Jaiswal said that a few days ago, he had hired a new driver named Maya Shankar. He drove the vehicle for 10-12 days. He then said he was going to Mumbai and brought another driver with him. He said that he was leaving for Mumbai. He said that during this period, the driver had also taken the vehicle out several times without informing him. On one occasion, he took the vehicle's key with him. This has led to the suspicion that he may have had a duplicate key made. In the CCTV footage, the suspect walks straight up to the car. He opens it as though using a remote key to unlock it and drives away. On this basis, the owner suspects that the driver may have been involved in the theft. However, his role has not yet been confirmed. Following a complaint by Piyush Jaiswal, an FIR was registered at Civil Lines police station at 1:46 a.m. on the night of 24 October. Police are investigating the case and searching for the stolen car.

stories.title: 30-year-old cop dies in Muzaffarnagar:Truck rams car on highway; he remained trapped and in agony; driver flees
stories.summary: A 30-year-old police sub-inspector was killed in a road accident in Muzaffarnagar. He was returning to the police station by car at around 11 p.m. late on Saturday night. A truck coming from the opposite direction collided with his car on the highway. The collision was so severe that the front of the Swift Dzire was badly crushed. Sub-Inspector Arun Chahar became trapped inside. Taking advantage of the darkness, the truck driver fled the scene with the truck. The truck driver neither informed the police nor pulled the sub-inspector out. Trapped inside for a long time, the sub-inspector remained in agony. Later, some passers-by happened to pass by and informed the police. The police reached the scene shortly afterwards. The sub-inspector was taken to a nearby Community Health Centre (CHC), where he died during treatment. Sub-Inspector Arun Chahar was in charge of the Stadium Police Post in the Civil Lines area of Muzaffarnagar. He had gone to Jansath for official work. The accident occurred near Chittaura on the Panipat-Khatima Highway while he was returning from there at night. Police checking CCTV footage Sub-Inspector Arun Chahar was originally from Agra. His police outpost was just 20 km from the site of the accident on the highway. Police said they were trying to identify the truck that caused the collision. CCTV footage from the surrounding area was being checked to trace the truck driver. Special team formed to investigate the accident After the Sub-Inspector's death, the SP formed a special team to investigate the accident. The forensic team has also examined the car. Investigators are also trying to determine what official work had taken the Sub-Inspector to Jansath. The body has been sent for post-mortem.

stories.title: Model Shraddha asks for sugar-free black coffee in jail:Both sisters restless in barrack, kept pacing around; social media accounts still active
stories.summary: Model Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and driver Tanveer, accused in the Shiva Sharma murder case in Lucknow, are in jail. On their second day in jail, the two sisters appeared restless. They kept talking to each other for a long time but did not speak to any other inmate. According to sources, Shraddha demanded sugar-free black coffee in jail. Citing continuous travel and fatigue, she requested coffee instead of tea. However, the jail administration made it clear that she would receive things only in accordance with the jail manual. Despite being in jail, Shraddha's social media profile remains active. Her Instagram followers are increasing, while the number of accounts she follows is declining. This has raised questions about where her account is being operated from and who is operating it. On 9 October, businessman Shiva Sharma died after falling from Shraddha's flat in Lucknow. Shiva's mother filed an FIR alleging murder against Shraddha. See three pictures of Shraddha... Both sisters kept pacing restlessly around the jail... Shraddha and Rashmi did not speak to anyone for 24 hours after reaching the jail. However, they kept asking the deputy jailer assigned to monitor them one thing or another. The two sisters have been lodged in a barrack housing 40-45 female prisoners. They are deeply distressed after suddenly losing their luxurious lifestyle. They keep pacing around the barrack. After they were shifted to the jail barrack, prisoners lodged in other barracks kept coming throughout the day to see Shraddha Dubey. According to sources, the people deployed there were also watching Shraddha Dubey. Several prisoners inside the jail tried to speak to the two women about the Shiva Sharma murder case, but they remained completely silent. They did not speak to anyone. Shraddha's followers increase, following decreases Model said: They slept until late evening; the incident occurred at night When businessman Shiva's body was found, there was lipstick on his face and stomach. Asked about this, Shraddha said he was her boyfriend, which was why there was lipstick on his face. On the morning of the incident, at around 7 a.m., Shraddha Dubey, Shiv Sharma and others reached Awadh Green Apartment. They then slept until late evening, after which the incident occurred at night. Shiva and Shraddha had argued before the incident During the police investigation, the maid said that Shiva Sharma and Shraddha Dubey had argued on the day of the incident. The entire incident took place afterwards. The police have now recorded the statement of Shraddha Dubey's maid. Statements have also been recorded from the neighbours who helped take Shiva Sharma to hospital after he fell. In addition to their statements, the police have recorded statements from other people who knew the two closely. Now read the full story... Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Hazratganj on 9 October. Shiva had been living with Shraddha for the past four months. After the incident, he was wearing only underwear. Lipstick had been applied to his face. Several cigarette burn marks were also found on his body. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, has filed a murder case in connection with his death against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver Adil. It is alleged that Shraddha pushed Shiva from the fourth floor. Police have arrested three of the accused.

stories.title: Flight operations suspended for 4 hours at Varanasi airport today:Notice to air missions issued; take-offs and landings to be restricted after 11 am
stories.summary: The NOTAM (Notice to Air Mission) issued from 21 October for the air show in Varanasi ends today. No flight will take off or land at Varanasi Airport for four hours, and the airport's runway will remain completely closed. The NOTAM was issued from 21 to 25 October to ensure security and smooth air traffic in view of the grand and historic air show being held at Varanasi's Namo Ghat. Today is its final day. Restrictions to take effect from 11 a.m. Airport director Puneet Gupta said that the NOTAM had been in effect at Varanasi Airport since 21 October. On its final day today, Sunday, no passenger, private or any other aircraft will be allowed to land at or take off from Varanasi Airport between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. Only Air Force aircraft will remain in the flying zone and will take off and land on the instructions of the ATC tower set up by the Army. Fluctuations in flight operations during the air show The airport director said that after intensive aircraft rehearsals on 21 October, regular flights could not operate the following day, 22 October, because of technical reasons and scheduling constraints. The air show was halted for a day on Friday because of the local MLC elections. As the show was not held, regular flights operated as usual between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. on Friday, providing major relief to passengers. However, the air show was in full swing on Saturday, and not a single regular commercial aircraft took off from Babatpur Airport as fighter jets and other aircraft performed in the sky. Dozens of Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa flights affected This four-hour daily air restriction (no-fly zone) has had a direct and widespread impact on passengers travelling to and from Varanasi, as well as on airlines. Several major domestic and international flights operating in the afternoon had to be rescheduled. • Impact on Air India Express: On Saturday, the timings of the airline's domestic flights to Mumbai, Bengaluru and Delhi, as well as its international flight to Sharjah, were significantly changed because of the air show. • IndiGo flights revised: IndiGo Airlines also had to alter its busy schedule. As part of this, the timings of flights to Hyderabad, Bengaluru, the national capital Delhi and Pune were revised and shifted forward or backward. • Akasa Air services affected: Akasa Air's daily flight from Varanasi to Bengaluru, known as the Silicon Valley, was also affected by the restriction and has been rescheduled. Important guidelines from the airport administration for air passengers Puneet Gupta said that, for the convenience of air passengers and to prevent any possible chaos at the airport, the airport administration and all airlines had issued a joint special advisory. Passengers have been strictly instructed to contact their respective airline's customer care, official website or toll-free number and check the revised and confirmed timing of their flight before leaving home for Varanasi (Babatpur) Airport. They have been advised to confirm the timing in advance so that they do not have to wait at the airport for a long time due to the change in schedule.

stories.title: Businessman Shiva’s death- was he pushed or did he jump?:What digital and forensic evidence does police have against Shraddha Dubey, and will ‘Sirji’ save her?
stories.summary: The death of Lucknow hotelier Shiva Sharma is making headlines across the country. Treating it as a murder case, the police have sent his girlfriend, Shraddha Dubey, to jail. Before filing the chargesheet, police are gathering digital and forensic evidence. However, several individuals and stories linked to Shiva's death still remain behind the scenes. What happened on the evening of 9 October in Shraddha Dubey's flat that led to Shiva falling off the terrace? Was Shiva upset with Shraddha? Did a fight break out between them, leading Shraddha to push Shiva off the terrace in anger? Or was Shiva so deeply distressed after the altercation that he chose the path of death? In either scenario, Shraddha could face punishment, provided the charges are proven in court—whether it is proven as murder or abetment to suicide. Shraddha Dubey's case is also considered high-profile because she reportedly has deep connections within Lucknow's bureaucracy. Police claim that statements from people connected to Shraddha and Shiva are being recorded to strengthen the case. However, it is also believed that Shraddha Dubey's ‘Sirji’ is attempting to shield her. In today's Sunday Big Story, let us understand how strong the evidence is against Shraddha. What are the circumstances under which Shraddha could defend herself? And how significant has been the role of 'Sirji' in this entire affair? According to Dr. K.K. Singh of KGMU's Post-Mortem Department, Shiva had been taken to another hospital before being brought there. He was alive at that time, as he had a venflon and catheter fitted in his arm for a drip. However, by the time he was brought to KGMU, he had already passed away. As soon as the ward boy informed them of his death, Shraddha and the people with her left the premises. Investigations so far reveal that after leaving the hospital, Shraddha returned to her flat. After grabbing clothes and money from there, she left Lucknow along with driver Tanveer and her sister Rashmi. On the morning of 10 October, the three reached Rupaidiha in Bahraich district. They parked their black Scorpio in a parking lot and entered Nepal. For the next six days, they stayed in various parts of Nepal. On 13 October, Shraddha released three videos within 12 hours claiming innocence. She also appealed that her name should not be linked to any official, stating she had no connection with anyone. In the videos, Shraddha claimed that Shiva's mother, Ranjana, arrived at the hospital and started a quarrel, which is why she left. However, according to doctors at KGMU, Shraddha had left about an hour before Ranjana reached the hospital. After spending 6 days in Nepal, Shraddha returned to Lucknow on 16 October. She gave an interview to a news agency in which she maintained her innocence. However, she went missing once again before her arrest. Audio evidence and CDR-Location key evidence against Shraddha Shiva's mother has filed an FIR for murder against Shraddha. According to Shraddha, Shiva took his own life by jumping. Between these two facts, let's look at how strong the evidence and witnesses are that the police possess to prove Shraddha guilty in court: CCTV and Crime Scene Evidence: There were no CCTV cameras inside the flat. However, the police have secured DVRs from CCTV cameras installed within the campus and in other houses in the neighborhood. Movements of suspicious individuals have surfaced in these recordings. Shraddha's Call Recordings, Talk of Teaching a Lesson: Following Shiva's death, three call recordings between him and Shraddha have surfaced. In one recording, Shraddha is arguing with him over the delay in bringing cigarettes. In the second recording, she is using abusive language, threatening to beat him like a dog. In the third recording as well, Shraddha is threatening Shiva, saying she will beat him in a way that people will remember. These three recordings indicate that Shraddha was continuously threatening Shiva. Chats and Bank Transactions also crucial: What kind of relationship existed between Shraddha and Shiva is the most critical aspect in this case. The police will examine how their relationship was from the beginning to the end. For this, the chats between the two will be reviewed, and financial transactions between them will be scrutinized. Even if the investigation points toward Shiva committing suicide, the underlying reason will still be sought, with Shraddha remaining the central focus. How did a situation arise where Shiva, sitting right next to Shraddha, jumped from the apartment and ended his life? Statements of Witnesses and Former Driver: Statements of 7 people, including eyewitnesses—residents of neighboring flats, the domestic help, the driver, and a former driver—have been recorded. The domestic help stated in her statement that a fight was taking place between Shiva and Shraddha on 9 October. Shraddha was repeatedly threatening Shiva by citing her connections. The police also reached Shraddha's father in Raebareli and questioned him for 2 hours. Recovered Mobiles and Electronic Gadgets: While bringing Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi, and driver Tanveer to Lucknow on transit remand from Nagpur, the police seized their mobile phones and other electronic items. These have been sent for forensic examination. Additionally, efforts are underway to locate the two mobile phones that Shraddha had thrown away in Nepal. Call Detail Records and Location: Shraddha was continuously on the run after the incident. The STF traced her to Nagpur and arrested her using her location data, internet calls, and WhatsApp data. Face-to-Face Interrogation of Shraddha, Her Sister, and the Driver: Injuries Prior to Death: The post-mortem report mentions 10 severe injuries on Shiva's body that occurred before his death. After falling from the flat, he sustained injuries to his head, face, and body. Fractures were found in his ribs. Deep internal fractures occurred in his bones due to the fall from height. Based on claims by his mother, Ranjana Sharma, and forensic observations, there is mention of marks indicating assault and alleged cigarette burns on the body, reinforcing the suspicion of physical torture and a scuffle prior to death. The cause of death has been stated as excessive internal and external bleeding leading to profound shock. Only Underwear on the Body, Lipstick on the Face: At the time of Shiva's death, he was wearing only underwear. Initial examination of the body revealed lipstick marks on his face, further heightening suspicions of murder or foul play. Delay in Medical Treatment—This Will Be the Police's Stand: The post-mortem and medical history also revealed that after the incident, instead of immediately taking Shiva to a hospital, there was a delay of approximately 2 to 3 hours as he was moved around from one place to another. 'Sarji' Helpful, Shraddha Left for Nepal After Lucknow Interview In one of Shraddha's recordings, she was heard threatening Shiva while invoking the name of 'Sarji'. It is reported that Shraddha is confident this 'Sarji' will save her. 'Sarji' is said to be a senior bureaucracy official, and his influence was also visible during Shraddha's interrogation. Police officers did not question her about the audio recording. Apart from that, most of the interrogation revolved around her period as a fugitive. It is also reported that while Shraddha was being brought back from Nagpur, she was offered black coffee and paneer tikka along the way. Even when Shraddha reached Hazratganj, there was no sign of distress on her face. During questioning, in response to several questions, she stated that her lawyers would answer them. How many challenges face the police in building a case against Shraddha? Senior Advocate of Lucknow High Court, Mukesh Sharma, answered questions from Dainik Bhaskar regarding the investigation against Shraddha. Question: Why did the police not seek Shraddha's remand? Mukesh Sharma: The police likely do not have strong evidence in this case at present, which is why they did not request remand in court. They are currently gathering evidence through investigation; after this, they may seek Shraddha's remand to question her on matters arising from that evidence. Question: How strong must the evidence be to secure a remand? Mukesh Sharma: There is currently no eyewitness in this case. Everything relies on Shraddha's statement and chats, but securing a conviction based solely on these will not be easy. The police will have to conduct a very deep investigation into this matter. If an eyewitness is found, it could lead toward Shraddha's conviction. Question: Can Shraddha get bail quickly? Mukesh Sharma: Over the next 10 days, what evidence the police manage to gather will determine whether bail will be granted or denied. In this matter, Shraddha Dubey and driver Danish might get bail quickly, as their role has not significantly surfaced in the investigation so far. Legal Protection Is a Right, But If Provided Early, Questions Will Be Raised We spoke to Senior Advocate AP Singh of the Supreme Court regarding this matter. He states that every accused person must receive legal protection; however, if this protection is provided even before the trial or case proceedings formally begin, it is improper. Who helped Shraddha in Nepal, who assisted her in Lucknow, and how the accommodation in Nagpur was arranged—these remain key questions. AP Singh added, "In this case, apart from the CDR and CCTV footage, the accused should undergo polygraph tests, brain mapping, and lie detector tests. As for bail, it makes no sense at this stage, which is why the court rejected it."

stories.title: Village-like chaos in elections contest of the ‘educated’:Clashes and assaults in 25 cities; why are MLC polls being called the semi-final for 2027?
stories.summary: The MLC elections, which have traditionally concluded peacefully, were unusually tumultuous this time. On polling day, incidents of clashes and violence were reported in around 25 cities, including Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Agra, Bareilly and Muzaffarnagar. This is the first time such incidents have occurred in the history of MLC elections. Why has politics played such a dominant role in an election involving educated sections of society, such as teachers and graduates? We will explore the reasons in today's UP Explainer. Question 1: Why did clashes break out in this year's teachers' and graduates' elections? How did politics come to dominate the contest? Answer: Several reasons can be identified. - In the past, these elections were fought mainly around non-political teachers' organisations, such as the Sharma, Chandel and Thakurai factions, and local independent intellectuals. Their issues were largely limited to teachers' salaries, the old pension scheme and arrears. Over time, however, political parties also began taking an interest in these elections. - Although these elections are not contested directly on party symbols, political parties field their official candidates. This time, ahead of the Assembly elections, the BJP and the Samajwadi Party (SP) turned the contest into a prestige battle. - Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took charge of the election campaign and held meetings across the state. In Lucknow, he addressed a teachers' and graduates' voters' conference for teachers' candidate Umesh Dwivedi and graduates' candidate Avnish Singh. Similarly, he held special meetings and gatherings in Ghaziabad, Gorakhpur, Bareilly, Varanasi, Ballia and Agra to boost workers' morale. The BJP's entire cadre was seen alongside him. - The contest became a prestige battle in Gorakhpur and Varanasi. In Muzaffarnagar, the presence of a state minister and office-bearers of both parties at polling booths increased aggression among grassroots workers. Sharp allegations and counter-allegations further heightened tensions, eventually leading to clashes and commotion. - The MLC elections have given the SP and BJP an opportunity to assess how prepared their grassroots organisations and booth-management machinery are for 2027. This is why both parties threw their full weight behind the contest, treating it as a semi-final ahead of the Assembly elections. As a result, elections that are usually peaceful also became violent and highly politicised. Question 2: Why did the Gorakhpur and Varanasi seats become a matter of prestige for the BJP? Answer: The most obvious reason is that these seats are in the regions associated with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, respectively. Any lapse here could raise questions directly about the party's top leadership. There are several other reasons as well. - In the 2020 elections, the SP won both the teachers' and graduates' seats in Varanasi. Losing seats in PM Modi's parliamentary constituency was a major embarrassment for the BJP. Later, during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Congress's Ajay Rai remained ahead of PM Modi for several rounds. This created the impression that not only the BJP but also PM Modi's popularity was declining. However, the BJP is determined not to repeat any mistakes this time. - The contest for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad seat has become particularly interesting and personal. After being denied a BJP ticket, Dr Sanjayan Tripathi rebelled. Sensing an opportunity, Akhilesh Yadav dropped the SP's announced candidate, Kamlesh Yadav, and fielded Sanjayan instead. - Another BJP leader, Ajay Singh, also entered the fray as an independent after being denied a ticket. The situation became even more complicated when BJP MLC Devendra Pratap Singh, elected from the graduates' constituency in the same region, opened a front against the party's own candidate, Dhruv Tripathi. He was reportedly upset after not being given a seat on the stage at a party event. - On October 19, Devendra wrote an open letter on social media, urging voters to vote against what he called an insult. Then, on October 22, just a day before polling, he released a video alleging that teachers were being threatened to secure votes in the MLC elections. - As a result, the Gorakhpur-Faizabad teachers' constituency became a contest between rebellion within the party and the party cadre. Aggressive campaigning by rebel or opposition candidates in the Chief Minister's home region pushed the BJP to adopt an equally aggressive approach to avoid being put on the back foot. - SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had focused on these two major centres in eastern Uttar Pradesh as part of a specific strategy. The SP believes that if it can give the BJP a tough fight or defeat it in the political strongholds of Yogi Adityanath and PM Modi, it will deal a major psychological blow to the BJP's confidence ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. - In short, Gorakhpur and Varanasi are not merely seats. They represent Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's 'fortress' and PM Modi's 'Kashi model'. Any setback in these constituencies could damage the BJP's credibility. This has turned the election into a do-or-die battle for both parties. Question 3: Why are the MLC elections being seen as a semi-final for 2027? Answer: Three major reasons stand out. I) They will reveal the preferences of educated voters: Teachers and graduates are considered among the most aware sections of society and are often opinion-makers who shape public sentiment. They directly assess government policies and administrative functioning. The voting pattern of this section, just before the 2027 Assembly elections, will indicate which political direction people in this segment of the state are leaning towards. II) An aggressive face-off between the SP and BJP: This is the first contest in which the BJP and SP have faced each other directly since the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Chief Minister Yogi himself took charge of the BJP's campaign, while the SP deployed its cadre aggressively at polling booths. By turning the contest into a matter of prestige, both parties activated their election machinery for 2027. III) A test of grassroots and booth-level organisation: MLC constituencies cover vast areas, with a single seat often spanning several districts. Registering voters across such a large area, bringing them to polling booths and maintaining a strong presence at every booth is a real test of the organisational strength of both parties' cadres. However, it is important to remember that a large section of the population, including rural voters, farmers, labourers, young people without graduate degrees and women, does not participate in these elections. A candidate's personal image, caste and reach among teachers and graduates also play a major role, beyond party affiliation. Therefore, the outcome of the MLC elections does not necessarily translate directly into the results of the 2027 Assembly elections. Even so, the results due on October 27 will certainly offer some indications about the direction of Uttar Pradesh politics. If the BJP wins - The BJP will present its victory as an endorsement by educated voters of the policies, development work and law-and-order record of its double-engine government. This would send the morale of party workers soaring. - If the BJP manages to retain the trust of educated voters despite being in power for two consecutive terms, it will signal that the Opposition's narrative around the CJP movement, vote theft and paper leaks has failed to gain traction. If the SP wins - The SP will highlight the result as a sign of discontent among unemployed young graduates and the working population. It will project the outcome as evidence that Uttar Pradesh's educated voters want change. - Overall, although the MLC election results will not directly change the government, they could indicate the political direction and prevailing mood ahead of 2027. They will also give both parties an opportunity to finalise their election strategies.

stories.title: UP PET exam:Girls made to remove earrings, anklets, and chains; hair buns checked, cop takes student to correct centre on bike
stories.summary: The first day of the Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET-2026) is underway in Uttar Pradesh. The examination is being held at 1,372 centres across 60 districts. Candidates were allowed entry only after verification of their admit cards and Aadhaar cards, biometric matching and face-retina scans. In Kannauj, a student who reached the wrong examination centre broke down in tears. A police officer on duty took her to the correct centre on his motorcycle. In Lucknow, girls’ kalawa threads were cut, while earrings and hairpins were removed. Boys were asked to take off their shoes and socks. In Kanpur and Bareilly, girls were asked to open their hair for checking. In Aligarh, women removed their anklets and necklaces and handed them to family members before entering the centres. In Mathura, boys cut their kalawa threads with their teeth and were asked to remove their belts. In Aligarh, candidates were also asked to leave their handkerchiefs outside. Examination centres are being monitored through CCTV cameras. Police personnel in plain clothes are patrolling outside the centres. The examination is being conducted in two shifts. The first shift runs from 10 am to noon, while the second will be held from 3 pm to 5 pm. Entry for the second shift will begin at 1 pm, and the gates will close at 2.30 pm. One-fourth mark will be deducted for each wrong answer The examination will be conducted offline using OMR sheets. It will consist of 100 multiple-choice questions, each carrying one mark. A deduction of one-fourth of a mark will be made for every incorrect answer. The question paper will include five questions each on history, geography, economics, the Constitution, general science, mathematics, Hindi, English and reasoning. There will be 10 questions each on current affairs, general knowledge, Hindi comprehension, and graph and table analysis. Biology and Chemistry will not have separate sections; science questions will be covered under general science. Exam centres allotted 500–600 km away Siddharth Singh from Jaunpur has to travel 520 km to Mainpuri to appear for the Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET). He said he would have to leave home a day before the examination. Mohammed Rahman from Prayagraj faces an even longer journey, as his centre has been allotted in Ghaziabad, 650 km away. These are not just the stories of two candidates but reflect the difficulties faced by thousands of young people appearing for the PET. They are worried about whether to focus on exam preparation or the extra time required for travel, as centres have been allotted 500–600 km away. Commission chairman says centres were allotted by computer Commission chairman Satya Narayan Sabat said Uttar Pradesh is a large state, with a distance of around 1,100 km between its two ends. He said the most suitable arrangement had been made in view of the centres available for 3.5 million candidates. Candidate numbers are high in eastern districts such as Varanasi, Azamgarh, Ballia and Jaunpur, while the number of examination centres there is limited. In comparison, western Uttar Pradesh has fewer candidates and more centres. Therefore, examination centre allocations were adjusted according to requirements. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to commission chairman Satya Narayan Sabat, who said the commission takes steps to prevent cheating. Examination centres are now allotted through an automated system, which is why some candidates have been assigned centres farther away this time. Understand in three points: Who was allotted a centre where, and why Candidates with disabilities: Under the government policy, they have been given examination centres in their home districts as a concession. Female candidates: Keeping their safety in mind, they have been allotted centres outside their home districts but in another city within their division. Male candidates: They have been allotted examination centres in other divisions. Passing PET is mandatory for recruitment to Group B and C posts Passing this Preliminary Eligibility Test is mandatory for government jobs under the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC). Only after clearing it can candidates apply for recruitment to Group B and Group C posts. Since the admit cards were released, candidates have been demanding a change of examination centres on social media. They argue that the PET is only an initial screening test for Group B and Group C government jobs, such as lekhpal, junior assistant and village development officer (VDO). It is not a final recruitment examination, so they say there is no reason to send candidates such long distances for it. Five times Sikkim's population in PET candidates The examination will be held over three days, with two shifts each day. The commission has set up a total of 1,372 centres across 60 districts in the state. A record 3,541,296 candidates have applied this year. An average of around 600,000 candidates will appear in each shift, with nearly 1.2 million taking the exam each day. The total number of PET candidates is around five to six times Sikkim's population, which is approximately 700,000.

stories.title: Bomb attack on Dussehra night in Lucknow caught on CCTV:Five bombs hurled at youths as attackers warn, ‘This is just a trailer; you’ll see a bigger blast next’
stories.summary: A bombing incident was reported in Lucknow's Aliganj area on the night of Dussehra. Some local strongmen threw crude bombs and hand grenades one after another at a young man and his friends in the middle of the market. The victim and his companions were injured in the sudden attack. After the incident, the accused also called the victim and threatened to kill him, saying that this was only a trailer and that he would see a bigger blast next. Attack took place at a general store 50 metres from the house Aman Gupta, a resident of Sector Q ED/222 in Aliganj under the Madiyaon police station area, told police in his complaint that his friend Shiv Om Pal had come to his house to meet him on the night of Dussehra, 20 October. Between around 12 and 1 a.m., they were standing with their friends near Lalla General Store, just 50 metres from their home. Meanwhile, youths lying in wait there suddenly attacked them. Friends also suffered injuries Victim Aman Gupta alleged that the attackers targeted him and his friends, hurling five crude bombs at them in quick succession. The blasts one after another triggered panic in the area. Aman suffered serious injuries to several parts of his body in the bombing, while his friends also sustained injuries. Attackers made threatening phone calls The attackers were so emboldened that after carrying out the attack, they also called Aman on his mobile number and threatened to kill him. The accused threatened him over the phone, saying, "This is just the trailer; after this, you will see a major blast." Victim Aman Gupta also has a video of the entire incident, which he has handed over as evidence to the officer in charge of the local police outpost. Demand for strict action against the accused The victim submitted a written complaint to the Madiyaon police, seeking strict legal action and the registration of a case against the accused. Meanwhile, Madiyaon police said they had taken cognisance of the matter and were conducting a thorough investigation.

stories.title: High Court makes Meerut SSP stand for 45 minutes:Accused not produced in person; SSP admits his officers made a mistake
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court kept Meerut SSP BBGTS Murthy standing in court for 45 minutes on Saturday. The case concerns an accused who obtained bail after promising to marry and later went back on the promise. The court had cancelled the accused's bail and ordered the SSP to send him to judicial custody. However, the SSP's junior police officers did not produce the accused before the High Court and instead presented him before the CJM's court. The CJM also sent the accused to jail. Explaining himself before the High Court, the SSP said, "I was on leave. My juniors made a mistake." Thereafter, the bench of Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal also expressed serious displeasure over the conduct of Meerut's Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM). The court termed it gross negligence and indiscipline and directed that a copy of the order be placed before Meerut's administrative judge so that appropriate administrative action against him could be considered. Read the full case now Last year, Nitish alias Siddhant alias Sethi raped a girl in the Sardhana police station area of Meerut after promising to marry her. In the High Court, he promised to marry the victim and sought bail. On 18 March, the High Court granted Sethi bail. As soon as he was granted bail, Sethi broke his promise. The victim approached the High Court, seeking cancellation of the accused's bail on the grounds that he had violated his undertaking. During the hearing on Saturday, both the victim and the accused were present in court. When the court questioned the accused, he flatly refused to marry the victim. Order issued to take Meerut SSP into custody The High Court said that the accused had directly violated the undertaking given while obtaining bail. The court immediately cancelled his bail. It directed the Meerut SSP, who was present at the spot, to take the accused into custody immediately and produce him before the concerned magistrate for judicial custody. Police produced the accused before the CJM Meerut Earlier, after the accused failed to appear in the case, the High Court issued a non-bailable warrant against him on 28 September and clearly directed the SSP Meerut to execute it and produce the accused directly before the High Court. After the warrant was issued, instead of bringing the accused to the High Court, the police produced him before the CJM Meerut's court, which sent him to jail. SSP admitted his mistake The court had then asked the SSP Meerut to appear in person and provide an explanation. The SSP, who appeared on Saturday, said he had been on leave from 28 September to 2 October and that the lapse had occurred on the part of his subordinates. Warned to remain vigilant in future The court considered it negligence, but said that the SSP himself was the authority responsible for executing the warrant. Therefore, it was his responsibility to produce the accused before the High Court. Instead of passing any adverse order against him, the court directed him to remain present in the courtroom until 4 p.m. He was warned to remain vigilant in future. High Court calls Meerut CJM's conduct gross negligence The court also expressed serious displeasure that, despite the Meerut CJM being aware that the High Court had issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) directing that the accused be produced before it, he sent the accused directly to jail in judicial custody instead of directing that he be taken to the High Court. The High Court termed this gross negligence and indiscipline on the part of the Meerut CJM. It directed that a copy of the order be placed before Meerut's administrative judge so that appropriate administrative action could be taken against the CJM. Now, learn about IPS Murti Before being posted in Meerut, IPS officer Murti was the Senior Superintendent of Police in Jhansi. He was sent to Jhansi in April 2025. He has previously served as SP in Kasganj and Kanpur Dehat. Murti was selected as an IPS officer in the Uttar Pradesh cadre through direct recruitment via the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Civil Services Examination in 2015. He has been in the Indian Police Service for the past 11 years. His first posting was in Ghaziabad in 2015. He has also served as SP in the Intelligence Department in Lucknow. BTech in Computer Science and an MBA in Marketing BBGTS, who was born on 12 February 1985 in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, is 41 years old. He received his entire education in Hyderabad. He holds a BTech in Computer Science and an MBA in Marketing. He has received several awards during his police service. He was honoured with the DG Commendation Disc Silver in 2022, the DG Commendation Disc Gold in 2023 and the DG Commendation Disc Platinum in 2025.

stories.title: Women beat up police officers and tear uniforms in UP:Mob frees history-sheeter as sub-inspector and constables flee for their lives
stories.summary: Family members of a history-sheeter attacked police who had arrived in Muzaffarnagar to arrest him. Women surrounded the sub-inspector and constable, grabbed their collars, pushed and jostled them, and abused them. They tore the police personnel's uniforms and ripped off their nameplates. The history-sheeter's family members freed him from police custody and helped him escape. As the police personnel ran after the accused, his family members began beating the sub-inspector and constable. The police personnel somehow fled the spot and saved their lives. Sub-inspector Rupesh Kumar and constable Kuldeep were injured in the attack. Police took both of them to hospital. Forces have been deployed in the village, and a search is under way for the absconding history-sheeter and his family members. The incident took place in the Sikheda area. History-sheeter tried to flee as soon as he was taken into custody At 7 p.m. on Saturday, Sub-Inspector Rupesh Kumar and constables Kuldeep and Rajveer reached Sikhera village. A warrant had been issued by the Court of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate against Sahil alias Bhuriya of the village. According to Sub-Inspector Rupesh Kumar, the policemen reached the house and took the accused, Sahil, into custody. Sahil then tried to flee. The women and men in the house got into a confrontation with the policemen and surrounded them. Sahil's mother Ayesha, wife Jaane Jahan, sisters Sana, Saniya, Saifi and Shoha, and brother Zaid abused the policemen and, along with others, attacked them. Constable's collar grabbed, uniform torn and he was assaulted Sub-inspector Rupesh Kumar said that the accused's family members grabbed the constable's collar. They assaulted him with kicks and punches and freed Sahil from the police officers' custody. When the police personnel tried to chase Sahil, the accused caught them again. They assaulted them a second time, tore their uniforms and even ripped off their nameplates. The police team somehow escaped from the spot and saved their lives. The attackers also chased them. The assault and commotion created stampede-like conditions in the village. Some people's shoes and slippers were left behind at the spot as they fled. Sahil described as an active history-sheeter According to Sub-Inspector Rupesh Kumar's complaint, several criminal cases have been registered against Sahil alias Bhuriya at several police stations. He has been described as an active history-sheeter at Sikheda police station. His history-sheet number is 36-A. A case has been registered against Sahil at Sikheda police station. According to the police, he was wanted in this case as well. After the incident, SI Rupesh Kumar and Constable Kuldeep underwent medical examinations. The sub-inspector then reached the police station and had a case registered against the accused. The police are searching for the named and absconding accused.

stories.title: UP village head and wife fire multiple rounds:Hand revolvers to children, say ‘This is how you aim’
stories.summary: A video has emerged from Gonda showing the village head and his wife firing a licensed revolver. In the video, children can also be seen holding revolvers and taking aim. However, it has not been confirmed whether the children fired the weapons. The video is said to be from Diwali last year. It emerged at 6 p.m. on Saturday. After the video surfaced, the police began an investigation. The police said the licence would be cancelled and action would be taken. Village head and wife seen firing in three videos The matter concerns Pure Tilak village in the Itiyathok Kotwali area. Three videos of village head Shakil Ahmed Khan and his wife, Parveen, have surfaced. In one video, the village head is seen sitting on a chair and firing a gun. In the second video, he is seen standing and firing a revolver. In the third video, his wife, Parveen, is seen firing. During this, children are also seen holding the revolver and taking aim. He said he fired after getting the revolver repaired Village head Shakil Ahmed Khan said there was a problem with his licensed revolver. He said he was firing it after getting it repaired. He said the video was from Diwali last year. Police say action will follow after the licence is seized Itiyathok Kotwali in-charge Gaurav Singh Tomar said, "A video of the firing has surfaced. The licensed revolver will be taken into custody and action will be taken in accordance with the rules. The licence will be cancelled." He said, “No one is allowed to engage in celebratory firing. Only the licence holder is permitted to keep the weapon. Seeing the revolver in the hands of the licence holder's wife and children is also a violation of the rules. Strict action will be taken based on the investigation.”

stories.title: Akhilesh’s voter list irregularity allegations prove correct:Election Commission suspends 5 BLOs; computer operator also faces job loss
stories.summary: The Election Commission has taken action in the voter list irregularities case in Azamgarh. It has directed that a computer operator and five BLOs be immediately removed from voter-list-related work. It has also ordered notices to be issued regarding the removal of these six employees from service. The commission said, "Of the 13 entries bearing the name Vikas Yadav found in the district, two had already been removed, while the remaining 11 names turned out to belong to different individuals." Following the investigation, Form 8 was filled out for 10 individuals to correct their names and details. Read the full report... SP had raised the issue Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference on 15 October and alleged that the name of a person called Vikas Yadav appeared 10 times on the voter list for Assembly Constituency 347 in Azamgarh. The Election Department immediately took cognisance of the complaint and sought a detailed investigation report from the Azamgarh district election officer. After receiving the report, the Election Department issued instructions for action after fixing responsibility on the staff and officials concerned. The investigation examined not only the role of the staff who prepared the voter list, but also that of the officials responsible for supervising their work. 11 different people from Azamgarh included among the 13 entries The investigation found that the name 'Vikas Yadav' was recorded 13 times in Hindi. However, a voter with the same name and father's name was found to be associated with the Chauri Chaura Assembly constituency in Gorakhpur district, and his entry was different from the other 13 entries in Azamgarh. Of the 13 entries recorded in Azamgarh's electoral roll, two had already been deleted. The remaining 11 entries were found to relate to 11 different individuals in the district. According to the investigation report, all these individuals are residing in their respective villages. Commission's clarification Of these 11 individuals, Form 8 has been filled out to correct the names and other details of the 10 individuals apart from the actual Vikas Yadav. This means the investigation did not confirm the existence of 10 fake entries in different places in the name of the same person; rather, it found that the names and details of different individuals needed to be corrected. Action to be taken against six employees The Election Commission has directed that the computer assistant at the voter registration centre and five BLOs found guilty in the case be immediately removed from work related to the electoral rolls. It has also ordered that notices be issued regarding the termination of their services. In addition, instructions have been issued to serve notices before taking action against the concerned computer assistant and BLOs under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Further action will be taken in accordance with the rules after the concerned officials are given an opportunity to present their case. Departmental action against three officials as well The negligence in the matter has not been considered limited to lower-level employees. Directions have been issued to initiate departmental proceedings against the then Electoral Registration Officer and two Assistant Electoral Registration Officers for negligence in discharging their responsibilities while preparing the electoral roll. Charge sheets will be issued against these officers. In addition, directions have been issued to serve notices on them before initiating action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Electoral rolls of all Assembly constituencies in Azamgarh to be investigated The Election Department has not confined the matter to just one Assembly constituency. The District Election Officer, Azamgarh, has been directed to conduct a detailed investigation into such discrepancies in the electoral rolls of all Assembly constituencies in the district. The District Election Officer will have to submit a detailed investigation report within one week. 13 'Vikas Yadavs' in Azamgarh voter list: Election Commission takes major action after Akhilesh Yadav's allegations; 6 employees to be removed from service, departmental inquiries to be registered against 3 senior officers. The Commission has sought a detailed report on the entire district within one week. The main purpose of this extensive investigation is to ensure that similar problems, such as identical names, fake entries, spelling errors or laxity in data entry, do not remain in any other assembly constituency.

stories.title: Noida STF arrests wanted robbery suspect in Meerut:Police catch the ₹50,000-rewarded accused at Sabzi Mandi crossing
stories.summary: The Noida unit of the STF arrested Kunal alias Kuldeep Tyagi, a wanted criminal carrying a ₹50,000 reward in connection with a robbery case in Meerut, in Lucknow on Saturday. The accused was present near the vegetable market crossing in the Jankipuram police station area. The STF informed the investigating officer from Meerut's Medical police station and carried out a joint operation with him to arrest the accused. According to the STF, on 15 April 2025, the accused entered a house in Takshila Colony in the Medical police station area of Meerut with his associates, intending to commit a robbery. When the occupants resisted and raised an alarm, all of them fled the spot. The accused had been absconding in the case. A reward of ₹50,000 had been announced for his arrest. Also accused of murder over a land dispute During questioning, the accused said that he was around 25 years old and had studied up to Class 12. In 2018, he had committed a theft at the Radha Soami Ashram in the village with his aunt's son, Manish. As he was a minor at the time, he was sent to a juvenile home in Bulandshahr. The two stayed there for around five to six months. After this, he attempted to break open and rob an ATM at a bank near DAV College in Bulandshahr with his associates Suraj and Saurabh. However, they were unable to break open the ATM. In this case, Suraj and Saurabh were arrested and sent to jail, while Kunal fled. The accused is also alleged to have shot and killed Satveer over an old land dispute in the Khurja Dehat police station area of Bulandshahr. After a case was registered in the matter, he was arrested and spent around one and a half years in jail. He met his accomplices in the robbery conspiracy in jail According to the STF, Kunal met Manish Solanki in jail. After being released, he joined Manish, Harsh and Vicky alias Vikas in planning to rob a large sum of money kept in a house in Meerut's Takshila Colony. On 15 April 2025, they all entered the house with the intention of carrying out the robbery, but had to flee after the occupants resisted and raised an alarm. According to the STF, the accused had been constantly changing locations to evade arrest. The operation to arrest him was carried out under the supervision of Additional Superintendent of Police Raj Kumar Mishra and led by Deputy Superintendent of Police Navendu Kumar. stories.title: Mother pushes son away before coming under truck:Wheel crushes her head in Kanpur Dehat; flesh pieces collected in a plastic bag
stories.summary: A mother in Kanpur Dehat died after saving her son. The woman was crossing the road with her nine-year-old son when a speeding truck came in front of them. The mother pushed her son away and came under the truck herself. The truck's wheel ran over the mother's head, killing her instantly. The accident was so horrific that pieces of flesh were scattered across the road for 50 metres. Police had to collect the pieces of flesh in polythene bags. The accident took place in the Rania police station area on Saturday afternoon. Now, read the full story... Mother loses her life while saving her son Dharmendra Singh Chandel, who lives in Perajore village, is a tiles worker. His family comprises his wife, Maya Devi (33), and four children-Kanhaiya, Gopal, Kishan and Divyanshi. On Saturday afternoon, Maya came to Raipur to take her nine-year-old son Kishan to a doctor. She was returning home with him afterwards. She was crossing the Auraiya-Etawah Highway to board a tempo. At the same time, a speeding truck was travelling from Auraiya towards Kanpur. On seeing the truck approaching, Maya immediately pushed her son Kishan backwards. The boy escaped unharmed, but Maya came under the truck herself. She died on the spot after a wheel ran over her head. The son screamed after seeing his mother writhing in agony before his eyes. As a crowd began to gather, the driver abandoned the truck and fled the spot. CO Sanjay Singh said, “The body has been sent for post-mortem. The truck has been seized and a search is under way for the driver. A case will be registered and action taken on the basis of the family's complaint.”

stories.title: Akhilesh calls people from Uttarakhand UP’s biggest infiltrators:CM Dhami recalls Rampur Tiraha firing, says ‘Father ordered firing, son calls them infiltrators’
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has said that the highest number of infiltrators in Uttar Pradesh are from Uttarakhand. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has strongly objected to the statement. Questioning the description of people from Uttarakhand as infiltrators, Dhami reminded Yadav of the Rampur Tiraha firing incident. The Chief Minister said that Uttarakhand is both Devbhoomi and Veerbhoomi. This sacred land has given the country saints, soldiers and numerous personalities dedicated to national service. In such a situation, calling its people infiltrators is an insult to their self-respect and struggle. It is worth noting that Akhilesh Yadav's wife is herself from Uttarakhand. Her family used to live in Pauri, but later moved to Jogiwala in Dehradun. Dhami targets Akhilesh by referring to an incident during his father's tenure Chief Minister Dhami mentioned the Rampur Tiraha firing incident, one of the most sensitive chapters in the Uttarakhand statehood movement, in his statement. He said that when Akhilesh Yadav's father, Mulayam Singh Yadav, was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, protesters demanding a separate Uttarakhand state were fired upon at Rampur Tiraha in Muzaffarnagar. Linked Devbhoomi's honour to the statehood movement Dhami's statement prominently highlighted Uttarakhand's identity and the history of the statehood movement. People had fought for a long time in the movement demanding a separate state. The Rampur Tiraha firing incident is one such event from that movement that continues to hold an important place in Uttarakhand's political and social consciousness. Referring to this background, the Chief Minister said that portraying the identity of the people of Uttarakhand in a derogatory manner was an insult to their struggles and sacrifices. In this way, Dhami made Akhilesh Yadav's alleged statement not merely a political comment, but an issue linked to the pride of the state. 3 questions for Congress, seeks response on ally's statement Chief Minister Dhami also cornered the Congress on the issue. He asked whether the Congress supported the statement made by its political ally, Akhilesh Yadav. Was the Congress willing to accept the people of Uttarakhand being called infiltrators? The Chief Minister said that the Congress should answer the people of Devbhoomi. Through this question, Dhami brought the Congress, along with the Samajwadi Party, to the centre of the political debate. The Congress's official position on the issue and the full context of Akhilesh Yadav's statement will now be important. Indiscriminate firing took place in Mussoorie on 2 September 1994 Police opened indiscriminate fire on Uttarakhand statehood activists in Mussoorie on 2 September 1994, during the government of the then Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav. Six activists were killed and around 18 people were injured in the firing at Jhulaghar. The then police circle officer, Umakant Tripathi, was also killed in the firing. The incident shook the entire hill region and further intensified the movement for a separate state. See pictures from 2 September 1994- 16-year-old Sanjeev was hit by five bullets Sanjeev Chauhan, a direct victim of the Mussoorie firing, was just 16 years old at the time. Originally from Kandakhhal village in Tehri, Sanjeev's family was living in Mussoorie's Bakery Hill at the time. He was a high school student. He was hit by five bullets in the firing at Jhulaghar on 2 September. Around 18 other people were injured in the incident. Anger erupted in Mussoorie after the Khatima firing On 1 September 1994, seven people were killed in police firing on activists protesting in Khatima over the demand for a separate state. When news of the incident reached Mussoorie the next day, anger and grief spread across the city. People came out of their homes and began gathering at the Mussoorie Library. Raising slogans, the activists reached Jhoolaghar on Mall Road. During this, the police opened fire on them. Belmati Chauhan, Hansa Dhanai, Balbir Singh Negi, Dhanpat Singh, Madan Mohan Mamgain and Rai Singh Bangari were killed in the firing. The then Deputy Superintendent of Police, Umakant Tripathi, also died in the firing. Firing incidents took place at several places in 1994 During the Uttarakhand statehood movement in 1994, police opened fire on protesters not only in Mussoorie and Khatima, but also in Muzaffarnagar, Dehradun, Kotdwar, Nainital and Srinagar. More than 40 activists were killed in these incidents. Activists say cases were registered against the officials responsible for opening fire on unarmed protesters, but several cases are still pending in the courts even after more than three decades. The issue of the guilty not being punished continues to be raised among statehood activists.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar alleges govt jailed people offering namaz after beating them:Says education minister had to resign; ‘those wearing blue bands will get justice’
stories.summary: Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad said on Friday that the government is beating people who offer namaz on the road with shoes and sending them to jail. "They do not know that when the blue bands are put on, we will not stop until justice is secured. Look at how the Union Education Minister had to resign." Chandrashekhar reached Morna in Muzaffarnagar at 2:30 p.m. During this, he said, "The government's police do not grant permission for Babasaheb's birth anniversary. They certainly raise the slogan of 'together with all, development for all', but appeasement runs through every vein of theirs. These people want to weaken the country. We will work to eradicate this mindset." The meeting is being held in support of party candidate Ravindra Bhati from the Mirapur Assembly constituency. Members of the Gurjar community welcomed MP Chandrashekhar on the stage by presenting him with a statue of Emperor Mihir Bhoj. Read MP Chandrashekhar's key statements... Everyone's children should study in government schools Speaking about bringing changes to education policy, Chandrashekhar said they would introduce a policy under which, after Class 1, all children should receive education in government schools-whether they are the children of villagers, Secretariat officials, patwaris, kanungos, tehsildars, sub-divisional magistrates, additional district magistrates, district magistrates, commissioners, additional chief secretaries, the chief secretary, village heads or district panchayat chairpersons. Government jobs should go only to those who have educated their children in government schools. Poor people cannot compete with private schools yet. Paying a monthly fee of ₹10,000 is still not possible for the poor. Government will never provide free education On the one hand, this government's policy is to shut down government schools and ruin the future of the poor. On the other hand, the Azad Party's policy is to provide education to all children from Classes 1 to 12. Whenever we talk about education, the government talks about temples and mosques. It talks about Hindus and Muslims, because it will give you free flour, free lentils, free rice and free salt and sugar, but it will not provide free education. This is because education gives you the understanding to move forward. Voter count around three lakh The social equation in the Meerapur Assembly constituency is such that the support of different communities influences the electoral contest. Amid the presence of other parties such as the Rashtriya Lok Dal and the Samajwadi Party, it is important for the Azad Samaj Party to expand its support. The Mirapur Assembly constituency has around three lakh voters. There were 3,25,277 voters in the 2024 by-election, while the figure was reported to be 2,99,491 according to a 2026 report. Muslim, Dalit, Gurjar and Jat voters are considered important to the electoral equations in the Mirapur Assembly constituency. According to estimated social data available in media reports, the constituency is said to have around one lakh Muslim voters, approximately 50,000 Dalit voters, around 30,000 Gurjar voters and approximately 29,000 Jat voters. Besides these, voters from the Saini, Pal, Kashyap, Prajapati and other backward classes also play a role in the electoral arithmetic. These community-wise figures are estimates and do not represent an official caste-wise voter count. The aim is to mobilise support for candidate Ravindra Bhati and strengthen the party's political activity in the area.

stories.title: Shraddha seen holding deceased boyfriend's hand while leaving:Sister was also with them; CCTV footage from before Shiva’s death emerges
stories.summary: Two more videos of Shraddha Dubey, the accused in the murder of millionaire businessman Shiva Sharma in Lucknow, surfaced on Saturday. In the first video, Shraddha is seen alone, while in the second, she is seen descending the stairs holding Shiva's hand. Her sister Rashmi is also with the two in both videos. The first video of Shraddha was recorded early in the morning and shows her returning alone after attending a late-night party. She is seen wearing a western outfit. The second video is said to be from 4 August. Several videos linked to Shraddha Dubey have been the subject of discussion since Shiva's death. On Thursday, a court sent model Shraddha Dubey, her sister and their driver to jail in 10 days' judicial custody. Before this, the police questioned her for 6.5 hours at the Hazratganj police station. The three were arrested from an apartment in Nagpur 11 days after the incident. 'She was upset about CCTV cameras being installed in the apartment' Ajay Rai, a neighbour who lives in Shraddha's apartment complex, said she was extremely short-tempered. She used words that even a man would think twice before saying, but she spoke in that language without hesitation. Shraddha also argued with us when we installed CCTV cameras. She returned to her flat while hurling abuses. 'They left using the lift on the day of the incident' In addition, nobody, including Shraddha, used the stairs on the day of the incident. They all cleverly used the lift to leave because Shraddha knew that CCTV cameras had been installed on the first floor. She also knew the direction in which the CCTV camera installed towards the balcony was pointed because the side where Shiva fell is the back of the CCTV camera. Meanwhile, Shraddha's flat and Ajay Rai's flat are on the same side of the building.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at 6 shops opposite Amity University:Cylinder blast kills one; 6 fire engines douse flames in 30 minutes
stories.summary: A fire broke out at around six tea and snack shops opposite Amity University in Sector 125, Noida, on Saturday afternoon. The flames spread rapidly through the tin-shed shops. Small LPG cylinders were heard exploding, triggering panic at the scene. During firefighting and rescue operations, a man was found unconscious. He was taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The deceased was identified as Sahil Sharma. The police have sent the body for a post-mortem. A plume of black smoke from the fire was visible from around 2 km away. People recorded videos of the incident from nearby buildings, which later went viral on social media. Around 20 minutes after receiving the alert, five fire engines reached the spot and began firefighting operations. First, take a look at these three pictures Fire spread rapidly after cylinders exploded; rescue operation lasted an hour The tea and food stalls opposite Amity University were made of tin sheds. The fire spread from one shop to another. During the incident, small cylinders kept at some shops exploded, causing the flames to intensify. After the fire was extinguished, the shops were filled with thick smoke. To check whether anyone was trapped inside, firefighters entered wearing fire jackets and oxygen kits. The rescue operation continued for around an hour. During the operation, one person was brought out and taken to hospital, but he could not be saved. Rescue operation lasted an hour Firefighters also removed six to seven partially burnt cylinders from the shops. They cooled them by spraying water to eliminate the risk of another fire or explosion. The goods kept inside the shops were reduced to ashes in the blaze. Chief Fire Officer (CFO) Pradeep Kumar said the fire was extensive and engulfed the entire cluster of tin-shed shops. A large number of LPG cylinders were found inside the shops. Vehicular movement on the road halted The shops were located along a road approximately 45 metres wide. Vehicular movement was stopped during firefighting and relief operations. A crowd gathered at the scene. According to officials, the cause of the fire is not yet known and is being investigated. The shops are reportedly believed to have been built illegally. As the college was closed at the time of the incident, there were fewer customers at the shops and several of them were shut. This helped avert a bigger tragedy. The police have sent the deceased's body for a post-mortem and initiated further proceedings.

stories.title: SP alleges OBC quota posts cut in TGT recruitment:Chairman says reservation is correct, based on school-wise vacancies
stories.summary: An issued for the recruitment of teachers and principals in aided schools in Uttar Pradesh has triggered allegations of reservation rules being ignored. It is being claimed that the OBC quota was reduced while more than 16% of seats were reserved for the EWS category. Samajwadi Party spokesperson Manoj Kaka claimed in a post on X that the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) were given 16.25% reservation instead of the prescribed 10%. Meanwhile, the Other Backward Classes (OBC) received 25.02% reservation instead of 27%. He alleged that, after the recruitment of 69,000 teachers, the interests of the OBC community were once again being undermined. However, speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, commission chairman Prashant Kumar said there had been no error in the reservation process. He said the recruitment was announced based on school-wise vacancies. Posts were advertised under the category to which the vacant post in each school belonged. The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission (UPESSC) had issued three recruitment s on October 23 for teachers and principals in aided secondary schools. Under these s, recruitment will be conducted for 17,735 trained graduate teacher (TGT) posts, 1,172 headmaster posts in high schools and 1,475 principal posts in intermediate-level schools. However, questions are being raised over reservation in the TGT recruitment. Bhaskar investigated these allegations. Read this report to find out the truth… Chairman Prashant Kumar says, ‘Misinformation is being spread’ Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission chairman Prashant Kumar said that the reservation figures being shared on social media were calculated by adding all 17,735 TGT posts together. The recruitment lists 6,704 posts (37.80%) for the unreserved category, 3,698 (20.85%) for Scheduled Castes (SC), 13 (0.07%) for Scheduled Tribes (ST), 4,438 (25.02%) for Other Backward Classes (OBC) and 2,882 (16.25%) for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). Now, here is what social media claims Social media posts claim that, according to the prescribed reservation percentages, 3,725 posts (21%) should have been allocated to SCs, 355 (2%) to STs, 4,789 (27%) to OBCs and 1,773 (10%) to EWS. Based on these figures, it is alleged that 27 fewer posts were allocated to SCs, 342 fewer to STs and 351 fewer to OBCs, while EWS was given 1,109 additional posts. Chairman says reservation was implemented by treating each school as a unit Commission chairman Prashant Kumar told Dainik Bhaskar that the recruitment is being conducted on the basis of school-wise vacancies. Reservation has been implemented by treating each school as a separate unit. This means that a vacant post in a school has been advertised under the category to which it belongs. Appointments will also be made according to the category of the vacant post in the respective school. Reservation is being calculated on social media by adding up all the posts, which is creating confusion about the recruitment process.

stories.title: Sub-inspector calls woman to room for private meeting:Officer says, ‘Follow my orders and I’ll make your rivals meet Mukhtar’s fate’; suspended
stories.summary: The sub-inspector who called a woman complainant in Mau and asked her to meet him alone has been suspended. A 16-minute audio recording of an objectionable conversation with the woman had emerged. The incident took place at the Dubari police outpost under Madhuban police station, around 32 kilometres from the district headquarters. The accused sub-inspector has been identified as Om Prakash Singh. The woman is associated with the Nishad Party. She is from Gorakhpur and currently lives in Mau's Madhuban area. After the audio emerged on 21 October, Superintendent of Police Sarvesh Kumar Mishra attached the sub-inspector to the police lines. After the audio was confirmed during the investigation, he was suspended on Friday evening. First, here is what the audio contains... An audio recording of a conversation between the victim and accused sub-inspector Om Prakash Singh surfaced on 21 October. In it, the accused sub-inspector can be heard referring to action against the opposing party in the woman's case. The sub-inspector said, "If you listen to me, we will make the condition of your opponents like that of Mukhtar Ansari. I took serious action in your case, but you stopped speaking to me. Tell me, did I fall short in any way? I have done so much now that they will keep making rounds for six months. Has anyone been able to overturn my order? Once I have said something, that is final." In the audio, the accused sub-inspector asks the woman to make a video call. He also says that a man will come to pick her up and that she should come with him, while talking about meeting her. He says she will come back to his room. During the conversation, he repeatedly makes objectionable remarks. Now, the full story... A woman living in Madhuban and associated with the Nishad Party had gone to the Dubari Police Outpost a few days ago. Sub-Inspector Om Prakash Singh was posted there. The woman had a land dispute with some people from her village. Acting on her complaint, Sub-Inspector Om Prakash Singh called the other party to the police outpost and took the necessary action. The complainant said the police had taken action against her opponents. As she was leaving for home, the sub-inspector took her mobile number. The woman alleged that the sub-inspector then began calling her repeatedly. Sub-inspector attached to police lines after audio emerges, then suspended The audio caused an uproar in the police department. The SP immediately attached sub-inspector Om Prakash Singh to the police lines and assigned CO Satyendra Bhushan Tiwari to investigate the matter. Following the preliminary investigation report, the sub-inspector was suspended. Further investigation will now be conducted by Jitendra Singh, the CO of Mohammadabad Gohna. CO says audio confirmed as genuine during investigation CO Satyendra Bhushan Tiwari said: An audio recording of SI Om Prakash Singh had gone viral. The preliminary investigation confirmed that the audio contained indecent and objectionable conversation. He has been suspended.
