stories.title: 'After 2027, Congress leaders will dance on streets':BJP MP Ravi Kishan on Kharge's statement, says entire Congress has lost its mental balance
stories.summary: BJP MP Ravi Kishan Shukla strongly criticised Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge over his recent statement on Monday. He said Congress leaders were frustrated and had lost their mental balance after seeing the BJP move ahead. He added that after 2027, Congress leaders would beat their chests and dance on the streets. Speaking to people at his residence in Gorakhpur on Monday morning, Ravi Kishan said such language was not expected from a senior leader like Kharge. He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi's father was no longer alive, yet comments were still being made about him. He said this showed the thinking of Congress leaders and their frustration. Ravi Kishan also said Congress leaders knew they had no political future left. He claimed that 10 lakh people had gathered in Varanasi to see the Prime Minister, while Congress leaders could not even fill a hall with a capacity of 500 people. He said this was the reason behind their frustration. They start having epileptic seizures as soon as they see the Prime Minister's face Ravi Kishan said that whenever Congress leaders see Prime Minister Narendra Modi's face, they start having epileptic seizures. Their mental condition will worsen further after the 2027 Assembly elections. He said that using such derogatory language about the Prime Minister's father was against Indian civilisation, culture, values, moral principles and decency. Was such language used at the behest of the Gandhi family? Ravi Kishan also shared a post on his Facebook wall condemning the incident. He said he wanted to ask Sonia Gandhi whether Kharge had used such language at the behest of the Gandhi family and, if not, whether Congress would ask him to resign. He said the Prime Minister was held in the hearts of crores of people. The country would not tolerate insults to him and his family. Congress should answer whether such indecent language was in keeping with the dignity of the office of national president.

stories.title: 63-year-old man dies by suicide in Gorakhpur:Records video accusing landlord and his wife of harassment
stories.summary: A 63-year-old man died after consuming poison at his shop in Gorakhpur. Before the incident, he had recorded a video accusing his landlord and the landlord's wife of mentally harassing him by involving him in false cases. He held them responsible for his death. After receiving information about the incident, his family rushed to the shop and found him unconscious. They called an ambulance and took him to the hospital, where he died late on Sunday night during treatment. The police took his body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. Further investigation is underway. The case falls under the Kotwali police station area. What happened? Shadab Khan, a resident of Bakshipur, told the police that his 63-year-old uncle, Nazir Ahmad Khan, also known as Pappu, had consumed a poisonous substance at his shop at around 3 pm on Sunday. The family members said they found a video on their mobile phone on Monday. After watching it, they filed a written complaint against the accused at the police station. In the 1-minute-30-second video, Nazir Ahmad Khan said he was taking this step because he was troubled by his landlord, Anoop Kumar Jaiswal, who lives in Bakshipur under the Kotwali police station area, and the landlord's wife. The police have started an investigation into the case. The allegations made in the video are being investigated. He had accused him of molesting his wife They would regularly harass me over one matter or another. Some time ago, Anoop had accused me of molesting his wife. I presented evidence at the Kotwali police station and managed to prove my innocence. Now, a case has been filed over something else, which I know nothing about. The police came, conducted an inquiry, submitted their report and left. They said that something or the other was being done to the shop without notice. The water pipe has been broken, and no one can even stand inside the shop. I am distressed, and therefore I am ending my life. Police engaged in investigation Shadab Khan said that the deceased was unmarried and had no children. The Kotwali station house officer said that the body had been sent for post-mortem. An FIR has been registered and further action is under way. The situation at the spot is peaceful.

stories.title: Violent clash at Lohia Hospital’s main gate:Two groups attack each other with sticks, overturn several roadside stalls
stories.summary: A fight broke out between two groups on Monday outside Gate No. 8 of Lohia Hospital in the Vibhutikhand police station area of Lucknow. The argument soon turned violent, with both groups attacking each other with sticks. Someone at the spot recorded the incident, and the video later spread widely on social media. The video shows several young men chasing and beating each other with sticks. The fight caused chaos in the area. Patients face problems The fight caused problems for people who had come to Lohia Hospital for treatment. They could not enter the hospital through the gate while the clash was going on. The fight continued for around half an hour. Even after the police arrived following a complaint, the men involved in the fight continued attacking each other in front of them. Some people who had come to the hospital for treatment had stepped outside to buy food and drinks. When a roadside cart was overturned during the clash, their food also spilled onto the ground.

stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh News: उत्तर प्रदेश में प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी को लेकर कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खरगे की टिप्पणी पर मंत्री योगेंद्र उपाध्याय ने अपनी प्रतिक्रिया दी है। उन्होंने खड़गे के बयान पर नाराजगी जताते हुए कहा कि अभद्र भाषा का इस्तेमाल करना उनकी संस्कृति का हिस्सा है। उपाध्याय ने अपनी बात रखते हुए कहा कि अगर किसी व्यक्ति को तोहफा नहीं दिया जाता है, तो वह कुछ समय के लिए रोता है। लेकिन अगर किसी व्यक्ति को मूल्य नहीं सिखाए जाते हैं, तो वह जीवन भर रोता है। उन्होंने कहा कि जब किसी राजनीतिक व्यक्ति में मूल्यों की कमी होती है, तो वह केवल खुद ही नहीं रोता, बल्कि अपने बयानों से पूरे समाज और देश को भी रुलाता है। मंत्री ने आगे कहा कि ये वही लोग हैं जिनके नेतृत्व में मूल्यों की कमी है और इसी वजह से इस तरह के बयान दिए जाते हैं।

stories.title: Yogi says India has two ‘Miyans’, one junior, one senior:Accuses them of favouring Bangladeshi infiltrators in Kanpur
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will visit Bithoor in Kanpur today for Valmiki Jayanti. He will offer prayers at the historic Maharishi Valmiki Ashram there. He will then address a public meeting at Nanarao Peshwa Park. During the visit, he may announce development projects worth around ₹400 crore for the Bithoor and Bilhaur Assembly constituencies. The district administration has completed preparations for the Chief Minister's visit. On Sunday evening, officials reviewed the security arrangements at the public meeting venue, including the stage and the park. See 3 pictures... Programme to begin at 10 a.m. Activities at the public meeting venue will begin at 10 a.m. as part of the Chief Minister's programme. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will then arrive in Bithoor. He will first pay his respects at the Maharishi Valmiki Ashram, followed by an address at a public meeting in Nanarao Peshwa Park. According to the proposed programme, the Chief Minister may remain in Bithoor for around 2 hours. During this time, he will also review exhibitions set up by various departments. Development projects worth ₹400 crore likely to be announced Development projects worth around ₹400 crore are likely to be announced for the Bithoor and Bilhaur Assembly constituencies at the Chief Minister's public meeting. Preparations have been made for the foundation-laying ceremonies and inaugurations of several development works under these projects. For this, details of projects have been sought from various departments, including the Public Works Department (PWD), Kanpur Development Authority (KDA), nagar panchayat and nagar palika. Beneficiaries of 10 schemes to be honoured The Chief Minister may also honour beneficiaries of various government schemes during the public meeting. The key schemes include: Old-age Pension Scheme Chief Minister Housing Scheme Ration Card Scheme Tool Kit Distribution Scheme Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Scheme Preparations are also under way to honour beneficiaries of other schemes. Beneficiaries of around 10 schemes may be included in the programme. Political discussion over CM's visit after By-election Political circles are also abuzz with discussion over the Chief Minister's visit to Bithoor. Earlier this month, the elder brother of MLA Abhijeet Singh Sanga won the by-election for Nagar Panchayat chairperson in the Bithoor area. In this context, the Chief Minister's visit after the by-election is being considered important not only from the perspective of regional development but also politically.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav says ‘we want power, not sainthood’:Welcomes 4 BJP leaders to SP, gives house keys to 5 beneficiaries
stories.summary: Former Uttar Pradesh-cadre IAS officer Ram Bahadur Pasi, who was close to Mayawati, joined the Samajwadi Party on Monday, 26 October. Several prominent leaders from Badaun, Meerut and other districts also joined the SP in the presence of Akhilesh Yadav and Shivpal Singh Yadav. This is being seen as a major step in terms of the SP's PDA strategy. Who is Ram Bahadur Pasi? Ram Bahadur, a PCS officer of the 1977 batch, was promoted to the IAS in 2010 and retired in 2015. He has held key positions such as District Magistrate of Gonda and Vice-Chairman of the Lucknow/Ghaziabad Development Authority (LDA). In 2017, he contested the Mohanlalganj seat on a BSP ticket but lost to the Samajwadi Party candidate by a margin of just 530 votes. He subsequently formed the Nagrik Ekta Party and joined the BJP in 2022. He is now beginning a new innings with the Samajwadi Party. After joining the Samajwadi Party, Ram Bahadur Pasi said, "I feel fortunate that the national president inducted me into the Samajwadi Party, and I thank him. I was in service until 2015. Akhilesh Yadav was the Chief Minister when I retired." Sabina Parveen enters politics after returning from the United States Sabina Parveen, who returned from the United States, also joined the Samajwadi Party. She said, "I have not come to join the SP; I have come to become part of Akhilesh Yadav's movement. People are leaving India, while I am returning from the United States. We have to fulfil the dreams our ancestors had seen. I want to work in the education, health, research and development sectors." Sabina has expressed her desire to work at the grassroots level in the Kundarki Assembly constituency and become the SP candidate. Prominent figures from Budaun, Meerut and other districts also join the party Other prominent figures joining the party include- After joining the Samajwadi Party, Dara Singh Prajapati said, "I have not joined for a ticket or for an adjustment. I have joined the SP to make Akhilesh Yadav the chief minister." Mantosh Yadav, who builds houses for the poor, honoured During the programme, Akhilesh Yadav honoured Mantosh Yadav, who builds houses for the poor and provides them for just ₹5 lakh. The keys to their new homes were also handed over to five beneficiaries on stage. Senior SP leader Shivpal Singh Yadav, along with MPs Awadhesh Prasad (Ayodhya), Harendra Malik (Muzaffarnagar), Aditya Yadav (Badaun) and the Aonla MP, was also present.

stories.title: Lucknow triple murder over car parking dispute:Neighbour opens fire, killing father, son and brother; son was to marry on December 5
stories.summary: Three members of a family were shot dead in broad daylight in Lucknow on Monday. The victims were a father, his son and the father's younger brother. The father and son died on the spot, while the brother died at a trauma centre. The incident took place at around 10:35 am in the Saadatganj police station area. Shivaji Tiwari (62), who lived in Brahmin Tola in Naubasta, was a retired Secretariat employee. He had also served as the district-level general secretary of the RSS. His brother, Shivendra Tiwari, also known as Shambhu, worked at Lucknow University. Shivaji's son, Suyash (30), ran an electrical goods business. He was scheduled to get married on December 5. On Monday, Suyash parked his car near a raised platform in the area. A short while later, when Shambhu came outside, Rishabh started arguing with him over the parking. Hearing the argument, Shivaji also came out of the house. During the dispute, Rishabh lost his temper and shot both of them. When Suyash came out after hearing the gunshots, Rishabh shot him on the stairs near the house. Rishabh (30) worked as a navigation officer in the Merchant Navy. He was reportedly removed from his job. Police Commissioner Tarun Gaba visited the crime scene. Around 50-60 police personnel have been deployed at the spot. See pictures

stories.title: 3 sisters’ funeral processions leave together in Firozabad:Mother repeatedly faints; father dies of shock after son’s death
stories.summary: An accident in Firozabad devastated an entire family. Five people from the same village died, including three biological sisters. When the three sisters' funeral biers were carried out together, the entire village broke down in tears. Their mother became hysterical on seeing her daughters' bodies. She kept losing consciousness as she wept. Meanwhile, the father could not bear the shock of his son's death. He too, having been battling cancer, passed away. Six people from the village have now died in the accident, while 10 others are injured. The accident took place at around 9 p.m. on Sunday in Chhatanpur village under Nasirpur police station, about 35 kilometres from the district headquarters. After collectively arranging the marriage of Tesu and Jhanjhi, villagers were heading outside the village towards a beri tree for the immersion ceremony. At that point, a Delhi-registered Brezza car coming from the Lucknow-Agra Expressway ran over the villagers walking along the roadside. See the pictures below : Learn about the accident At around 9 p.m. on Sunday, villagers in Chhatanpur village, under the Nasirpur police station area, were heading towards a Bari tree outside the village for immersion after collectively solemnising the marriage of Tesu and Jhanjhi. Women, men and children were moving ahead while singing traditional wedding songs. Meanwhile, a Delhi-registered Brezza car coming from the Lucknow-Agra Expressway ran over the villagers walking along the roadside. Babli, 18, the daughter of Brajesh from the village, died in the accident. After the death, the car driver sped away towards Shikohabad. The villagers pursued the car on motorcycles and reached a spot near a hospital around 9 kilometres away, where they tried to surround it. Seeing himself surrounded, the driver hit a motorcycle and again drove the car towards the accident site. Car occupants flee after hitting someone, return to run them over when surrounded As the car fled, it ran over around 15 villagers again. This time, three daughters of Shishupal Yadav of the village-Akanksha (17), Anjali (15) and Gunnu (10)-and Harish Kumar (25), the son of Gambhir Singh, died on the spot. Chandraveer (55), the son of Amar Singh; Umashankar (40), the son of Ram Brajesh; Dheeraj (30) and Sonu (29), the sons of Sukhveer; and Mayank (11), Chandraveer's son, were among 10 people injured. All of them were admitted to the district hospital, where they are undergoing treatment. After the accident, villagers caught the four youths in the car and beat them with sticks. The police then reached the spot, rescued them from the crowd and took them to the police station. It is reported that the occupants of the car were intoxicated at the time of the accident. After the accident, District Magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma, Senior Superintendent of Police Aditya Langhe and other officials visited the hospital and took stock of the situation. Witnesses said: The driver had been drinking Shivani, an eyewitness to the incident, said the car hit people from the village. The driver had been drinking. After hitting them once, he drove away. He returned and hit them again. The identities of two people travelling in the car have been established. They include Aqeel and Irfan, residents of Wazirpur in Delhi. Two of them are also reported to be in serious condition after being beaten. Now read the village report The family is devastated following the deaths of Sishupal's three daughters, Akanksha, Anjali and Gunnu, in the accident. His wife Radha and two sons, Govind and Babu, are inconsolable. When the funeral biers of all three daughters were carried out together, hundreds of villagers were moved to tears. While Babli's father Brajesh is employed as a peon at JS University, his wife Sangeeta also fainted after crying uncontrollably. Villagers helped her. Meanwhile, Harish's father, who lost his life in the accident, was suffering from advanced cancer. He had been undergoing treatment in Lucknow for a long time. Harish's wife Soni was inconsolable. Harish had got married three years ago. They had a son a year ago. However, the child died soon after birth. Harish's mother Kanti Devi and brothers Monu and Suraj were devastated. When Harish's father, who was admitted to a hospital in Lucknow, was informed of his death, he too suffered a deep shock. He died shortly afterwards. Relatives are bringing his body to Firozabad.

stories.title: Teen falls 30 feet from overbridge, dies in UP:Parents faint on seeing son's body; had gone out to get guitar
stories.summary: Only son died after falling 30 feet from an overbridge in Sant Kabir Nagar. The teenager fell face down onto the road below. The accident occurred at around 12 midnight. The boy's parents fainted after seeing his body. Police, who reached the spot after receiving information from local residents, sent the body for a post-mortem examination. The teenager was identified as Shashwat Rai (17). His father, Sanjay Rai, is a government teacher at the Composite School in Gagani Babu, under the Mehdawal development block. His mother, Anita Rai, is a private teacher at Blooming Buds private school. Shashwat was originally a resident of the Awal Kewatliya locality in Mehdawal. The family had been living in a rented house in Khalilabad city for the past five years. According to his family, Shashwat left home at around 8 p.m. on a bike to fetch his guitar. Shashwat also had a four-year-old sister.

stories.title: Bank manager’s wife dies after sudden fall at hotel:Head injury proves fatal; couple married four months ago in Jhansi
stories.summary: A bank manager's wife died at a hotel in Jhansi. The couple had married just four months earlier. They had booked a room at the hotel and checked in on Saturday. The next day, as they were preparing to check out, the woman, who was standing at the room's door, suddenly fell backwards, landing on her head and suffering a severe head injury. Blood spread across the floor. Her husband picked her up and carried her into the room before taking her to a nearby hospital with the help of the hotel staff, where doctors declared her dead. The incident took place in the Seepri Bazaar police station area at 12 noon on Sunday. CCTV footage of the incident has also emerged. It shows the woman walking towards the room with her husband and a hotel employee. The employee and her husband enter the room, while the woman follows them to the door. Within four seconds, she collapses while standing. According to the police, the deceased, Muskaan (27), was staying at Hotel Rishabh with her husband, Nilesh (33). Nilesh is a resident of Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, and is posted as a society manager at MP Gramin Bank. Muskaan's father has accused his son-in-law of murder. Watch two CCTV clips- Married four months earlier and had come to her maternal home for examination Ramjilal Simoliya, who lives in Nainagarh, Premnagar, said, "My daughter Muskaan married Nilesh on 29 June. We held her wedding with great fanfare at Hotel JS Grand. Muskaan's JE exam was scheduled for 28 October, so we brought her home on 10 October. I thought she would sit the exam and stay with me for a few days." "We had no idea that Nilesh would suddenly arrive at night and take Muskaan away early in the morning. Nilesh arrived at around 11:30 pm on the night of 23 October. The next day, he lied to me and took Muskaan with him. He said he was going to his maternal aunt's house in Ganesh Vihar Colony. I told him, 'Go on, son.'" "On Sunday, Nilesh called and said, 'Please come to Rudra Hotel at Chitra Chauraha.' There is no Rudra Hotel in our area. When we searched, we found out that it was Rishabh Hotel. When we reached Rishabh Hotel, we found that instead of taking Muskaan to his maternal aunt's house, he had taken her to the hotel. The hotel register showed their entry from 23 to 24 October." Son-in-law called us to the nursing home Ramjilal said that while they were at the hotel, Nilesh called again and asked them to come to Kapoor Nursing Home. They reached Kapoor Nursing Home, but Nilesh was not there either. Nilesh called them again and asked them to come first to the medical college and then to the Civil Hospital. When they reached the Civil Hospital, they found Muskaan dead there. Nilesh says that Muskaan had fallen. However, I suspect that he grabbed my Muskaan by the face and hit her head against the wall. She has suffered an injury to her head. Father-in-law says: Son-in-law had relationships with other women Ramjilal Simauliya said, "Nilesh used to work in a private job. He got a job at a bank just 15 days ago. He has relationships with other women. He already has a wife who lives in Indore. We learnt this after our daughter's wedding. He would repeatedly tell my daughter, 'My first wife is better. You do not have what she has.'" SP City says cause of death will be known after post-mortem SP City Preeti Singh said, When the police reached the hospital, the husband was present there. He said they were checking out and were going to the room with the hotel staff to collect their belongings. Muskaan suddenly fell at that point. The police reached the hotel and inspected the scene. The couple had stayed in room number 212. CCTV footage is being examined. The allegations made by the deceased's father are being investigated. The cause of death will become clear after the post-mortem report is received.

stories.title: Brother kills sister over interfaith marriage in Mathura:Buries body in cemetery; she married Hindu man 4 months ago
stories.summary: In Mathura, a brother strangled his sister to death for marrying a man from another religion. He then buried her body. When her husband called her from Rajasthan, her phone was switched off. After he was unable to contact her despite making considerable efforts for 15 days, he called her family and asked about her. At first, they kept evading the question, and then stopped answering his calls. He suspected that something had happened to her. He subsequently informed the police at a police station in Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan, that his wife had been kidnapped. Rajasthan Police emailed Mathura Police on 23 October, asking them to investigate the case. Following this, police from the Govind Nagar police station in Mathura began making inquiries. Police first questioned the young woman's family. They continued to give evasive replies. Initially, they said they did not know where the girl was. Later, her brother said that she had died after suffering an electric shock. On the night of 24 October Police detained the brother on suspicion. During questioning, he repeatedly said that his sister had died from an electric shock, but when the police put him under pressure, he said that he had strangled her to death and buried her body in a cemetery. On Sunday, the young woman's body was exhumed from the cemetery on the orders of the city magistrate and sent for a post-mortem examination. The brother, who is accused of the murder, has been arrested. The police are questioning the mother and maternal aunt after taking them into custody. The case relates to the Govind Nagar police station area of Mathura. Read the full case in detail They fell in love after working together in Delhi for two years According to the police, Nazia, also known as Jannat, who lived in Badrinagar Nai Basti in Mathura, worked at a factory in Delhi that manufactured sportswear. It was there that she met Ravindra, a resident of Pacherikalan village in Rajasthan's Jhunjhunu district. They became friends after talking to each other. Their friendship then turned into an affair, which continued for two years. When they told their families about their relationship, Ravindra's family agreed, but Nazia's family did not agree to the marriage. Marriage four months ago When Nazia's family refused to accept the relationship, she left home four months ago. She then married Ravindra. For three months, Nazia's family kept asking her to sever ties with him, but she refused. After this, her family pretended to accept the relationship. On 25 September, Nazia's mother and maternal aunt somehow lured her to Mathura by engaging her in conversation. After she stayed there for a few days and said she wanted to return, her family began opposing her. Husband grew suspicious when Nazia did not return even after 15 days When Nazia did not return even 15 days after going to her parents' home, her husband grew suspicious. He then called Nazia's family members. At first, they kept evading him. Later, they stopped answering his calls. Ravindra then began fearing that something untoward had happened. Ravindra lodged an FIR alleging that his wife had been kidnapped in Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan. On 23 October, Rajasthan Police sent an email to Mathura Police to register the FIR and investigate the case. Police questioned her brother The investigation was handed over to the Govind Nagar police station. When the police questioned the family, they continued to give evasive answers. On the basis of suspicion, the police took the girl's brother, Akram, into custody late on Saturday night. The police then questioned him about how his sister had died. Initially, he said that she had died of electrocution. But when the police applied pressure, he told them that he had strangled his sister to death and buried her body in the cemetery after the murder. Body exhumed on City Magistrate's orders The police then arrested Akram and informed senior officials about the case. Following this, the cemetery was dug up on Sunday on the orders of City Magistrate Anupam Mishra. Nazia's body was exhumed and sent for a post-mortem examination. Akram was also arrested. The police are now waiting for the post-mortem report. SP says investigation report awaited SP City Rajiv Kumar Singh said the matter had come to his notice. The young woman's body was exhumed from the cemetery and sent for a post-mortem examination. The incident is being investigated. As the investigation is still under way, it would be premature to say anything about it.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi acquitted in Shah defamation case after 8 years:Judge delivers verdict in 16 minutes; 3 reasons behind court’s decision
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has been acquitted by the MP-MLA court in the defamation case linked to Amit Shah. Rahul was present in court when the verdict was delivered. He appeared before the MP/MLA court in Sultanpur in an eight-year-old defamation case related to his remarks about Union Home Minister Amit Shah. During the previous hearing, Rahul Gandhi's legal team had submitted written arguments. The Congress MP had admitted that he made the remarks against Amit Shah in 2018 in good faith. He said his intention was not to defame anyone. The case was related to remarks Rahul Gandhi made about Amit Shah in Bengaluru in 2018. During the previous hearing, Santosh Pandey, the lawyer for complainant Vijay Mishra, had said that Rahul Gandhi had accepted the incident and his speech. He urged the court to find Rahul Gandhi guilty. According to Congress district president Abhishek Singh Rana, Congress workers from the Kurebhar, Dhanpatganj and Jaisinghpur blocks will welcome Rahul Gandhi at 9:30 am after he enters the area from the Purvanchal Expressway. At 9:40 am, workers from the Kadipur, Akhandnagar, Karaundikala, Motigarpur and Dostpur blocks will welcome him at the Tatiya Nagar bypass. At 9:45 am, Congress workers from the PP Kamicha, Lambhua and Bhadainya blocks will be present at Tedhui intersection to welcome him. At 9:55 am, teams from the Youth Congress and the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) will welcome him in front of Aastha Hospital in Golaghat. At 10 am, workers from the Baldirai, Kudwar and Dubepur blocks will welcome him at the Golaghat Diwani turn. Members of the City Congress Committee and other local leaders will welcome him at the gate of the District Court. Convoy collides in Sultanpur Earlier on Monday morning, vehicles in Rahul Gandhi’s convoy collided on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur. Five vehicles travelling behind the convoy and an ambulance were involved in the accident. Some people sustained minor injuries. Rahul Gandhi was travelling to Sultanpur to appear before the MP/MLA court. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) will now investigate the accident. The Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) has formed the SIT. The SIT comprises three officers and will be headed by Lucknow Range IG Kiran S. Sultanpur ASP Brij Narayan Singh and DSP (Traffic) Ram Krishna Chaturvedi will also be part of the investigation. The SIT will investigate the exact cause of the accident and examine any lapses in security or traffic management. It will also recommend measures to prevent such incidents in the future and submit its report to police headquarters as soon as possible. In this eight-year-old defamation case, Rahul had admitted that he made a statement against Amit Shah in 2018 in good faith. He said his intention was not to defame anyone. Vijay Mishra, a BJP leader from Sultanpur, filed the case against Rahul in August 2018. The allegation is that Rahul made the statement during a press conference in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on 8 May 2018: “The president of a party that talks about honesty is accused of murder.” Welcome to be held at different locations According to Congress district president Abhishek Singh Rana, Congress workers from Kurebhar, Dhanpatganj and Jaisinghpur blocks will welcome Rahul Gandhi at 9:30 a.m. after he gets off the Purvanchal Expressway. At 9:40 a.m., workers from the Kadipur, Akhandnagar, Karaundikala, Motigarpur and Dostpur blocks will welcome him at the Tatiya Nagar bypass. At 9:45 a.m., Congress workers from PP Kameicha, Lambhua and Bhadaiya will be present at Tedhui Tiraha. At 9:55 a.m., the Youth Congress and NSUI teams will welcome him outside Aastha Hospital in Golaghat. At 10 a.m., workers from the Baldirai, Kudwar and Dubeypur blocks will welcome him at Golaghat's Diwani Mod. The City Congress Committee and other local leaders will welcome him at the gate of the civil court. Case against Rahul was filed in 2018 BJP leader Vijay Mishra from Sultanpur filed a defamation case against Rahul Gandhi in the MP/MLA court in August 2018. Mishra said, "On 8 May 2018, Rahul held a press conference in Bengaluru, Karnataka. The Congress leader had said, 'Amit Shah is an accused in a murder case.' The Supreme Court mentioned this in the Judge Loya case. Therefore, I do not believe that Amit Shah has any credibility. The president of a party that speaks of honesty and probity is an accused in a murder case." During the 2018 Karnataka Assembly election, Rahul Gandhi allegedly made the comment about Amit Shah, who was the BJP president at the time, at a rally in Bengaluru. Rahul Gandhi is alleged to have said that the BJP spoke of honest politics, but its president was an accused in a murder case. Amit Shah's name was linked to the 2005 alleged fake encounter case involving Sohrabuddin Sheikh. However, in 2014, a special CBI court in Mumbai discharged him from the charges in the case. When did Rahul Gandhi appear for the first time? The MP/MLA court in Sultanpur summoned Rahul Gandhi in the case on 27 November 2023. Rahul Gandhi subsequently appeared in court on 20 February 2024 and secured bail. Two sureties of ₹25,000 each were furnished for this. Rahul Gandhi's statement in the case was recorded in court on 26 July 2024. During this, he presented his side regarding the allegations against him. Demand for voice sample comparison rejected A CD was submitted to the court on behalf of complainant Vijay Mishra. A request was made to have the voice recorded on it matched with Rahul Gandhi's voice sample through the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL). The trial court rejected the application on 2 May. After this, the complainant's side filed an application in the Sessions Court. The Sessions Court also rejected it on 15 July. The decision was then challenged in the High Court. In September, it came to light that a petition related to matching the voice sample had been filed. Following this, proceedings in the final arguments in the case moved forward. Two sections invoked against Rahul A case has been registered against Rahul Gandhi under Sections 499 and 500 in this matter. Section 499 deals with spreading false rumours about someone, making comments about them and defaming them. Section 500 provides for punishment for defamation. Rahul could face up to two years in prison in this case. Rahul's Parliament membership was cancelled in a defamation case Rahul Gandhi's membership of Parliament was cancelled on 24 March 2023. The Surat court sentenced him to two years in prison in a defamation case. Rahul was then the MP from Wayanad. However, his membership was later restored after his sentence was suspended. Read what the Justice Loya case was about... Justice Loya's son had described his father's death as natural. The Supreme Court had also termed it a normal death and dismissed the petition seeking an SIT investigation into the matter. Justice Brijmohan Harikishan Loya died in Nagpur in December 2014. At the time, he had gone to attend the wedding of his colleague's daughter. Judge Loya was hearing the much-discussed Sohrabuddin Sheikh encounter case in Gujarat, in which Amit Shah was an accused.

stories.title: FIR against SP leader for construction in Dalmandi:Work continued despite court stay, complaint over installing shutter, and threats
stories.summary: Despite a court order restraining construction, work is alleged to have been carried out on a house in Varanasi's Dalmandi. Chauk police have registered a case against two people, including Samajwadi Party leader Imran Ahmed Bablu, in connection with the matter. Mohammad Wasim, the owner of the house, has alleged that the old shutter of the disputed property was removed and replaced with a new one. He was also allegedly threatened with death when he objected. According to Wasim's complaint, the court has barred any change to the condition of the house or any new construction. Despite this, construction was allegedly carried out again on the night of 22 October. Police are investigating the matter. Dispute over ownership of half the house According to Chauk police station in-charge Vijay Kumar Shukla, Mohammad Wasim owns half of a house in Chahmama, Dalmandi. A case concerning ownership of the house is pending in court. The court has ordered that no changes be made to the house until the dispute is decided. Waseem alleges that despite the court's order, Samajwadi Party leaders Imran Ahmed Bablu and Sawab Ahmed removed the old shutter and installed a new one in the remaining part of the house. They then locked the shutter and took possession of the portion. Accused of threatening to kill him when he objected According to Waseem, the Public Works Department (PWD) had marked a red line near the house. It is alleged that the old shutter installed next to it was removed and replaced with a new one. Waseem said this portion had remained after part of the house was demolished during earlier action. He said he had filed a complaint through Dial 112 and at Chowk police station on 20 September. It is alleged that when he objected to the construction, the accused threatened to kill him. Accused of resuming construction on the night of 22 October Waseem alleged that construction was resumed on the night of 22 October. During this, bamboo poles and supports were put up, and two new shutters were installed in place of one. On the victim's written complaint, Chowk police registered an FIR against Samajwadi Party leader Imran Ahmed Bablu and Sawab Ahmed. Police said the case is being investigated.

stories.title: Woman killed after being hit by motorcycle in Gorakhpur:Attacked while returning from an engagement ceremony with husband; hunt on for 2 suspects
stories.summary: Two motorcycle-borne criminals attacked a couple travelling on a motorcycle beyond Bharwal village in Gorakhpur's Belipar police station area on Saturday night. The wife, who was riding pillion, fell from the motorcycle after the criminals rammed into it and died. On the basis of the husband's complaint, police have registered a murder case against the two motorcycle-borne criminals and begun an investigation. Raids are being conducted to trace the accused. Suddenly pushed, woman fell on the road Santosh Pandey, a resident of Malaon village in Belipar, had gone to a marriage hall in Gorakhpur on Saturday with his wife, Meera Pandey (54), to attend the engagement ceremony of a young woman from her maternal family. At around 10 p.m., the couple were returning to their village by motorcycle when two unidentified men riding a racing motorcycle approached them from behind. They had just crossed Bharwal village when, it is alleged, the motorcycle-borne men pushed his wife. Meera fell on the road and sustained serious injuries. Immediately after the incident, Santosh telephoned his cousin, who lives in the village, and informed him. The cousin then reached the scene. The family took Meera to Gorakhpur District Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Based on the written complaint, police registered a case against two unidentified people. The identification of the accused and the reasons behind the incident are being investigated. Meera was the mother of three daughters The family is in mourning following the death of 54-year-old Meera. She had three daughters, two of whom are married. Her youngest daughter, Shweta, lives in Gurugram. After receiving news of their mother's death, family members are waiting for her to arrive. South SP Dinesh Puri said a case has been registered on the basis of the husband's written complaint. The reason for the incident will become clear once the assailants are arrested.

stories.title: ‘Thank God Ram did not kill a minority’:UP Election Commission hits back at Sanjay Singh; says software isn't casteist
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Election Commission said the voter list for the recent Legislative Council (MLC) election also contained the unusual name 'Ram killed Sharma'. The commission said that computers and software are not casteist and admitted that a mistake had occurred. The commission said, "There is also a strange name in the MLC election voter list: 'Ram ne Sharma ko maara' (Ram beat Sharma). Computers or software are not casteist. We accept that a mistake was made, but fortunately, there was no caste discrimination even when the mistake occurred." (Thank God, Ram did not beat a minority person. Otherwise, along with being accused of caste discrimination, we would also have been accused of communal bias.) The response came after AAP Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh questioned why the voter list included the name "Ram ne Yadav ko maara" (Ram beat Yadav). Sharing a video of a man named Rajesh Yadav on X, Singh asked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, "Why did Ram beat only Yadav? Why did Ram not beat someone named Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai or Bisht? Is your computer deeply casteist? Are you carrying out the agenda of a political party?" Election Commission had earlier clarified the name errors On October 22, the Election Commission had issued a clarification regarding the errors in the voter list. In a post on X, it said that the process of adding names to the voter list for the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) elections had been carried out online for the first time. As a result, some errors occurred in certain places. Out of 14.81 lakh names on the voter list, only 158 appeared unusual when read. The commission explained that the computer was supposed to transliterate English names into Hindi, but instead, it translated their meaning. For example, a person's name was 'Ramhit Yadav'. While typing, the spelling became 'Ram hit Yadav', and the computer translated it into Hindi as 'Ram ne Yadav ko maara' (Ram beat Yadav). Complaints of errors in voter list received Before the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) elections, complaints of errors in the voter list had surfaced. Some names and addresses were so unusual that readers were left shocked. In some cases, a voter's name was listed as 'Takkar Marna' (to hit), while another entry showed the father's name as 'Ram ne Sharma ko maara' (Ram beat Sharma). Claims also circulated on social media that dozens of names in the voter list for the Allahabad-Jhansi graduate constituency were fake. Dainik Bhaskar investigated these claims by checking the viral lists against the MLC voter lists of the respective districts. The check revealed some surprising details. Names claimed to be fake Part number 73 (serial number 420): Name – Ram ne Maara Yadav Ko; Father's name – Phool Chandra Yadav Part number 69 (serial number 351): Name – Takkar Marna; Father's name – Takkar Marna Part number 133 (serial number 768): Name – Ravi Sharma; Father's name – Ram ne Sharma ko Maara Part number 189 (serial number 1034): Name – Moorkh Kali Devi; Father's name – Ramjeet Patel Part number 15 (serial number 82): Name – Mohammad Pagal Rehan; Father's name – Mohammad Hashim Part number 81 (serial number 696): Name – Narendra Yadav; Father's name – B.Com To verify the viral claims, the updated voter lists for the Jhansi and Prayagraj (Allahabad) areas were checked. One error found in Jhansi voter list The viral list claimed that a voter named 'Khalid Ali ne Kaha' was listed at part number 252, serial number 566, in Jhansi. However, when the official list updated in December 2025 was checked on the Election Commission's website, that part contained only 537 voters. This means there was no entry at serial number 566. However, a major error was found in the name listed at part number 133, serial number 768.

stories.title: Fake captain caught at Varanasi air show:Was roaming in the restricted helipad area of Namo Ghat; intelligence agencies questioned him
stories.summary: A fake captain was caught in the helipad area of Namo Ghat in Varanasi ahead of an air show. He was roaming in the restricted area while claiming to be an Army captain. Security personnel caught him after becoming suspicious. His posting as a captain in the Army could not be confirmed, after which he was handed over to the police. The युवक was identified as Arpit Chaturvedi. Intelligence agencies questioned him for hours. The police registered a named FIR against him. Roaming in highly sensitive helipad area Security arrangements had been tightened in Varanasi in view of the Air Force air show scheduled for Sunday. Despite this, a युवक reached the restricted area of the helipad at Namo Ghat on Saturday. The personnel deployed on duty found his activities suspicious. During questioning, he claimed to be an Army captain. His answers and demeanour increased the personnel's suspicion. The authorities and local police were subsequently informed. After receiving the information, police and administrative officials, along with officers from the Intelligence Bureau (IB), the Local Intelligence Unit (LIU) and the Air Force, reached the spot. The youth was taken into custody and questioning began. No evidence of posting as captain found in army records Given the sensitivity of the matter, the youth was taken to the office of a senior officer of the Varanasi Police Commissionerate. There, intelligence units of the IB, LIU and Air Force questioned him for several hours. During the initial questioning, he identified himself as Captain Arpit. He gave his address as being near the PWD Colony in Jadid Bazar, under the jurisdiction of Cantt police station. However, checks of Army records and the address he provided did not confirm that he was a captain. After the investigation, he was identified as Arpit Chaturvedi. According to officials, he is originally from Varanasi's Nadesar area. Father runs a pathology centre According to the DCP of Kashi, Arpit's father runs a pathology centre in the city. An investigation is under way into why the young man claimed to be an army officer and how he reached the restricted helipad area. Security and intelligence agencies are also gathering information related to the case. A named FIR has been registered against Arpit Chaturvedi at Adampur police station on the complaint of Chandan Kumar, in-charge of the Namoghat police outpost. The police have taken action against him and filed a charge sheet.

Commandos descended from a helicopter onto a cruise ship at Namo Ghat using ropes. Within moments, they climbed back onto the helicopter. Namo Ghat echoed with the roar of 52 fighter jets, including the Rafale and Sukhoi. People applauded as the Sukhoi performed aerial manoeuvres. The fighter jets made sudden turns in the sky, sometimes swooping towards the ground before abruptly climbing and performing loops. A total of 100 aircraft participated in the air show. These included 15 transport aircraft, 32 helicopters and the vintage aircraft Sarnath. The aircraft took off from 12 airbases across the country to perform aerial manoeuvres in the skies over Kashi. Large crowds gathered to watch the show. Foreign tourists said they thoroughly enjoyed the aircraft displays. October 25 will be the third and final day of the air show. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will also visit Kashi on the occasion. The event is being organised to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force. Two pictures of the aircraft displays…

stories.title: Chandrashekhar-Owaisi alliance in UP almost finalised:Aims to cover 40% Dalit-Muslim population; Chandrashekhar wants to break Mayawati’s record
stories.summary: A new political alliance could be announced in Uttar Pradesh on Constitution Day. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekhar Azad may announce the alliance at Lucknow’s Ramabai Maidan. Under the proposed arrangement, Owaisi’s party will contest 40 to 45 seats in Uttar Pradesh, while Chandrashekhar’s party will contest the remaining seats. Both parties aim to build a Dalit-Muslim political combination in the state. Dalits account for around 21% of Uttar Pradesh’s population, while Muslims make up approximately 19%. If the alliance takes shape, it will seek to consolidate support among communities that together account for nearly 40% of the population. How much electoral influence can the Owaisi-Chandrashekhar alliance gain? How effectively can the Owaisi-Chandrashekhar partnership consolidate Dalit and Muslim support? How many seats in Uttar Pradesh could the alliance influence, and which parties stand to gain or lose from the potential political realignment? Read the full report… Chandrashekhar Azad plans major show of strength in Lucknow on November 26 The Azad Samaj Party and Bhim Army are preparing for a major show of strength at Lucknow’s Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan on November 26. Chandrashekhar Azad has named the event the ‘Save the Constitution Mega Public Meeting’. He has booked the venue for three days. The ground has a capacity of around five lakh people, and Mayawati is so far the only leader to have filled it during a public meeting. Chandrashekhar aims to position his party as an alternative to BSP Chandrashekhar wants to match that record and send a message to Dalit voters that his Azad Samaj Party is now ready to emerge as an alternative to the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). To achieve this, the party is preparing to mobilise supporters from across Uttar Pradesh. Assembly in-charges appointed by the party have also been tasked with bringing crowds to the rally. Each has been asked to mobilise between 1,000 and 1,500 people from their respective Assembly constituencies. 87 Assembly in-charges announced, with more rallies across UP Chandrashekhar has announced the names of 87 Assembly in-charges in two lists so far. Following the BSP’s model, the Azad Samaj Party has appointed Assembly in-charges who are subsequently declared candidates during elections. Over the past three months, Chandrashekhar has addressed more than 12 public meetings and rallies across Uttar Pradesh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has been his main target in these speeches. Four rounds of talks held over alliance with Owaisi’s AIMIM AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali, responding to questions about an alliance with Chandrashekhar’s party, said, “We are preparing to contest all 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. Which party we will ally with and how many seats AIMIM will contest will be decided by our party leader, Asaduddin Owaisi.” However, he did not deny reports of a possible alliance with Chandrashekhar’s party. According to sources associated with the party, Shaukat Ali and Chandrashekhar have held four rounds of talks on the alliance. Chandrashekhar has also spoken to Owaisi about the matter. The two parties are reportedly at odds over Muslim-dominated constituencies, with both seeking a larger share of these seats. Owaisi’s party wants to contest 40 Muslim-dominated Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. All eight public meetings Owaisi has held in the state so far have been in Muslim-dominated areas, drawing large crowds, particularly young Muslims. In his speeches, Owaisi has frequently targeted the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress. He argues that Muslim youth are no less capable than others but are not given opportunities to advance in politics. Chandrashekhar aims to finalise alliance before November 25 Chandrashekhar is trying to resolve the remaining differences over the alliance before November 25. He wants to announce the alliance at a public meeting scheduled to be held at Lucknow’s Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan. A leader associated with the party claimed that preparations were also underway to invite Owaisi to the rally. However, AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali said the Azad Samaj Party had not yet sent any formal invitation. Muslim voters will back whoever can defeat the BJP, says political analyst Zaigham Murtaza, a political analyst who closely follows western Uttar Pradesh politics said, “Chandrashekhar has a stronger influence among young Dalit voters, particularly those under 40.” He added, “Owaisi enjoys a similar appeal among young Muslims. In the 2022 Assembly elections, AIMIM fielded candidates in 95 constituencies, but they failed to secure even 0.50% of the total votes.” He stated, “This shows that while Owaisi's rallies draw large crowds, the support does not necessarily translate into votes. Muslims are likely to back Owaisi or Chandrashekhar's party only if they believe their candidates have a realistic chance of defeating the BJP.” He further said, “A significant section of Dalits, particularly young voters, could support Chandrashekhar's party, potentially improving its vote share.” Murtaza expects that an alliance between the two parties could bring Dalit and Muslim voters together in some constituencies, provided they field strong candidates. A large section of Muslim voters may support the alliance if it appears capable of challenging the BJP. Otherwise, Murtaza believes, the alliance is unlikely to secure the support of more than 20% of the Muslim population. Meanwhile, senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana also supports Murtaza's assessment. He said, “Owaisi is highly popular among Muslims, particularly young people, who may vote for him. However, the bigger challenge is winning over the majority of Muslim voters.” He added, “Many believe that only the SP-Congress alliance can unseat the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh and that no other alliance has the strength to do so.” Chandrashekhar-Owaisi alliance could alter three political equations: 1. SP and BSP could lose support: The Samajwadi Party's core support base has traditionally included Muslims and Yadavs, while the Bahujan Samaj Party relies on Dalit voters. An alliance between Chandrashekhar and Owaisi could divide Dalit and Muslim votes, eating into the opposition's secular vote base. 2. BJP could benefit from vote division: A split in Dalit and Muslim votes, along with voter polarisation, could give the BJP a significant advantage in several constituencies. 3. Chandrashekhar and Owaisi could emerge as a third front: If the alliance secures even 5–6% of the vote, it could establish itself as a significant third front in Uttar Pradesh politics. Alliance could hurt SP and BSP in constituencies with large Dalit-Muslim populations Uttar Pradesh has 41 Assembly constituencies where Dalit and Muslim voters together account for more than 50% of the electorate. In these seats, the two communities have the potential to play a decisive role in election outcomes. Another 62 constituencies have Muslim voter shares ranging from 25% to 70%, while Dalit voters account for 30% to 42% of the electorate in 39 constituencies. Senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana said, “The SP and BSP stand to lose the most if Chandrashekhar and Owaisi join hands. Chandrashekhar is drawing support from Dalits, a core BSP constituency, while Owaisi's party could influence Muslim voters who form a key part of the SP's Muslim-Yadav (M-Y) support base.” Senior journalist Zaigham Murtaza further added, “The alliance could lead to triangular contests in constituencies with large Dalit and Muslim populations. In such seats, the BJP could benefit the most, as a division of votes could improve its chances of winning.” Muslim voters could play a decisive role in reserved constituencies Several of Uttar Pradesh’s 84 reserved Assembly seats have sizeable Muslim electorates that can influence election outcomes. In constituencies such as Nagina, Purkazi, Dhanaura and Nehtaur, candidates may belong to the Dalit community, but the results can hinge on the voting preferences of Muslim voters, who account for 35–40% of the electorate. Like Mayawati, Chandrashekhar belongs to the Jatav community. Bihar experiment offers clues to alliance’s prospects in Uttar Pradesh The alliance took shape before Uttar Pradesh, during the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections. It fielded candidates in 64 of the state’s 243 constituencies. AIMIM contested 35 seats, Chandrashekhar’s party fielded candidates in 25, and Swami Prasad Maurya’s Janata Party contested four. Five of Owaisi’s candidates won in the Muslim-dominated Seemanchal region, giving the alliance a total of five seats. Senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana believes the alliance could have a much greater impact in Uttar Pradesh. One reason, he says, is that Chandrashekhar has built a stronger political base in UP than in Bihar. Chandrashekhar himself hails from western Uttar Pradesh and is the MP from Nagina, where more than 60% of voters are Muslim. Western UP also has the highest concentration of Muslim-dominated constituencies. In this context, Rana says, even securing 5–6% of the vote through a Chandrashekhar-Owaisi alliance would be a significant achievement.

stories.title: Amit Shah heads to Lucknow to counter Rahul-Akhilesh:Seat-sharing with allies a major challenge; what is BJP’s strategy for 2027?
stories.summary: Amit Shah has followed a set strategy for assembly elections. He becomes active in a state four to six months before the polls and turns the tide in the BJP’s favour. Haryana, Maharashtra, Bihar and, most recently, West Bengal are examples. The Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections are around four months away. The Rahul-Akhilesh combine has made the contest tougher. Shah is now visiting Lucknow on October 30–31. So, how will Amit Shah counter this alliance? And how will he find a way to accommodate alliance partners? Today, we will decode these questions in the UP Explainer. Question 1: How will Amit Shah counter the SP-Congress alliance? Answer: Amit Shah could adopt four strategies to counter the opposition alliance. I) Exploiting the rift between the SP and Congress Although the SP and Congress appear united publicly, a tussle over seat-sharing has already begun. The Congress is demanding 140 seats, of which around 75 are non-negotiable, meaning it wants to contest these seats under any circumstances. The SP, meanwhile, insists that seat allocation should be based on ground realities. A similar situation arose in Haryana and Madhya Pradesh. In Haryana, the Congress sidelined the AAP, while in Madhya Pradesh, it sidelined the SP. Amit Shah shaped the narrative that parties fighting over every seat before the election would threaten to topple the government every day if they came to power. Only the BJP, he argued, could provide a strong and stable government. In Bihar, where the Congress formed an alliance with the RJD, Shah adopted a different strategy. He allegedly supported a rebel candidate or a leader from a third party behind the scenes against a strong alliance candidate, turning the contest into a triangular fight. When senior leaders force an alliance, grassroots workers who have fought against each other for years often struggle to work together. Shah could exploit this divide and use the BJP’s panna pramukhs (page-level booth workers) to mobilise voters and bring them to polling booths. II) A caste-based counter to Akhilesh’s PDA formula Akhilesh Yadav’s strategy centres on uniting the PDA vote bank: Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities). Amit Shah is likely to counter this by focusing on non-Yadav OBCs and non-Jatav Dalits. The BJP will seek to convey that an SP government would increase the dominance of a particular social group, especially Yadavs and Muslims. Shah’s strategy will be to reassure non-Yadav backward communities such as Kurmis, Mauryas, Shakyas, Sainis, Nishads and Rajbhars that their interests and dignity are best protected under the BJP. III) Implementing the 2017 ‘win the booth’ formula Amit Shah believes that regardless of what political leaders say in their speeches, elections are won by workers deployed at polling booths. This approach is reflected in his micro-management strategy. The party will directly engage with booth presidents and Shakti Kendra coordinators to strengthen weak areas of the organisation. The panna pramukh committees at every booth could be restructured to reflect the new political equations. The aim would be to ensure that before SP-Congress supporters reach polling booths, BJP’s page-level workers have already mobilised voters from 10–15 families. The party will try to maintain this lead until polling ends. IV) ‘Muslim appeasement’ versus law and order The SP-Congress alliance’s biggest strength is the consolidation of Muslim votes in its favour. Amit Shah is likely to counter this by making nationalism, the Ram temple and the Yogi government’s strict law-and-order policy central election issues. The campaign is likely to emphasise that if the SP-Congress alliance comes to power, Uttar Pradesh could return to an era of Goonda Raj (rule by criminals) and appeasement politics. This narrative would seek to unite Hindu voters across caste lines and consolidate their support for the BJP. Question 2: How will Shah manage MLAs who are upset after being denied tickets? Answer: The BJP could deny tickets to around 40% of its sitting MLAs this time. This could lead to more rebellion and internal sabotage, but Amit Shah is skilled at managing such situations. He mainly relies on three strategies. I) Offering positions in Delhi and Lucknow in advance Amit Shah assures MLAs that losing a ticket does not mean the end of their political careers. Uttar Pradesh has dozens of government corporations, commissions and boards whose chairpersons enjoy cabinet or minister-of-state rank. Shah could assure disgruntled leaders that they would be accommodated in these positions if the government returns to power. Leaders with a strong political base who are capable of contesting elections but lose their tickets due to local political equations could be promised seats in the Legislative Council or Rajya Sabha. Others may be appointed as organisational vice-presidents, general secretaries or in-charges of other states to protect their standing and prestige. II) Amit Shah’s one-to-one counselling Amit Shah’s biggest strength is his direct and candid communication. He personally meets leaders upset over being denied tickets and presents them with survey reports from the Intelligence Bureau (IB), private agencies, and the party organisation. Shah explains that the party has a larger goal. If the BJP loses that seat, the opposition will grow stronger. This combination of emotional appeal and political pressure often works. III) Assigning responsibility for the new candidate’s victory In some cases, Shah denies a sitting MLA a ticket and instead makes that leader responsible for ensuring the new candidate’s victory. The leader is tasked with winning the seat for the new candidate and told that doing so would demonstrate their influence and could earn them a bigger reward. Overall, Amit Shah follows a straightforward principle: “Either compromise with dignity or be prepared for political isolation.” Using this strategy, he has managed to prevent rebellion even after dropping sitting MLAs in states such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Haryana. Question 3: How will he persuade alliance partners to agree to seat-sharing arrangements? Answer: This is another major challenge. Alliance partners are demanding more seats to expand their political strength, while the BJP wants to limit their share to 50–60 seats. Amit Shah has consistently used two formulas to manage pressure over seat-sharing. I) BJP symbol, alliance partner as the candidate This is one of Amit Shah’s oldest and most reliable tactics. When an alliance partner insists on contesting a seat where the BJP has a strong support base, Shah fields the alliance partner’s leader on the BJP symbol. The same formula helped seal the deal with the Nishad Party in the 2022 elections. At the time, six Nishad Party leaders contested on the BJP symbol, and five of them won. Sanjay Nishad’s son, Sarvan Nishad, also won the Chauri Chaura seat in Gorakhpur on the BJP symbol. Meanwhile, the Nishad Party contested 10 seats on its own symbol, a plate filled with food. II) Calculating strike rate and vote transfer Shah allocates seats based on past performance. He reminds alliance partners that the BJP’s committed cadre votes are also transferred to them, making victory easier. Winning 35 out of 45 seats is better than winning just 20 out of 100. In politics, this is known as improving the ‘strike rate’. Question 4: What strategy could be used to counter anti-incumbency in UP? Answer: When a government remains in power for a long time, public resentment can grow over local MLAs, officials, and certain government decisions. This is known as anti-incumbency. The BJP has been in power in UP for 10 years. In this situation, these three points will be crucial. I) Dropping a large number of sitting MLAs Anti-incumbency usually affects local MLAs more than the Chief Minister. People become unhappy when their MLA fails to deliver or does not visit the constituency. This time, the BJP could drop 40% of its sitting MLAs from the candidate list. II) A new, silent vote bank of beneficiaries Amit Shah goes a step beyond caste politics and focuses on ‘beneficiary politics’. In UP, crores of families have benefited from central and state government schemes such as free ration, the PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala LPG connections, Ayushman cards and the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi. Shah assigns party workers the task of visiting these beneficiaries door to door and reminding them that the assistance came from the Modi-Yogi governments. III) Using national issues to overshadow local concerns If the election is fought on issues such as drains, paved roads and unemployment, the BJP could suffer losses. Amit Shah, however, changes the election narrative completely. The campaign is shifted towards nationalism, the Ram temple, development in Kashi and Mathura, and strict law and order. When the debate centres on goonda raj and Muslim appeasement, voters may set aside smaller local problems and rally behind the BJP.

stories.title: Hema Malini, 78, dances for 90 minutes as Maa Ganga:Descends onto stage on a crane, depicts Ganga’s arrival on Earth
stories.summary: The 2026 Braj Raj Utsav began in Mathura on Friday with MP and actress Hema Malini's dance-drama 'Ganga'. Hema Malini, 78, played Mother Ganga in the performance. She danced and acted on stage for around one and a half hours. The performance depicted Ganga's journey from her descent to Earth to the present day. It also highlighted the river's rising pollution and conveyed the message that Ganga must be saved. Hema Malini wore a white sari and jewellery during the performance. Her expressions and gestures during the dance were a sight to behold. The other artists also portrayed the river's deteriorating condition. See the pictures... Journey through four eras depicted The programme began with the guests lighting ceremonial lamps. This was followed by a dance drama depicting King Bhagirath's penance. He had resolved to bring the Ganga to Earth to liberate his ancestors. Lord Shiva then caught the Ganga's powerful flow in his matted locks. The dance drama presented the story of the Ganga from the Satya Yuga to the Kali Yuga. It portrayed, through dance and acting, the changes that took place in society in different eras and people's relationship with the Ganga. Episodes from mythology, Indian history and culture were also shown. The suffering of the Ganga, distressed by pollution, was depicted Through a dance drama, Hema Malini highlighted that the river regarded as a source of life and salvation is now on the verge of dying because of neglect and pollution. She delivered a message to keep the Ganga, Yamuna and other rivers clean and protect natural heritage. As part of the Braj Raj Utsav, cultural programmes are being held this year at Vrindavan's newly built Swami Haridas auditorium as well. Other activities of the festival will begin on 24 October at the Railway Ground in Dhauli Pyau, Mathura.

stories.title: Baghpat ASP apologises with folded hands to BJP district chief:CO also says sorry after he was removed from polling booth
stories.summary: Chaos broke out during the final 10 minutes of polling for the Teacher MLC election at Khekra block in Baghpat. BJP workers accused the Circle Officer of misbehaving with them and forcing them out of the polling station. On receiving the information, MLA Yogesh Dhama reached the spot. Angry, he sat on a protest inside the block premises. At around 5 p.m. on Friday, Circle Officer Rohan Chaurasia reached the block premises and apologised to BJP district president Neeraj Sharma. He said, "Sorry sir, I made a mistake." The ASP also apologised with folded hands. The matter was settled after this. Former block chief Devendra Gurjar said the Circle Officer had failed to recognise BJP district president Neeraj Sharma. This led to a heated exchange between the two. After reports that Neeraj Sharma had been manhandled, a large number of people reached the block premises. Read the entire sequence of events... Polling for the teachers' MLC election was under way at Khekra block. At around 3:30 p.m., Khekra Circle Officer Rohan Chaurasia asked BJP worker Naveen Sharma, who was present at the polling station, to leave. An argument broke out between the two. Naveen immediately called district president Neeraj Sharma, who was outside the polling station. As soon as Neeraj Sharma arrived, he had a heated exchange with the CO. The CO also asked him to leave the polling station. Neeraj Sharma then called the MLA and other workers and informed them about the incident. MLA sits on protest with party workers MLA Yogesh Dhama reached the block premises with party workers and sat on a protest after placing chairs there. On receiving the information, ASP Praveen Singh Chauhan and Baghpat CO Sukanya Sharma also reached the spot. For around one hour, the officers tried to persuade the MLA and the workers to end the protest, but they remained firm on their demand for a public apology. At around 5 p.m., CO Rohan Chaurasia reached the block premises. Accepting his mistake, he told the BJP district president, "Sorry sir, I made a mistake." After this, the ASP also apologised with folded hands. The matter was resolved after the officers apologised. SP said-BJP was trying to get bogus votes cast SP spokesperson Jitendra Yadav alleged that BJP workers had been trying to get bogus votes cast since morning. When the CO stopped them in the evening, a dispute broke out over this. He also accused the BJP workers of acting dictatorially.

stories.title: UP TGT recruitment announced for 17,735 posts:Applications open from October 24, exams on December 23–24
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission (UPESSC) has released the recruitment notification for trained graduate teachers (TGTs) in the state's secondary schools. Under the recruitment drive, 17,735 vacant assistant teacher posts will be filled. The online application process will begin on 24 October. Candidates will be able to pay the application fee until 23 November, while the deadline for making corrections to the application form has been set as 26 November. According to the commission, the total includes 16,193 posts in boys' schools and 1,542 posts in girls' schools. The written examination will be held on 23 and 24 December. Selection will be made from a merit list prepared on the basis of an objective written examination carrying 360 marks. Applications must be submitted through OTR Candidates must visit the Commission's official website www.upessc.up.gov.in to submit their applications. One-Time Registration (OTR) has been made mandatory for applying. According to the Commission's instructions, the registration and application form must be completed in English. The application fee has been fixed at ₹1,000 for candidates belonging to the General, Other Backward Classes (OBC) and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) categories. Candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) will have to pay ₹500, while candidates with disabilities will have to pay a fee of ₹300. Candidates aged 21 to 62 years will be eligible to apply The minimum age for recruitment must be 21 years as on 1 July 2026. The maximum age limit has been set at 62 years. Selected candidates will receive a pay scale of ₹44,900 to ₹142,400 under Pay Matrix Level 7. For the educational qualification, candidates must hold a graduate degree in the relevant subject with a minimum of 50% marks or a postgraduate degree with 45% marks. They must also have a B.Ed. from an institution recognised by the NCTE. For physical education, the required qualification is B.P.Ed./B.P.E. Candidates must also have passed the Upper Primary-level Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Government or the Central Government. 120 questions, examination to be completed in two hours The written examination will carry a total of 360 marks. It will consist of 120 multiple-choice questions, and candidates will have two hours to complete it. There will be 30 questions on general knowledge and 90 on the relevant subject. Each correct answer will carry three marks, while one mark will be deducted for each incorrect answer. Hindi has the highest number of posts at 2,791 Among the subject-wise vacancies, Hindi has the highest number of posts, at 2,791. There are 2,517 posts in English, 2,482 in social science, 2,493 in science and 2,349 in mathematics. In addition, 1,289 posts have been earmarked for Sanskrit, 849 for physical education, 798 for home science, 775 for fine arts and 660 for biology. Candidates can find detailed recruitment guidelines, the subject-wise syllabus and the prescribed certificate formats on the commission's official website. Commission Deputy Secretary Sanjay Kumar Singh said that, according to the important dates related to the recruitment examination, the was published on 23 October. The online registration and application process will begin on 24 October. The deadline for candidates to pay the online application fee is 23 November. If there is any error in the application form, it can be corrected until 26 November. The recruitment examination will be held on the scheduled dates of 23 and 24 December.

stories.title: Wife flags officer husband’s crores-worth property:Claims he leads a lavish life and drives a 0007-number Thar; minister orders investigation
stories.summary: Bulandshahr electricity department SDO Krishna Kaushik has come under scrutiny over allegations of corruption and disproportionate assets. His wife herself has filed a complaint in the matter. Energy Minister AK Sharma directed the managing director of PVVNL to investigate the case on 20 October. The SDO's wife claims that her husband owns a Thar with a VIP registration number and leads a luxurious lifestyle. He has several plots and flats, she said, adding that this was not possible on his salary. She had complained about her husband to the energy minister and the governor on 30 September, accusing him of misusing his position to make money through improper means. The SDO came into the spotlight after a dispute with his wife. She had accused him of forcing her to undergo an abortion and provided the police with information about his alleged illegal assets. On 24 September, an FIR was registered at Jahangirabad Kotwali against the SDO, his mother-in-law and father-in-law, and his sister-in-law and her husband, following his wife's complaint. Read the entire case in chronological order Krishna Kaushik is an SDO from the 2019 batch Krishna Kaushik is originally from Khairthal in Rajasthan's Alwar district. He is an SDO from the 2019 batch at Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited. His first posting was as AE (Meter) in the Test Division in Bulandshahr. About three years later, in 2022, he was appointed SDO in the First Subdivision of Bulandshahr's Sikandrabad Division. Before this, he was posted at the Gajraula office in Amroha district. The SDO owns a Thar with registration number 0007 and leads an expensive lifestyle The wife alleged that the SDO drives expensive cars and leads a lavish lifestyle. He owns the top-model Thar Roxx with the registration number 0007. It is priced at around ₹30 lakh to ₹35 lakh. She also alleged that large sums were spent on buying expensive jewellery and equipping the house with modern facilities. These claims have not been verified. Wife says officer bought properties from Sikandrabad to Noida The wife stated in her complaint that Krishna Kaushik purchased several properties in his father's name during his posting in Secunderabad. These reportedly include a residential plot measuring around 200 square metres in Neelkanth Colony, Secunderabad. She also claimed that he bought a house in the Yamunapuram area of Bulandshahr at a cost of around ₹1.5 crore. It has also been alleged that he owns a flat worth crores of rupees in a Godrej Group residential project in Noida. The departmental inquiry will now establish the ownership of these properties, the sources of funds used to purchase them and the status of the related documents. It may also examine whether there is any discrepancy between the properties and the officer's known income. Inquiry being monitored from Shakti Bhavan According to Ravish Gupta, managing director of Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, the complaint cell at Shakti Bhawan in Lucknow is conducting an investigation based on the SDO's wife's complaints and administrative documents. He said departmental and legal action would be taken in accordance with the rules after the investigation report is received. The investigation report is now awaited. The course of further action will become clear only after facts related to the allegations, the actual ownership of the properties and the sources of income emerge. Video of taking ₹50,000 had gone viral A video of Krishna Kaushik surfaced in 2024, when he was posted as SDO First in the Sikandrabad division. In the video, he was seen taking ₹50,000 in the name of an electricity connection. The then managing director, Isha Duhan, suspended him. Read the wife's other allegations against the officer Police also named Krishna Kaushik's father, Ashok Kumar, mother, Tara Devi, sister, Nisha Sharma, and brother-in-law, Dev Sharma, in the case. SP Rural Antariksh Jain confirmed the case and said that a case had been registered and was being investigated.
