stories.title: Man dies after getting stuck to high-tension wire:Brother faints from burns while trying to rescue him in Jhansi
stories.summary: A young man was burnt alive after receiving an electric shock from a high-tension line in Jhansi. He was laying a wire in the field with his brother when it came into contact with an 11,000-volt line. The shock was so powerful that smoke continued to rise from the young man's body even after he fell to the ground. When the younger brother touched the young man, who was burning alive, his hand was also severely burnt. After receiving information about the incident, family members put out the fire. They then took the young man to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place in Rajapur village in the Raksa area, 17 km from the district headquarters. Now, the full incident in detail ... Murari Parihar, who lives in Rajapur village in Raksa, is the village watchman. He has two sons, Deepak and Akash, and a daughter, Anju. Deepak married Kavita around two years ago. They have a six-month-old daughter. Both sons helped their father with farming. Akash, who was injured in the accident, said, "A peanut crop had been planted in the field. At around 12 noon on Friday, I was putting up a wire in the field with my elder brother Deepak. As soon as he threw the wire upwards, it came into contact with an 11,000-volt high-tension line." Aakash said, "The moment my brother came in contact with the wire, there was a loud explosion. His entire body caught fire. I ran to save him. When I grabbed the wire with pliers, I too received a severe electric shock. Darkness descended before my eyes. When I regained consciousness, I was in hospital." It was later learnt that farmers working in nearby fields reached the spot after hearing the sound of the explosion. Deepak's clothes were burning. I was lying nearby. No one had the courage to go near him. After somehow moving the wire away, people took both of us to the medical college. Dr Ravishankar, the medical college's EMO, said: “The relatives brought the two brothers who had suffered burn injuries from an electric shock. Deepak Parihar had died before reaching the hospital, while Akash Parihar was admitted. His right hand is damaged. A team of doctors is treating him.”

stories.title: SP MLC candidate breaks down in tears in Agra:Says he will convert to Islam at Shahi Mosque, feels he is being treated like a terrorist from Pakistan
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party candidate Dr Akash Agrawal began sobbing on Friday over the Agra Teachers' MLC seat. Alleging irregularities in voting, he said, "My supporters are being harassed. Officials are behaving rudely with party workers. No action is being taken despite the complaint." Akash Agrawal said: "It feels as though I am a terrorist who has come from Pakistan. I am being harassed. I do not want to live in such a Sanatan faith. I will go to Lucknow's Shahi Eidgah next month and embrace Islam." The Samajwadi Party candidate said that victory or defeat made no difference to him. He said he was living in an independent India and would decide for himself which party to contest elections for. He alleged that booth capturing was still taking place during voting. Read the full report... Voting for the MLC election was held from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Friday. SP candidate Akash Agarwal alleged that everyone was sent out during the presiding officer's meal break in Kheragarh. He also alleged booth capturing at the Chhata booth. He said officials were behaving rudely with party workers. At around 3 p.m., Akash Agarwal went to meet Divisional Commissioner Nagendra Pratap with a complaint of booth capturing. He said, "I have complained about booth capturing, but no action is being taken." Aakash Agarwal became emotional over the alleged harassment of school managers supporting him by the police and administration. He said, "I do not want to live in a Sanatan faith where I am being harassed because of those who claim to be its guardians and protectors. I will go to Lucknow next month and convert at the Shahi Eidgah." He also said that it was his right to decide which party to contest elections for and which religion to follow. Agarwal alleged that action was being taken against him and the school managers associated with him because they were contesting the election. 'I feel as if I am a terrorist who has come from Pakistan' Aakash Agarwal alleged that he and his associates were harassed during the election. According to him, teachers and school managers associated with him were harassed in 12 districts. Police visited more than 100 schools because of him. Aakash said, "I have started to feel as though I am a terrorist who has come from Pakistan. If they want, they could even plant drugs or weapons on me and have me locked up." He said that if he had known earlier that contesting the election would cause so much trouble for his associates, he would not have contested it. 'Give me life imprisonment, but do not harass my associates' Aakash Agrawal said the government could send him to prison if it wanted, but should stop harassing his family and teachers. He said, "If you want to put me in prison, I will leave from here right now. Give me life imprisonment, but stop harassing my associates." He accused the officials of working under pressure from the government. Aakash said he had no desire to become an MLC. He had stood by his colleagues in the past and would continue to stand by them. Now, learn about Dr Aakash Agrawal Won as an independent in 2020: Dr Aakash Agrawal contested the Agra Division Teachers' MLC seat as an independent and defeated the BJP candidate. Defeated the BJP candidate by 2,376 votes: Aakash Agrawal received 6,690 votes, while BJP's Dinesh Chandra Vashishth received 4,314 votes. Hoped for a BJP ticket: Aakash Agrawal wanted a BJP ticket in the 2026 election, but the party nominated Harikishore Tiwari. Joined SP and received a ticket: After failing to secure a ticket from the BJP, Aakash Agrawal joined the Samajwadi Party. The party nominated him for the Agra division teachers' MLC seat. Raised teachers' issues: Aakash Agrawal raised issues such as honorariums for teachers in unaided schools, cashless treatment and the restoration of the old pension scheme.

stories.title: Husband accuses wife of killing 5-year-old son with poisoned milk:Says she left him 6 months ago in Hathras
stories.summary: After drinking milk on Thursday night in Hathras, a young man and two children fell ill. They were taken to hospital, where doctors declared one of the boys dead. As the young man and the other child were in critical condition, they were referred to Aligarh Medical College. The husband told police that he learnt about the incident on Friday morning. His wife had left him six months ago and had been living with her lover. He said she had given poison-laced milk to his two sons, aged five and six, and her lover. He said he wanted his wife to receive the strictest possible punishment. The incident took place on Thursday night in the Khandari Garhi locality of the Hathras Gate area. Eight days ago, the woman's lover came to live with her and the children Zahid, a resident of Rudayan village in the Sasni Kotwali area, had a love marriage with Kajal, who is also from the village, in 2019. They have two sons, Ashu, five, and Zoaib, six. Zahid goes around selling scrap. It has been reported that after a dispute between the husband and wife, Kajal began living separately with both children. She had been living with a young man named Danish for around six months. Danish, a resident of Gijrauli village, works at a footwear showroom. Around eight days ago, he moved with Kajal and both children into a rented house in the Khandari Garhi neighbourhood. Health deteriorated after drinking milk at 10 pm Husband Zahid said that at around 10 p.m. on Thursday, Kajal gave Danish and both children milk to drink. A few hours later, all three began to feel unwell. At around 1 a.m., they were brought to the emergency department of the district hospital. Doctors declared Ashu (five) dead, while Danish and Joeib were referred to Aligarh Medical College in critical condition. The child's body has been sent for post-mortem examination. It has not yet been confirmed what caused all three to fall ill. On receiving the news of his son's death, Zahid reached the post-mortem house. He alleged that Kajal had poisoned both his children. He also expressed suspicion about Danish's role. However, the police have not yet received a written complaint in the case, and the poisoning has not been confirmed. City Circle Officer Himanshu Mathur said: “The child's body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The police are investigating the matter from all angles. No complaint has been received regarding the incident so far.”

stories.title: Clash erupts during Varanasi Graduate MLC polls:SP candidate Ashutosh Sinha clashes with BJP workers, scuffle also breaks out with police
stories.summary: A clash broke out between Samajwadi Party candidate Ashutosh Sinha and BJP workers at a polling centre in Sadar tehsil during the graduate MLC election on Friday. The commotion, which began at around 1 p.m., also led to pushing and shoving involving police personnel. BJP workers alleged that Ashutosh Sinha had entered the polling centre and was asking voters for their votes with folded hands. Samajwadi Party leaders, meanwhile, described this as the BJP's frustration over its impending defeat and questioned the administration's role. Former minister Manoj Rai Dhoopchandi demanded that the election be cancelled and voting held again. Samajwadi Party MP Virendra Singh accused the BJP of creating a dispute during the election and using police personnel in its favour. See the pictures... Former minister Manoj Rai demanded that the election be cancelled Former Samajwadi Party minister Manoj Rai Dhoopchandi said that video recording was taking place at the polling station. He demanded an inquiry into the incident and said that if the election was being influenced in this manner, it should be cancelled and repolling held. He alleged that the administration was helping the BJP. However, the administration's role and the allegations that the election was being influenced have not been independently confirmed. Manoj Rai said that when the BJP starts losing, it creates such incidents. He alleged that BJP workers were misbehaving with administrative officials and Samajwadi Party workers. MP Virendra Singh said - When the BJP sees defeat, it picks fights Chandauli MP Virendra Singh said that Samajwadi Party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav had been a teacher and worked to improve the education system. He raised teachers' problems inside and outside the House, as well as while in government. Virendra Singh said that this was why the teaching community regarded the Samajwadi Party as one that worked in the interests of education and teachers. Virendra Singh alleged that when the BJP begins to see its defeat, its candidates or supporters start creating disputes. Accusing police personnel of working in the BJP's favour, he said officials were behaving like BJP workers rather than government employees. Several BJP leaders want to join SP: Virendra Singh The MP also claimed that several BJP MLAs in Uttar Pradesh wanted to join the Samajwadi Party and that there were dozens of such leaders. However, the party's national president had not yet opened the doors for them. BJP said: Ashutosh Sinha was seeking votes inside the polling booth BJP workers said Samajwadi Party candidate Ashutosh Sinha had entered the polling centre and was seeking votes from voters, which is against the rules. They objected to this and created a commotion. The workers also accused the candidate of practising caste politics. A scuffle broke out with police personnel during the dispute. For now, the allegations made by BJP workers, the claims of Samajwadi Party leaders and the role of the police are yet to be verified through statements by the relevant officials and video recordings from the polling centre.

stories.summary: Nepal is set to receive $21.6 million from the United Nations’ Loss and Damage Fund following the devastating Bhotekoshi floods that struck the country in August. The allocation marks the first time the global climate fund has earmarked money for a specific country to address climate-change-linked losses. Climate experts have welcomed the decision as a landmark step, but the funding is only a fraction of the nearly $5 billion Nepal estimates it needs for recovery and reconstruction.

stories.title: Lucknow model Shraddha Dubey to remain in jail:Court cites serious murder charges, denies bail
stories.summary: The bail plea of model Shraddha Dubey, accused in the death of Lucknow businessman Shiva Sharma, has been rejected by the CJM court on Friday. Her sister, Rashmi Dubey, and driver Tanveer, alias Danish, were also denied bail. All three had filed bail applications in the court on Friday. The judge refused to grant them bail, citing the serious nature of the case. The accused are now likely to approach a higher court for bail. The court said the case was serious and would be heard by a Sessions Court. It found no valid reason to grant bail to the accused at this stage. Shraddha, Rashmi and Tanveer were arrested from an apartment in Nagpur on Tuesday. They were brought to Lucknow and questioned for 6 hours and 35 minutes on Thursday. After the questioning, all three were sent to jail for 10 days. Shiva Sharma died on October 9 after falling from Shraddha’s flat in Lucknow. Following his death, his mother filed a murder case against Shraddha. She had been absconding before her arrest. Shraddha questioned for 6 hours and 35 minutes at Hazratganj police station When Shraddha reached the Hazratganj police station at 10 am on Thursday, she was seen covering her face. She entered the station with her hand raised to avoid being photographed. Police questioned her for 6 hours and 35 minutes. Her sister Rashmi and driver Danish were also questioned separately. According to sources, Shraddha remained silent during the questioning and repeatedly told the police to speak to her lawyer instead of questioning her directly. Later, police took all three accused in the same van to the Civil Hospital for medical examinations. The process took around 35 minutes, after which they were produced before the court. DCP says action will be taken against those who helped the accused Central DCP Arpit Vijayvargiya said the three accused arrested in Nagpur in connection with the Shiva Sharma murder case had been brought in for detailed questioning. Two mobile phones and other items recovered from them have been sealed and will be sent for forensic examination. He said the investigation was continuing based on the information gathered during questioning. Police are also checking who helped the accused during the past 10 days. Action will be taken against those found to have helped them, based on the available evidence. Shraddha called herself innocent during her time on the run While she was absconding, Shraddha Dubey gave a nearly three-minute statement to news agency ANI, claiming that she was innocent. She alleged that Shiva Sharma’s mother had made false accusations against her because she did not like Shraddha. What Shraddha Dubey said while claiming she was innocent 1. ‘The allegations are baseless; CCTV footage will prove my innocence’ Shraddha denied the murder allegations, saying Shiva Sharma had died by suicide. She claimed she saw him jump from the fourth floor of her building. She said CCTV footage from the building would prove her innocence and questioned why it had not been collected, even though cameras near the Nepal border had been checked. 2. ‘Shiva’s mother did not like me’ Shraddha said she had known Shiva for only four months, and they were friends for the first two to two-and-a-half months. He had started visiting her home only in the past two months. She claimed Shiva’s mother had accused her falsely because she did not like her. 3. ‘Shiva was my boyfriend and had a debt of ₹16–17 lakh’ Shraddha claimed Shiva had told her he was under financial stress because of loans and was receiving calls from creditors. He allegedly asked her for financial help. She also claimed that around a month earlier, he had taken jewellery worth ₹5–6 lakh from her home, calling it their personal matter and saying he had the right to take it because he was her boyfriend. 4. ‘I left the hospital because I was in shock and had breathing problems’ Shraddha said she left the hospital because she was traumatised and had difficulty breathing. She claimed she would otherwise have stayed to face the situation, but left after Shiva’s family allegedly assaulted her driver and accused her of murder. 5. ‘I have no connections with politicians or officers’ Shraddha denied having links with any politician or officer and said photographs with people did not prove any connection. She claimed she had been framed because Shiva’s mother disliked her, possibly because she was one or two years older than Shiva. She appealed to the police and judiciary for a fair investigation, saying a person should not be branded a criminal across the country merely because of a murder allegation. 6. ‘My sister has no connection with Shiva’ Shraddha said her sister had come to meet her after a long time and knew nothing about the case. She claimed her sister had no connection with Shiva and had been unnecessarily dragged into the case despite being innocent.

stories.title: Wedding held on mobile tower in UP:Woman says she cannot live without lover; boyfriend in Mumbai says ‘Qubool hai’ over phone
stories.summary: A girl climbed a mobile phone tower in Uttar Pradesh’s Bahraich district on Friday morning, insisting that she would marry her boyfriend at any cost. Even as her family and villagers pleaded with her to climb down, she remained on the tower. After more than three hours of high drama, the family finally agreed to her demand and arranged an online nikah. The girl’s boyfriend works in Mumbai. The family called a qazi from a nearby mosque, who contacted the boy over the phone and asked him to accept the marriage. The qazi then spoke to the girl sitting atop the tower and had her accept the nikah as well. The girl finally climbed down after she was convinced that the marriage had been solemnised. The dramatic incident took place in the Motipur area, around 60 km from the Bahraich district headquarters. The couple had been in a relationship for five months Fakhruddin, alias Nooruddin (21), and Saiba Begum, alias Mehak (19), live in different neighbourhoods of Basthanwa village, around 1 km apart. The two had been in a relationship for five months, but their families opposed their marriage. Two months ago, Nooruddin moved to Mumbai for work. Nooruddin’s family includes his father, Farukh, his mother and two brothers. The family earns a living through farming and labour work. Mehak’s father, Rais Ahmad, has died. Her mother, Hasmatunnisha, has been raising the children through wage labour. She had refused to let Mehak marry Nooruddin. However, Mehak continued speaking to him despite her mother’s scolding. Climbed a mobile tower after an argument with her mother On Friday morning, Mehak again argued with her mother over her marriage. She then left home and climbed a mobile tower outside the village. When villagers spotted her, they urged her to come down. However, Mehak refused, insisting that she wanted to marry Nooruddin. The villagers informed both families and the police about the situation. Mehak’s mother remained opposed to the marriage, while villagers continued trying to persuade both of them. A police team, including female officers, also reached the spot. The girl was assured that Nooruddin would be contacted and the marriage arranged if she came down. However, Mehak refused to leave the tower. Drama continued for three hours After villagers and police persuaded them, it was decided that the two would be married. A qazi was called from the village mosque. After three hours of drama, the qazi called the teenager on the tower and explained the marriage to her. She was made to accept the nikah over the phone. After this, Nooruddin, who was living in Mumbai, was informed about the matter over the phone. He too agreed to the marriage. The qazi also got him to accept the nikah over the phone. Once the girl was convinced that her nikah had taken place, she agreed to come down. With the help of women police personnel, Mahek was brought down. When her daughter came down, the mother backed out again As soon as Mahak came down, her mother again opposed the relationship. She said, "I do not approve of this relationship. If the girl still wants to live with the same boy, she can leave the house." The police then took the girl and her family members to the police station. After counselling them there, Mahak was sent home with her mother. Station House Officer Brahmanand Gaur said, “This is a case involving a love affair. The girl climbed the tower because she insisted on marrying her boyfriend. She was brought down after the nikah was completed. For now, she has been sent home with her family. Further action will be taken if a complaint is received.”

stories.title: Fire breaks out in moving 'Verna' car in Gorakhpur:Driver jumps out as smoke rises from engine, traffic jam on Medical College Road
stories.summary: A moving ‘Verna’ suddenly caught fire on Medical College Road in Gorakhpur at around 11:30 am on Friday. The driver jumped out and managed to save his life. Nearby shopkeepers managed to bring the fire under control. However, smoke continued to billow from the car. Fire brigade personnel then arrived in a fire engine and sprayed a powerful stream of water on the car's engine, completely extinguishing the fire. During this time, vehicles were stopped on both sides of the road, resulting in a long traffic jam. Two pictures of the incident Read the full story below : According to fire personnel, Mahindra has a showroom in Mogalaha near the medical college. On Friday, a Mahindra employee was taking a Lucknow-registered Verna car to the service centre when he had just reached Mogalaha. Smoke suddenly began billowing from the engine area. Seeing this, the driver abandoned the car and jumped out. Shortly afterwards, intense flames erupted from the front of the car, which began burning fiercely. Nearby shopkeepers managed to put out the fire using water and other materials, but thick smoke continued to come out. The fire brigade vehicle arrived about 20 minutes after the incident, following the alert. Fire personnel immediately began spraying the car with water at full pressure. The car had been completely gutted in the fire, which burned for about 20 minutes. Meanwhile, hundreds of people gathered to watch the incident.

stories.title: Premanand Maharaj resumes foot march after five months:Walks to Keli Kunj Ashram; devotees get emotional in Vrindavan
stories.summary: Premanand Maharaj undertook a foot procession in Vrindavan for the first time in five months on Friday morning. While travelling from the new ashram to Keli Kunj Ashram, he became emotional after seeing a large crowd of devotees at Varah Ghat junction. He then got out of his car and walked to the ashram as devotees standing on both sides of the road chanted "Radhe-Radhe" and "Shri Harivansh". After reaching Keli Kunj Ashram, Premanand Maharaj first worshipped Radha Rani and then paid his respects to his guru, Hit Govind Sharan Maharaj. He stayed at the ashram for around 30 minutes before returning to Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. On September 25, disciple Rasik Dulari died after jumping from the fourth floor of the Keli Kunj Trust building. Following this incident, Premanand Maharaj visited Keli Kunj Ashram for the first time on October 8. During that visit, he walked and gave devotees darshan but did not take part in a foot procession. He stayed there for around 15 minutes. Before this, Premanand Maharaj had undertaken a foot pilgrimage on May 27. He would regularly leave Shri Radha Keli Kunj Ashram around 3 am and walk about 1.5 kilometres to reach Saubhari Forest in Sunrakh Khadar, which is managed by the Forest Department. Check out the visuals below : Foot pilgrimage stopped in May due to health issues Saint Premanand Maharaj's foot pilgrimage was suspended indefinitely from May 17 due to health issues. His disciples said at the time that he was unwell. He had also stopped holding private one-to-one meetings with devotees. Both of his kidneys have failed, and he undergoes dialysis two to three times a week. Premanand Maharaj also released a video in which he made an emotional appeal to his devotees. He said, "Do not worry at all. Whether we meet or not, whether we speak or not, we love you all very much. The most important thing is that you should not worry about how we will move forward. Even without speaking, we will remain in your thoughts." However, ten days later, on May 27, he undertook the foot pilgrimage again. The pilgrimage was suspended once more after that. Got out of the car on the way to Keli Kunj Ashram Premanand Maharaj left Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram at around 5 am on Friday. When he reached the Varaha Ghat junction, he saw a large crowd of devotees waiting for his darshan. He got out of his vehicle and walked to Keli Kunj Ashram. Devotees became excited on seeing him and welcomed him with chants of praise from both sides of the road. Worshipped Radha Rani and sought his guru's blessings After reaching Keli Kunj Ashram, Premanand Maharaj first worshipped Radha Rani. He then visited the ashram of his guru, Hit Govind Sharan Maharaj, in the Varaha Ghat area, around 200 metres away. There, he sought his guru's blessings and offered prayers. After staying for around 30 minutes, he left for Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Maharaj visited Keli Kunj Ashram 15 days ago as well On the morning of 25 September, disciple Rasik Dulari ended her life by jumping from the fourth floor of the Keli Kunj Trust building. Sant Premanand Maharaj visited Keli Kunj Ashram for the first time after that on 8 October. On that occasion too, he walked to appear before devotees and stayed at the ashram for about 15 minutes. He then returned to the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram near the Lakshmi Ji temple in Belvan. The new ashram is 15 kilometres from Keli Kunj Ashram Premanand Maharaj's trust, Shri Hit Radha Keli Kunj, has built a new ashram named Yamuna Vihar Kunj. Since 18 May, Sant Premanand Maharaj has been staying at the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. It has been built on the banks of the Yamuna near Jahangirpur village in Mant tehsil. It is around one kilometre from the Lakshmiji Temple in Belvan. The ashram has two large halls, where Maharajji conducts satsangs and serves Radharani. A dialysis machine has been installed in a container here. Doctors perform dialysis on Premanand Maharaj from time to time.

stories.title: Tikait calls govt ‘vote chor’:Accuses it of stealing sugarcane and paddy; BKU holds mahapanchayat in Lucknow, demands higher sugarcane prices
stories.summary: Rakesh Tikait, national spokesperson of the Bharatiya Kisan Union, began a sit-in with his supporters at the gate of the Sugarcane Institute in Lucknow on Thursday night, ahead of the farmers' mahapanchayat. The mahapanchayat is proposed for Friday, but as permission for the event had not been granted, Rakesh Tikait began the protest a day earlier. He also appeared annoyed that the gate of the Sugarcane Institute was locked. Started sit-in a day early after permission was denied After permission was not granted for the farmers' mahapanchayat at the Sugarcane Institute, Rakesh Tikait reached the gate with his supporters. On seeing the gate locked, he protested and sat down for a sit-in. He demanded that the administration get the gate opened. Farmers' leaders taking part in the sit-in raised slogans against the Sugarcane Commissioner, saying, "Sugarcane Commissioner, come to your senses." Announces protest will continue until the gate is opened Rakesh Tikait announced that his protest would continue until the Sugarcane Institute gate was opened. He said the agitation would continue until the administration met their demands. Rakesh Tikait also announced that farmers would stage sit-ins and protests at all district headquarters in Uttar Pradesh. This indicated plans to turn the farmers' agitation into a statewide movement. Local police force deployed at the site A local police force has been deployed at the site after the sit-in began at the Sugarcane Institute gate. Farmer leaders and their supporters are staging the protest over their demands. Police stop Sonbhadra farmers, who raise slogans Meanwhile, police stopped Sonbhadra farmers near Sabha Kheda village on Thursday by putting up barricades as they were heading to gherao the office of the Consolidation Commissioner in Lucknow. The farmers, who arrived under the leadership of the Bharatiya Kisan Union Lokshakti (A.Ra.), have been staging a protest for around 521 days against irregularities in the consolidation process in Mainswar village of Ghorawal tehsil. The farmers allege that officials committed serious irregularities during the consolidation process, but the problem was not resolved despite repeated complaints. After being stopped near Kalli West, the farmers raised slogans, leading to a traffic jam on the road. Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police South Rallapalli Vasanth Kumar and Assistant Commissioner of Police Gosainganj Rishabh Yadav reached the spot and tried to convince the farmers. The farmers were then sent towards Kalli West. They reached Vrindavan ground on foot and on tractors via the canal route.

stories.title: 75-year-old man’s fiancée takes U-turn:Reel-maker Reena says ‘My husband has returned’; family says ‘You won’t marry an old man’
stories.summary: A video of 30-year-old Reena, who got engaged to an elderly man in Auraiya, has emerged. In it, she says: My husband has returned to me. He had seen the video of my engagement. There is now a fight going on at home. My family members have also said that I should not marry that old man. Radha didi is saying that I should marry her father, but I will not marry that old man. My husband has returned to me; we had not got divorced. Now I will marry him again. Three days earlier, the elderly man had said in a conversation that it was not an engagement but reel-making. Reena's aim was to increase her followers on Instagram. All this was done to become famous. My daughter had asked me to stage the act. Reena had got my daughter to make her do all this. On 14 October, a video of Reena and Ramsughar had surfaced on social media. In it, the two appeared to be getting engaged. The video also showed their haldi ceremony. Ramsughar's daughter Radha had said that the two would also get married soon. There is an age gap of around 45 years between them. Read what Reena said in the video My husband has returned home I am going to tell you the truth because my husband has returned home. He had watched the video, after which a fight broke out in my house. There has been a lot of arguing. Now we will get married again and show you. My family has said that I will not marry that old man. I had not divorced my husband. Now I will marry him again. My husband had left earlier, but he has now returned. There will be no other marriage now. I want to live with him. The engagement that took place has been cancelled. I will not marry that old man Radha didi is saying that I should marry her father, but I will not marry that old man. He is my husband. My family is complete now. When no one was supporting me, I had spoken to Radha didi about marrying her father. My family is complete now because my husband has returned. He watched my videos and then came back. I will now live with him. I have nothing to do with anyone and no connection with anyone. My family is complete now. I have remarried. I have nothing to do with anyone Radha Didi is saying that I should marry her father, but she should make her own blogs and not post blogs about me. I am happy with my family now. I have nothing to do with anyone. I have no connection with anyone-not Radha Didi or her father. Elderly man said he had made the video at his daughter's request Three days earlier, in a video released by Ram Sughar, he had said, "What do we have to hide? The girl is alone. There is no one around her. Her partner had married her and then abandoned her. Since then, she had been wandering around aimlessly. We also wanted her to benefit in some way and gain more followers." Ram Sughar said, My daughter Radha became acquainted with Reena through Instagram. Gradually, their friendship grew and they began making videos together. Reena had been visiting our home since then. After this, Reena wrote the engagement script. The engagement video of Ram Sughar and Rani Rajput was then filmed at a beauty parlour in Auraiya itself. Only 4,000 followers gained after engagement video After posting the video, Reena's Instagram account has gained only 4,000 followers. She now has 12.4k followers. Meanwhile, Reena's brother Sagar, who arranged the engagement, has just 711 followers on Instagram. The notable point is that no one can currently speak directly to Reena and Ramsughar. Reena and Ramsughar have managers, who decide whether to allow anyone to speak to them. Ramsughar's daughter arranged reel-making Ramsughar, a resident of Ariyari village in the Sahar area, has two daughters and a son. All of them are married. His son drives an auto-rickshaw. His elder daughter, Radha, lives with her father. Radha used to shoot videos with YouTuber Shivani, who was set to appear on Bigg Boss. Shivani is also a resident of Ariyari village. According to her daughter Radha, Reena got married 10 years ago. However, she was divorced just three years after the marriage. Reena gradually began making videos for Instagram and YouTube. Meanwhile, Reena's family consists of her mother and a brother, Sagar. Her brother Sagar was the one who arranged Reena's engagement to Ramsughar.

stories.title: Shraddha says ‘He was my boyfriend’ when asked about lipstick:Lucknow Police asked 120 questions in 6 hours 35 minutes; she was angry over pimples on her face
stories.summary: Police asked model Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the murder of multi-millionaire businessman Shiva Sharma, a total of 120 questions in sequence within six and a half hours. After the businessman died, lipstick was found smeared on his face and stomach. When police questioned accused Shraddha about this, she said, "Shiva was my boyfriend. I did not kill him. It was a suicide." Shraddha appeared angry during the interrogation. She said tying a dupatta had caused rashes to break out on her face. She told police that on the morning of the incident, they went out at 7 a.m. and went to sleep at 5 p.m. Shiva then committed suicide. Police questioned all three accused, Shraddha, Rashmi and Danish, in separate rooms. The interrogation revealed that Shraddha had travelled from Nepal to Lucknow, after which she left for Nagpur via Agra. On Tuesday, the UP STF arrested accused Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver Danish in Nagpur. After this, two police teams obtained transit remand from the court and brought all three to Lucknow on Thursday morning. After questioning them at Hazratganj police station, they underwent medical examinations at Civil Hospital before the court produced them. The court sent all three accused to 10 days' judicial custody. Shraddha's arrest: 3 pictures taken while she was being brought to Lucknow... Two mobile phones recovered Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and driver Danish had demanded that their medical examinations be conducted at the police station itself, but the police flatly refused. The accused had said there were large numbers of media personnel outside, so their medical examinations should be conducted there. The police have so far recovered two mobile phones, and there has been no FaceTime activity on them after 9 October. The phones are Apple 17 Pro Max models. During questioning by the police, Shraddha said that she had fallen ill and had developed a rash as a result. Model said - slept until late evening, incident occurred at night Businessman Shiva died after falling from the fourth floor. When his body was found, there was lipstick on his face and stomach. Asked why Shiva Sharma had lipstick on his face and stomach, Shraddha said that he was her boyfriend. That was why there was lipstick on his face. Meanwhile, at around 7 a.m. on the day of the incident, Shraddha Dubey, Shiv Sharma and others reached the Awadh Green Apartment. They then slept until late evening, after which the incident occurred at night. Did not stay in any city for more than 12 hours The police had also issued a lookout circular in the case to prevent Shraddha and the accused accompanying her from fleeing abroad. During her time on the run, Shraddha Dubey did not stay in any city for more than 12 hours. This was why the police could not arrest her for 11 days. In fact, the port number in the IP address was appearing incorrectly. As a result, the location was shown incorrectly and the teams went in the wrong direction. This was why one team went to Prayagraj, while Shraddha was arrested in Nagpur. Teams searched in several cities That day too, the police team had to go to another location in Nagpur because of the same technical glitch. The STF team reached the wrong place. But when Shraddha's location at the hotel was confirmed, the team was called back to that location. Meanwhile, the IP address was updated in four hours, while other details arrived within 12 hours. As a result, the police could track the location only after a 16-hour delay. This allowed Shraddha to flee every 12 hours. Shiva and Shraddha had quarrelled before the incident Police questioning has revealed that Shiva Sharma and Shraddha Dubey had an argument on the day of the incident. The entire incident took place after this. The police have so far recorded the statement of Shraddha Dubey's maid in the case. Statements have also been taken from the neighbours who helped take Shiva Sharma to hospital after he fell. Along with their statements, the police have also recorded the statements of other people who knew the two closely. She left the trolley bag and wore a burqa because people would call her VVIP Shraddha Dubey left the trolley bag while fleeing to Nepal after the incident. People accompanying her had advised her in Maharajganj that if she carried a trolley bag while crossing the border, people would think she was a VVIP. They said that if she travelled with a bag and wore a burqa, people would consider her a local and ordinary citizen. Since the area has a Muslim-majority population, Shraddha adopted this tactic. She was also on alert to conceal her identity. People advised him that the police would beat him if they caught him Police questioning revealed that people close to Shraddha had advised her, "When the police catch you, they will beat you badly." As a result, she said in her statement that she had become frightened and was therefore fleeing. After the incident, she also threw away her SIM card. She had tried to go to her home in Raebareli but, out of fear, could not make it there. During her time on the run, she also ran out of cash. Only ₹25,000 remained at the time of her arrest.

stories.title: 4 killed as car falls into ditch on Dausa highway:Tyre bursts, devotees returning to Agra after Khatu Shyamji darshan
stories.summary: A major road accident occurred on the Manoharpur-Dausa Highway (NH-148) near Raisar at 6:15 a.m. on Friday. The car, which went out of control after a tyre burst, plunged into a roadside ditch. Four people are reported to have died in the accident, while two others were seriously injured. As soon as the accident was reported, Raisar police reached the spot. With the help of local residents, the injured were pulled out and taken to hospital. The accident led to a long traffic jam on the highway. Police remained engaged in relief and rescue operations at the site. According to preliminary information, all the occupants of the car were returning to Agra after paying obeisance at the Khatu Shyamji temple. During the journey, the car went out of control after a tyre burst near Raisar and plunged into a ditch. Four friends died on the spot after their car went into a ditch following a tyre burst on National Highway 148 (Dausa-Manoharpur) in Raisar, Jaipur district, on Friday morning. Two others were seriously injured in the accident. The accident took place around 6 am in the Raisar police station area. The car was carrying six friends, all residents of Agra, Uttar Pradesh. They were returning after visiting the Khatu Shyamji temple when the driver lost control of the car after a tyre burst, causing it to fall into a ditch. Four friends die on the spot Circle Officer Ramkishan Bishnoi said the deceased have been identified as Atul, Mukul, Rupesh and Shiva. Rahul and Arpit were seriously injured and have been admitted to NIMS Hospital. The accident also caused a long traffic jam on the highway.

stories.title: FIR against 5 electricity department employees in Gorakhpur:3 brothers die of electrocution during idol immersion, cremated together
stories.summary: Three brothers were killed after coming into contact with a high-tension current during the immersion of a Durga idol in Jungle Ayodhya Prasad in Gorakhpur's Gulriha area. On the basis of a complaint filed by Dinesh Chauhan, the brother of the deceased Chandan, an FIR was registered at Gulriha police station on Thursday evening against electricity department SSO Sunil Maurya, junior engineer (JE) Niketan Gupta, and contract linemen Ajay Maurya, Brijesh Kumar and Ganga Nishad. Police have detained Sunil Maurya and Ramkesh. Vicky, Lucky and Chandan, who lost their lives after being electrocuted during the idol immersion, were cremated together on Thursday evening. As their funeral pyres burned together at Kolhuan Ghat in Gulriha, the family members were inconsolable. The bodies of all three victims were post-mortemed at BRD Medical College. They were then taken to the village at around 4 p.m. Hundreds of people gathered at the cremation ground. In view of the crowd, police and officials from several police stations were also present. Three people died in the accident, while nine people, including a beat constable, suffered electrical burns. The administration has formed a three-member committee to investigate the incident, and it will submit its report within three days. Brother makes allegations in complaint In his complaint, Dinesh said that at around 4.30 p.m. on Wednesday, villagers were proceeding for the immersion of a Durga idol. His younger brother Chandan (16), nephew Lucky (20) and Vicky (18) were also part of the procession. The department had been informed in advance to keep the power supply switched off during the immersion. It is alleged that the high-tension line passing overhead was switched on when the idol reached Rajai crossroads. As a result, Chandan, Lucky, Vicky, Virendra Vishwakarma, Shivani Chauhan, Priyanshu, Nandini, Monu, Shantanu, Anil Bharti, Satyawan Chauhan, Ramdas's wife Pushpa, Anil, Anshika, Anshu and two constables deployed on duty, Salman and Dhananjay Pandey, suffered electric shocks and burn injuries. Chandan, Lucky and Vicky died in the incident. The deceased's brother alleged that electricity department employees deliberately and in a pre-planned manner switched on the power supply, leading to the deaths of all three. Family devastated by the deaths of two sons Vicky and Lucky were two of three brothers. Their elder brother is named Jackie. Their mother is Seema and their father is Shivchandra. Shivchandra works in a private job in Hyderabad. The father, who was working away from home to support the family, could not have imagined that his two sons would die together. The family has been devastated by the deaths of both sons. Their mother, Seema, is inconsolable. The house, once filled with the liveliness of the children's presence, is now engulfed in mourning. Chandan was the youngest of four siblings. His family includes his brother Dinesh, sisters Neetu and Meera, mother Jayanti Devi and father Kedarnath. Kedarnath works as a labourer and is also the BJP's booth president. Chandan also worked as a labourer alongside his father and helped support the family. The family had been looking for a match for Chandan's sister. There had been hopes of a wedding in the house, but the accident changed everything. Only the memories remain of the son who used to go to work as a labourer with his father. Nine people suffer burns in accident Anshika, Shivani, Priyanshu, Monu Chauhan, Dhirendra Vishwakarma, Pushpa Devi, Shivangi Chauhan, Shantanu Chauhan and constable Dhananjay Pandey suffered electric shock burns in the accident. All of them have been admitted to BRD Medical College, where they are undergoing treatment. The District Magistrate has formed a three-member committee to investigate the accident. It comprises the Additional District Magistrate (City), the Additional Superintendent of Police (City) and the Superintending Engineer, Rural Electricity. The committee has been directed to complete the investigation and submit its report within three days. Families of the deceased seek ₹1 crore compensation each After three people died after coming into contact with a high-tension line, their families have placed their demands before the administration. The memorandum submitted by Chandan's father, Kedar Chauhan, seeks action against the responsible officers and employees of the Electricity Department and the police personnel deployed on duty. The families have demanded compensation of ₹1 crore each for the family of every deceased person, a government job for one member of each family and financial assistance for the injured. They have also demanded that the responsible officers and employees of the electricity department associated with Madarhawa Hydel be suspended and that murder cases be registered against them. In addition, they have demanded that the police personnel deployed for the immersion be suspended and murder cases be registered against them as well, and that the injured be given ₹50 lakh each from the Chief Minister's Relief Fund. Now, know the full story... Three brothers died in Gorakhpur on Wednesday evening after coming into contact with a high-tension line during the immersion of a Durga idol. Two of the victims were real brothers, while the third was their maternal cousin. Nine people were also injured in the incident. They were all travelling on a tractor-trolley to immerse the idol. Police reached the spot and sent the injured to the medical college. Meanwhile, people angered by the incident created a commotion outside the medical college, leading to a 1-km-long traffic jam. Shopkeepers shut more than 50 shops around the medical college and fled. As the commotion escalated, two battalions of the PAC arrived at the spot. The junior engineer and two police personnel were suspended. The lineman was dismissed from service. The traffic jam was cleared at 7:40 pm, around three hours later. The incident occurred at 5 pm on Wednesday in the Gulhariya police station area. See the pictures... DJ railing comes into contact with high-tension wire, three killed A Durga idol had been installed in Chauhan Tola of Jangal Ayodhya Prasad village. On Wednesday evening, five villagers were taking the idol to Kolhua Ghat for immersion. At around 4:30 p.m., the procession reached the area near Ramanand's doorway at Rajahi Chauraha. During this time, the iron railing installed on top of the DJ came into contact with a high-tension wire passing overhead. Twelve people, including Chandan (21), Vicky (18) and Lucky (17), who were near the DJ, were struck by the current. People present nearby took the injured to BRD Medical College. After examining them, doctors declared Chandan, Vicky and Lucky dead. Pushpa Devi, Nandini, Dhirendra, Monu, Anshika Chauhan, Shani Chauhan, Priyanshu, Shivani and Shantanu are undergoing treatment. Electricity department accused of negligence Following the accident, anger spread among villagers against the electricity department. They alleged that a shutdown had been requested in advance to ensure that the power supply remained switched off during the immersion of the idol. Despite this, the power was switched on, leading to the accident. Angry villagers blocked the Gorakhpur-Maharajganj four-lane road in front of the BRD Medical College gate at around 6 p.m. This led to a long queue of vehicles on the road. After receiving the information, District Magistrate Deepak Meena and SSP Dr Kaustubh also reached the spot with police personnel. JE suspended, 2 policemen suspended, lineman terminated District Magistrate Deepak Meena said three people were killed and nine injured after coming into contact with an 11,000-volt high-tension line. All the injured are out of danger. The victims' families had demanded action against electricity department employees and police personnel deployed on duty, as well as compensation. The junior engineer and two police personnel have been suspended. The lineman, meanwhile, has been dismissed from service.

stories.title: Special hoarding put up in Lucknow on Akhilesh’s birthday:Bid to connect with youth in AI, Gen-Z era; pledge to fulfil unkept promises
stories.summary: A hoarding put up outside the Samajwadi Party office on the occasion of party national president Akhilesh Yadav's birthday has become a topic of discussion in the city. Put up by Jairam Pandey, who was the Samajwadi Party candidate from the Mehdawal constituency in Sant Kabir Nagar district, the hoarding imagines Akhilesh Yadav as the future chief minister and carries the message: "What remained unfinished in 2017, all those tasks will be completed in 2027." The notable feature of the hoarding is that it does not merely convey birthday wishes; it also gives prominence to development and modern technology. The image shows Akhilesh Yadav standing with two young people. A modern city, greenery, infrastructure developed along a river and a drone in the sky can be seen in the background. The upper section of the hoarding mentions Gen-Z and AI. It also carries the English message: "To Empower The Youth Drive The Gain" Akhilesh Again, meaning empowering the youth and driving progress. Party workers celebrate Akhilesh's birthday twice Samajwadi Party workers celebrate Akhilesh Yadav's birthday twice a year. Official documents list his birthday as 1 July, while some workers also celebrate it on 23 October and consider that to be his real birthday. Every year, Jairam Pandey puts up a unique hoarding outside the party office, which becomes a talking point. From ‘I am coming’ to ‘ruler of 27’ Before the 2022 election, a large hoarding was put up outside Akhilesh Yadav's residence on 23 October 2021. It featured a picture of Akhilesh Yadav addressing a crowd, along with a countdown machine showing how much time remained until the election. The hoarding put up in 2025 carried the slogan "A government of a powerful engine". The hoarding with the slogan "Ruler of 27", put up on the same occasion in 2024, received the most attention.

stories.title: Kashi weather remains clear, AQI 126:Light morning fog expected from next week; winds blowing at 5 kmph
stories.summary: Weather remained clear in Kashi on Friday morning. The morning temperature was recorded at 26 degrees Celsius. Winds blew at 5 kilometres per hour, while humidity stood at 70%. However, despite the clear weather, the city's air quality is a cause for concern. Varanasi's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 126. This falls in the moderate category. At this level, sensitive people may experience breathing difficulties or discomfort. Light fog may be seen in the mornings from next week According to the weather department's forecast, light fog is likely to be seen in the mornings after the next week. There are currently no signs of any major change in the weather. In the coming days, sunshine may be accompanied by humid heat during the day, causing discomfort. With no active western disturbance, the possibility of immediate rainfall is low. Current weather conditions are giving farmers an opportunity to prepare for rabi crops. They can plough their fields and prepare the soil for sowing wheat, mustard, gram and peas. However, it would be better to determine the right time for sowing based on the crop variety, local temperatures and moisture in the soil. stories.title: ‘He made other men exploit me’:Ghazipur Class 10 student accuses constable of blackmail; cop claims she runs extortion racket
stories.summary: A 17-year-old Class 10 student has accused a police constable of sexually exploiting her on the promise of marriage, taking nude photographs and videos of her, and allegedly pressuring her to have sexual relations with other men in Ghazipur district. According to information, the accused police constable Mohit Yadav has denied the allegations and claimed that the girl traps people to extort money. In a phone conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, the girl alleged that she was being pressured to change her statement. She also claimed that Yadav had offered her Rs 4 lakh and said he could not marry her, but later contacted her after she approached the police and promised to marry her if she withdrew her allegations. “He had a relationship with me. How can I let him marry someone else?” she said, alleging that he had promised to marry her once she became an adult. Yadav, meanwhile, said he was due to get married and was under considerable pressure because of the case. He denied the allegations of sexual exploitation, although he acknowledged meeting the girl and spending time with her. The case falls under Dildarnagar police station limits in Ghazipur. A departmental inquiry into the complaint is under way. Read the report... What is the case about? On October 20, the student released a video seeking action against the constable. She alleged that Yadav had promised to marry her, taken her to a hotel and photographed and filmed her without clothes. She further alleged that he later blackmailed her and sent her to meet other men for sexual relations. In the video, she also said that her family was no longer supporting her and that she felt she had no one to turn to. How the two met on a train Yadav, who is from Pratapgarh, belongs to the 2025 batch of constables. He was posted to Ghazipur in April 2026, his first posting, and is currently stationed at the Bhadaura police outpost under Gahmar police station. He lives in government accommodation. The girl is from a village in the Dildarnagar area, around 15 km from the outpost. The student said she met Yadav on May 3, 2026, while returning from Lucknow with her aunt on the Howrah-Amritsar Express. According to her, Yadav was returning to Ghazipur after visiting his home in Pratapgarh following a period of leave. They were seated next to each other and began talking. “He told me he was a constable and asked me to save his number in case I ever needed help,” she said. Student alleges he took obscene photos and videos The girl said their friendship gradually developed and Yadav began talking about love and promising marriage. She alleged that he took her to a hotel, where he photographed and filmed her without clothes. According to the student, Yadav later told her that his parents would not agree to their marriage and that they would need to earn money for their future. She alleged that he then instructed her to meet men and lure them into agreeing to sexual relations. According to her account, she was told to give a missed call once a man agreed, after which Yadav’s associates would arrive and catch him. “I believed him and did what he told me. He sexually exploited me himself and also made other people exploit me,” she alleged. She claimed that he sent her to meet several men, including a doctor, and later began blackmailing her. She rejected his allegation that she ran a sex racket, saying he had been the one sending her to meet other people. These allegations have not been independently established. Student alleges pressure to withdraw complaint The student said Yadav’s marriage had now been arranged with someone else, and she did not want him to marry another woman after their alleged relationship. She claimed that he had offered her Rs 4 lakh but said he would not be able to marry her. She also alleged that her family wanted to end the matter because of the fear of social stigma. According to the student, Yadav called her on the morning of October 22, after she had complained to the police. She alleged that he said he was ready to marry her and asked her to come to him, but told her to change her statement first. “He said he would marry me once I became an adult, but I had to change my statement and say that he had done nothing to me,” she alleged. The student said the sexual encounters had taken place both with and without her consent. She said she wanted justice. Constable denies allegations, accuses girl of extortion Yadav said he first interacted with the girl on the train when he noticed someone recording her video. He claimed that the girl asked him to get the video deleted. He said he reprimanded the person recording it and ensured that the video was deleted. According to Yadav, the girl asked for his phone number as he was getting off the train, saying she might need help because he was posted at a nearby police station. He said she later called him and they began having ordinary conversations. He acknowledged meeting her and going out with her but denied the allegations of sexual exploitation. Yadav further alleged that the girl had relationships with several other people and claimed that her call detail records would reveal this. He also disputed her claim about her age, saying she had previously told him she was an adult. He alleged that she had told him her father held a government job, whereas he was a truck driver. Yadav claimed that she trapped people and extorted money from them. “It is not necessary that someone is the victim simply because she is a girl,” he said, adding that he was due to get married and was under significant pressure because of the case. These claims are also allegations and have not been independently verified. Student says she has struggled to get action The student said she first approached Ghazipur Superintendent of Police Vinay Kumar Singh on October 5, but alleged that her complaint was not heard. On October 17, she approached Zamania Circle Officer Ankit Tiwari, who recorded her statement, according to the report. She alleged that while she was returning, Yadav pressured her to change her statement and forced her to sign a document. On October 20, she released a video demanding action against the constable. According to Zamania Circle Officer Ankit Tiwari, a departmental inquiry was under way following the complaint against Yadav. “Further action will be taken on the basis of whatever emerges from the inquiry,” he added.

Massachusetts enforces a deadline for firearm registration as it nears the polls, raising concerns about the legal ramifications for compliant gun owners. In stark contrast, Idaho's ballot proposal to designate an official state firearm serves as a tribute to its hunting heritage without direct legal consequences.

"Entirely unbecoming in a democracy": Pushkar Dhami slams Kharge over remarks against PM Modi
stories.summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday criticised Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his remarks concerning Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father and targeted Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav over his alleged use of the term “infiltrators” for the people of Uttarakhand. Dhami questioned the Congress party’s alliance with the Samajwadi Party, saying it must decide whether the alliance or the self-respect of Uttarakhand was more important to it.

California judge pauses voter probes in 9 states over unreliable data, then delays ruling for appeal

This ruling follows concerns regarding the reliance on flawed data by federal agents during their investigations. Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín stated that the investigations risked intimidating eligible voters ahead of the elections. The case was brought forward by several civic organizations advocating for voter rights.

Meet Siddharth Vikram, the eighth grader who turned his brother's car accident into an idea for...
stories.summary: Siddharth Vikram has crafted ReHappy, a groundbreaking app that turns the monotony of physical therapy into exciting game-based challenges for young patients. Inspired by his brother's recovery journey, Siddharth's initiative aims to make rehabilitation fun and engaging. Earning a $25,000 prize in a national competition has propelled his vision forward, and he is now seeking technical guidance to refine the app's clinical application and features for youth rehabilitation.

SBI inaugrates centre of excellence for cybersecurity
stories.summary: The inauguration of CyRIS by SBI marks a significant step in advancing cybersecurity measures and threat intelligence in finance. Centered around THINK, INNOVATE, and DEFEND, it promotes a cooperative approach among banks, fintechs, and regulators to strengthen resilience. CS Setty, SBI chairman, underscored that bolstering cybersecurity is crucial for maintaining customer trust and proactively addressing threats, alongside regular training for employees and raising customer awareness on digital safety.

stories.title: Indiana husband secretly withdrew $220,823 before divorce; court split assets fairly
25 Arizona voters wrongly flagged by Trump administration regain voting rights days before midterms
stories.summary: Twenty-five US citizens in Arizona have regained their voting access after being wrongly flagged as possible noncitizens. Their registrations were restored following court-ordered mediation between Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap and Attorney General Kris Mayes on October 23. The agreement ended a lawsuit over the restrictions, allowing the affected citizens to vote in the November 3 midterm elections.

stories.title: Georgia rejects 700-acre data-centre campus twice in seven months
Why do people overpay for used cars with mileage just below round numbers?
stories.summary: A recent study showed that used car dealers profit from mileage readings just under round-number thresholds. The researchers analyzed millions of transactions to determine pricing impacts of left-digit bias. Buyers often overlook minor differences in mileage, focusing instead on the first digit. This inattention allows dealers to charge more for cars that appear to be better value.

stories.title: Irish father loses wedding ring in Italian stream; 3 strangers fly to Ireland to return it
stories.summary: During a delightful family vacation in Italy, an Irish father accidentally lost his wedding ring while enjoying time with his kids. Determined to recover it, his wife enlisted the help of three local good Samaritans who tirelessly searched the river for three days. Miraculously, they located the ring and even journeyed to Ireland to return it personally, forging unexpected bonds between the Irish family and their Italian rescuers.

stories.title: Congress to hold ‘Vote Bachao' rally at Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1; Amit Shah to lead padayatra in T'gana on Nov 2
stories.summary: Congress party president Mallikarjun Kharge announced a rally in New Delhi to protest vote theft allegations. The rally, titled 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao,' aims to challenge the special electoral roll revision process. Meanwhile, BJP leader Amit Shah will participate in a counter-march in Telangana on November 2. The political tension arises from differing accusations regarding electoral irregularities and vote deletions.

stories.title: DMK’s ‘maternal uncle’ jibe at CM Vijay over women’s safety in Tamil Nadu
'Thank God Ram didn't hit minority': UP CEO on caste bias allegations over voter slips row
Buffalo’s $800K Triangle House returns to market for just $479K
‘Baseless and false’: Israel def min rejects Netanyahu-army chief rift reports
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has denied reports of military tensions concerning potential actions against Iran. Katz stated there are no plans for an attack before the upcoming elections. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also rejected claims of disagreement with military chief Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir. In an interview, Netanyahu suggested that he had given instructions regarding the Iranian regime recently.

stories.title: Scarlett Johansson buys $27.5M Manhattan penthouse for $13M
stories.summary: Scarlett Johansson and Colin Jost have purchased a co-op penthouse in Manhattan, which took seven years to sell. The property was initially listed at $27.5 million and underwent several price reductions before the sale. It spans 6,000 square feet and features numerous luxurious amenities, including six bedrooms and seven bathrooms. The previous owners had made extensive renovations before selling, which likely facilitated the eventual sale.

stories.title: BJP protests across states over Kharge's 'baap' remark at PM Modi; demands apology
stories.summary: In response to Mallikarjun Kharge's recent remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi, BJP activists took to the streets in various locations including Bihar, Jammu, and Bengaluru. The protests, spearheaded by local BJP leaders, called for an official apology from Kharge. While Congress rallied behind Kharge, the BJP accused him of demonstrating a lack of respect towards Modi and his family, igniting a national debate on political respect and decorum.

stories.title: Rahi’s native land seek recognition for literary legacy
Rahi @100: Man of wit, words and verse
'He is aged, can say such things': TMC Mamata faction MP defends Kharge amid 'baap' remark row
'Unforgivable': MP minister Vishvas Sarang slams Kharge over remark on PM Modi
stories.summary: In a recent event marking Dr. Krishna Singh's birth anniversary in Patna, Madhya Pradesh minister Vishvas Sarang took aim at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for his disparaging remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late parents. Sarang criticized the need for greater respect towards cultural customs surrounding the deceased, labeling Kharge's comments as wholly unacceptable. He condemned the Congress party's silence on the matter, voicing concern over their current political behavior.

stories.title: 'We hear you': Rahul Gandhi's message to traders in Delhi amid anti-CEC stir
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has publicly backed the traders in Delhi struggling from the ramifications of ongoing protests and governmental restrictions. He pointed fingers at the administration for hampering commerce by suspending metro services and blocking roads. Traders are reportedly facing losses of around Rs 3,000 crore following previous rallies in October.

Meet Violet Clinton: New York student tracked 11,377 moths using beer-soaked T-shirts
Indian woman loses job in Ireland over visa delays, turns deportation notice into comedy
stories.summary: An Indian woman who moved to Ireland in 2022 to study at Trinity College Dublin is now using her real deportation notice in stand-up comedy performances. Jaishree Malik, 25, lost her job after delays in extending her immigration permission left her unable to work. Despite receiving further job offers, she could not resolve her visa status and now plans to return to India voluntarily on November 14.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi acquitted in 2018 defamation case over remarks on Amit Shah
stories.summary: A special MP/MLA court in Sultanpur dismissed a defamation case against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Monday. This case originated in 2018 due to remarks Gandhi made about Amit Shah during a rally. Vijay Mishra, a local BJP politician, filed the complaint alleging Gandhi's comments were defamatory. Rahul Gandhi appeared before the court in 2023, where he secured bail successfully.

stories.title: AI model uses face photos to estimate biological age, predict survival risk in cancer patients
stories.summary: A new AI model, FAHR-Face, estimates biological age and predicts cancer patient survival risk using facial photos. This model was trained on millions of images and showed an average error of about five years. Alongside this, another model identified high-risk cancer patients based on their appearance, highlighting significant survival differences. While results were promising in the US and Netherlands, further validation is needed in other populations.

stories.title: Mecca country officials to hold joint meeting in Tehran; discuss regional security
stories.summary: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey are set to visit Tehran for a joint meeting. This will be the first high-level contact since the renewed Houthi conflict escalated. The meeting aims to discuss regional security, drawing on Iran's experience with national security. Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure have increased, prompting military responses from the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen.

stories.title: Tharoor On Lula Victory: Congress MP hails Brazil poll result; warns on Brazil–US tensions
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor welcomed Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election as Brazil’s president in a recent post. Tharoor emphasized Lula’s commitment to social inclusion, economic justice, and poverty alleviation after his closely contested victory. The election reflects Brazil’s preference for democratic resilience and cooperation amid rising right-wing movements in Latin America. Issues surrounding the voting process emerged, with disputes raised by both campaigns before result announcements.

stories.title: Minnesota farmer's 300-acre farm at centre of will dispute; 2026 court ruling reverses estate reopening
stories.summary: In a significant Minnesota inheritance case, the state Court of Appeals has reinstated a 2017 ruling concerning the estate of farmer Clarence Vatthauer. Disputes arose from conflicting wills dated 1982 and 1989, leading to a previous court's decision being vacated. The appeals court's ruling underscored the necessity of procedural compliance and the need for finality in estate administration, reshaping the understanding of inheritance law.

stories.title: Beyoncé's childhood home in Houston finds buyer as fans flock to see the property
stories.summary: Beyonce's childhood home in Houston, Texas, found a buyer after being listed for $1.275 million in April 2026. Her family purchased the 1935 property in 1987 and lived there until 1994. The 4,010-square-foot house has undergone extensive renovations, including upgrades to its kitchen, bedrooms and outdoor spaces. Its connection to the singer attracted multiple offers and interest from fans across the United States.

stories.title: Artist bought a Giacometti chandelier for £250 in London; decades later, it sold for £2.922 million
stories.summary: A chandelier created by Alberto Giacometti sold for £2.922 million at a Christie's auction in February 2023. Originally purchased for £250 by British artist John Craxton in the 1960s, it remained in his family until his death. The chandelier was commissioned by art patron Peter Watson for the literary magazine Horizon, which published many famous authors. It underwent extensive authentication process before its auction, confirming its historical significance.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi's convoy involved in minor accident on Purvanchal Expressway
Leafy spurge may have arrived in North America through a Massachusetts ballast dump in 1827
stories.summary: Leafy spurge is an invasive plant that was first recorded in Newbury, Massachusetts, in 1827. It spread rapidly across the northern United States and southern Canada during the early 1900s. By this time, it was established in several states and regions, including Ontario and Iowa. The plant has significant ecological impacts, often replacing native vegetation and causing issues for grazing animals.

stories.title: PM Modi congratulates Brazil's Lula on re-election, says will advance Global South cooperation
Elon Musk pledges SpaceX shares to 72 million American children
Trump Claims Trade Imbalance: accuses Canada of exploiting US; says deal likely but no rush
stories.summary: Donald Trump has voiced concerns that Canada has been exploiting trade advantages over the United States for years. He asserts that talks between the nations are nearing a satisfactory agreement for the U.S. economy. Trump advocates for a sustainable deal rather than a temporary fix, criticizing Canadian tariffs and calling for transparency in trade practices. Despite the friction, he remains hopeful for a resolution to the ongoing trade conflict.

stories.title: ABBA’s Chiquitita raised over $5 million for UNICEF in 45 years; how the 1979 hit continues to protect children
stories.summary: ABBA's song Chiquitita has raised over US$5 million for UNICEF since its release in 1979. This funding supports various programs aimed at protecting vulnerable children from abuse and violence. The pledge originated during a concert at the United Nations to promote children's rights. In 2021, ABBA extended its support by pledging royalties from another song to UNICEF.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia’s Singapore plan: How Riyadh aims to protect Asian oil supplies from 2027
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is set to store crude oil in Singapore starting in the second half of 2027. This arrangement aims to enhance energy security in the region amid supply disruptions. Singapore's Jurong Rock Caverns will provide storage facilities for Saudi crude oil supplies. The agreement will allow Saudi Aramco to bring supplies closer to key Asian markets.

stories.title: BJP files police complaint against Kharge over 'baap' remark targeting PM Modi
stories.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party has lodged a police complaint against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in Patna. The complaint relates to Kharge's remarks about Prime Minister Modi during an event during 139th birth anniversary Bihar's first CM, Shrikrishna Singh. Krishna Kumar Singh, a BJP worker, demands an apology from Kharge within 24 hours. The initial report was filed at Kotwali police station, then transferred to Gandhi Maidan.

stories.title: 'Gotta stop killing them to know who we're dealing with': Trump says top Iranian leaders gone
'Utilizing Iran for politics': IDF chief, Netanyahu clash over military action ahead of Israel elections - report
stories.summary: Tension brews within Israel's leadership as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and IDF chief Eyal Zamir disagree on possible military action against Iran. This clash before elections raises eyebrows about political motives behind military strategies. Netanyahu highlights the imminent threat Iran poses and urges immediate action during Trump's administration. As the election approaches, Netanyahu faces tight competition from Gadi Eisenkot, suggesting possible political deadlock with no clear majority in view.

stories.title: 'Had enough': Thousands protest in Prague against Czech government's public media funding overhaul
stories.summary: Thousands gathered in Prague to protest government proposals affecting public television and radio funding. The planned changes would replace licence fees with state budget allocations, raising concerns about media independence. Critics argue that these measures may expose broadcasters to political pressure and reduce their financial stability. Public media employees announced plans for a strike on November 3, with a larger rally scheduled for November 15.

Trump praised Netanyahu's effectiveness as a leader throughout their joint military efforts, despite previous tensions regarding their strategies towards Iran. This endorsement marks a notable moment as it's uncommon for a sitting U.S.

stories.title: Riyadh airport partially reopens: Saudi intercepts Houthi ballistic missile, drones
stories.summary: A Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, claiming to protect the capital. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described King Khalid International Airport as unsafe for travellers and staff. The airport administration designated terminals for domestic and international flights despite warnings. Additionally, attacks against Yemeni civilian sites by Saudi warplanes were claimed to be extensive. Claims made by both sides regarding missile interceptions and airstrikes remain unverified.

EAM to UN: Lead during global crises, don’t just be a spectator
Massive fire engulfs Shiv Market near Jammu Railway Station, 35-40 shops gutted
John Stamos’ former California mansion drops from $13 million to $6.4 million after renovations
stories.summary: John Stamos’s luxurious California mansion has experienced substantial price drops since 2025. Initially, this Mediterranean-style estate in Calabasas was priced near $13 million, but after renovations by the current owners, it now stands at about $6.4 million. Stamos originally acquired the property in 1991 for $430,000 and sold it in 2001, illustrating the complexities in marketing highly personalized high-end real estate.

stories.title: Philadelphia Orchestra marks 14th China tour with $10.5m gift for global tours and new music
stories.summary: David L Cohen and Rhonda R Cohen have made an impressive commitment of $10.5 million to the Philadelphia Orchestra. This significant donation aims to fund international tours and foster cultural exchanges, while also introducing new music initiatives worldwide. Their contribution will establish the Fund for Cultural Diplomacy, enhancing the orchestra's role as a cultural ambassador, alongside launching the Artistic Innovation and Discovery Fund to spotlight underrepresented composers.
