Bel Air's 4,500-ton concrete mansion hits market for $36.5 million after nine-year project
stories.summary: A stunning new mansion in Bel Air has hit the market for a cool $36.5 million, slated for completion in 2026. Over a painstaking nine-year period, this exquisite residence was crafted utilizing robust reinforced concrete and expansive glass walls. With six spacious bedrooms and nine lavish bathrooms, it showcases luxury amenities throughout.

stories.title: Old deeds and a 1926 ruling shaped Florida rail land dispute as court rejects trail compensation claims
stories.summary: In a recent ruling, the US Court of Appeals clarified property rights as Florida landowners sought compensation when a railway corridor transformed into a public trail. The court determined that the railway held fee simple ownership of the land, supported by historical deeds and a condemnation judgment, nullifying any reversionary rights for landowners. Ultimately, this ruling emphasizes the significance of historical property rights in present-day legal scenarios.

stories.title: Scottish pickle business supplies 400 shops and targets £500,000 in 2026 sales
Archaeologists uncovered a 15th-century ship beneath Barcelona during car park construction
stories.summary: During the renovation of a former fish market, archaeologists made a fascinating discovery: the remains of the medieval ship Ciutadella I, dating from the 15th and 16th centuries. This vessel, containing around 30 ribs and seven planks, reveals valuable details about the maritime heritage of the region. With conservation measures in place, efforts are focused on safeguarding this archaeological treasure for further exploration and understanding.

stories.title: Ohio lowers Guilford Lake 20 feet for $14M dam repairs, refill set for 2027
'Disgrace at so many levels': Shashi Tharoor reacts to removal of Raihan Vadra's photos from exhibition
Iris Sets Auction Record: Monet canvas fetches €50mn in Paris; France hails new mark
stories.summary: At a Paris auction, Claude Monet's painting titled Iris fetched an astounding 50 million euros, setting a new record for artwork sold in France. The event not only celebrated this remarkable sale but also marked the centenary of Monet's passing, with three more of his exquisite paintings featured at the auction. Additionally, Christie's auction saw impressive sales from a variety of artworks, including several by Monet.

stories.title: Police Labrador rescues missing 70-year-old hiker in Hawaii; he now wants to adopt her
stories.summary: After missing for over a day in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, 70-year-old David Arai was successfully located by Trina, a skilled police dog, who led the search team through dense foliage. Found two miles from his rental car and suffering from dehydration, Arai expressed immense gratitude to his rescuers and is now contemplating adopting Trina, who has proven her tracking abilities with two recent rescues.

stories.title: Australian farmer turns poultry waste into power, fertiliser and natural food dye
'Can't drive into future looking at rearview mirror': India calls for urgent UNSC reforms
New Study Of Westminster Sarcophagus: Roman coffin holds medieval abbot; identity still debated
stories.summary: Excavations at Westminster Abbey have unveiled a medieval abbot's remains within an ancient Roman coffin, dated to the time between AD 987 and 1052. Notable candidates for the identity of this abbot include Ælfwig and Wulfnoth, who once steered the Westminster Benedictine monastery. The coffin, rich in history, has been preserved and examined since its 19th-century discovery, and today, visitors can appreciate its elaborate inscriptions.

stories.title: Paul Walker founded a Haiti relief group in 2010; it helped 13,093 people in 2025
stories.summary: A decade after the untimely death of actor Paul Walker, his humanitarian endeavor, Reach Out WorldWide, is creating a significant impact. In 2025 alone, ROWW assisted over 13,000 individuals through various global disaster-relief initiatives. This organization mobilizes skilled volunteers to meet immediate community demands following calamities, operating at no cost to families in need, all while upholding Walker's legacy of providing swift assistance during crises.

stories.title: 'Shaurya commandos' prepared: ITBP chief flags ‘ongoing’ China faceoff along Arunachal border
Ontario farmer rejects C$16 million offer to protect his 164-acre fruit farm
stories.summary: Charles Stevens and his family have decided to protect Wilmot Orchards by placing a conservation easement on the property. This easement effectively restricts future development for nearly 1,000 years, ensuring continued agricultural use. Their decision counters pressures from developers seeking to convert farmland into housing. The Stevens family aims to preserve the land for future generations of farmers.

stories.title: Finnish watchmaker Kari Voutilainen’s limited-edition steel watch sells for $1.016 million at auction
stories.summary: At a recent Phillips auction, an exquisite stainless-steel timepiece crafted by renowned watchmaker Kari Voutilainen commanded an impressive $1.016 million, far surpassing its estimated value. The Voutilainen 28Sport Limited Edition features a stunning blue guilloché dial complemented by a striking black onyx center. Originally acquired in 2021, this watch's sale underscores the increasing allure of exceptional and rare watches within the collector community.

stories.title: Portland man turns $48,412 backyard makeover into $85,000 rental business
stories.summary: Rob Nachbar skillfully turned his once-simple backyard in Portland into a thriving rental space known as Pong Springs. This five-year renovation, which cost $48,412, prioritized weather-resistant structures and enhanced privacy features. Since its launch on Swimply, Nachbar has generated approximately $106,000 in revenue. The yard not only hosts various events but also provides the family with a serene private retreat—combining leisure and financial success.

stories.title: Sudan’s RSF fighters deliberately targeted atleast 43 hospitals during el-Fasher siege: Report
stories.summary: A recent BBC investigation has uncovered alarming evidence of the RSF's assault on numerous healthcare facilities in el-Fasher, Sudan. The findings reveal egregious breaches of international humanitarian law and suggest potential war crimes. The conflict has tragically resulted in healthcare workers being killed, injured, or kidnapped, significantly worsening the humanitarian crisis. UN officials have characterized the situation as possessing attributes of genocide due to persistent ethnic hostilities.

stories.title: 2 Election Commissioners complained against poll panel officer, but Cabinet Secretariat took no action: RTI
'Lifting sanctions will make Putin stronger': Zelenskyy on Trump ties
'No standing to lecture India': New Delhi hits out at Pakistan over minority rights at UN
Jason Momoa buys Queenstown estate for NZ$15 million, NZ$3.5 million above valuation
stories.summary: Jason Momoa has recently acquired a significant property in Queenstown, New Zealand for NZ$15 million. The estate, formerly owned by Sir Sam Neill, demonstrates the increasing interest in the local real estate market. Property values in the region have risen significantly, attracting overseas buyers. Momoa has deep connections to New Zealand, having visited frequently for leisure and work. He has also invested in the local film industry and nightlife scene.

stories.title: Texas farmer grows from 27 to 10,000 sheep by grazing solar farms across 40,000 acres
stories.summary: JR Howard experienced hardships early on with only a small number of sheep, making it tough to earn a living. However, after landing a grazing contract with solar farms, he expanded his flock and income significantly. This eco-friendly grazing method is being embraced by renewable energy companies as a cost-effective way to manage vegetation, while farmers benefit from expansive grazing land without hefty property expenses.

stories.title: California family spends $4,000 and 200 hours turning its yard into a free Jurassic Park attraction
stories.summary: In Granada Hills, a family has dedicated $4,000 to create an elaborate Jurassic Park-themed display for Halloween. After investing over 200 hours, they've constructed life-sized dinosaur replicas and an automated escape show, complete with grand entrance gates. Open to the public at no cost, this attraction fosters community spirit as neighbors flock to capture the experience and enjoy this festive installation.

stories.title: Congress defaming India to shield Nehru-Gandhi family: PM Modi
stories.summary: “Dimagi naxals have captured Congress so much that it has lost its ability to think. Those who used to cause destruction in forests are now determined to wreak havoc on the country through Congress,” PM Modi said, referring to hardcore Left elements accused of being sympathetic to Maoists and now vocal in protests against EC and govt.

stories.title: Media Losses Cloud Empire: MrBeast’s $5bn business leans on his fame; long-term durability in doubt
stories.summary: MrBeast has transformed his YouTube fame into a business empire valued at $5 billion, spanning chocolate, television and financial technology. His Feastables brand generated $250 million in sales and over $20 million in profit in 2024. However, his media business lost nearly $80 million despite strong revenue. With major investor backing and a fintech acquisition reaching seven million users, MrBeast faces the challenge of turning online popularity into sustainable, profitable businesses.

stories.title: 'Keep it up': Trump backs Ramaswamy's attack ad against Ohio rival
stories.summary: In his post, Trump did not directly address the allegations of abuse but attacked Acton, writing: "I suggested, on the other hand, that Vivek should keep it up, and let everyone listen to the mother of a defective, dishonest, and incapable Candidate, explain how the daughter is a DISASTER who, uncontrollably, lies, cheats, and steals!"

stories.title: 'He put it back': Trump says Ukraine's Starlink restored, stays silent on Musk
stories.summary: Ukraine depends heavily on Starlink for communications between military units, coordinating operations and receiving early warnings during Russian missile attacks. The satellite-based network also supports the use of drones, which Ukraine deploys both to strike Russian targets and to defend against incoming attacks. Disruptions to connectivity can therefore affect the military's ability to operate drones and respond to Russian assaults.

stories.title: Goose Creek Estate Listed: Quirky 1958 ranch hits market at $1.227 million; licensed short-term rental
stories.summary: Nestled at 108 Hampton Avenue, this unique property in Goose Creek is now on the market. It boasts three distinct kitchens, creatively themed bedrooms, and a generous indoor pool. Spanning 5,390 square feet, this estate is perfect for multigenerational families or as a lucrative short-term rental option. The outdoor spaces are ideal for entertaining.

stories.title: Necklace nearly sold for £15 at car boot sale fetches £99,000 at auction
stories.summary: Imagine a dusty car boot sale where a unique necklace fashioned from human hair and whale bone was nearly sold for just £15. Fortunately, it caught the eye of an expert at Ewbank's auction house, revealing its immense worth, which fetched an incredible £99,000 at auction. This story underscores the vital role of appraisals in recognizing hidden treasures that often go unnoticed in clearance sales.

stories.title: In call with Israeli counterpart, PM Modi says urgent need to restore West Asia peace
stories.summary: PM Modi said he had received acall from Netanyahu during which the leaders reviewed the sustained momentum in bilateral ties and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the partnership. Modi did not mention Netanyahu’s invitation in his post on the conversation. “We exchanged views on developments in West Asia and underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region,” Modi said on X.

stories.title: Collisions Fall After Wildlife Overpass: I-25 crossings cut crashes by up to 91%; Colorado plans six more
stories.summary: A network of wildlife crossings in Colorado has reduced collisions along Interstate 25 by approximately 85 percent. This system includes fencing, underpasses, and an overpass which opened in December 2025. Recent studies show a significant decline in wildlife-related crashes since the introduction of these measures. Various species, including elk and pronghorn, have begun using these crossings effectively.

stories.title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
stories.summary: PM Modi and his Polish counterpart Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.

stories.title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
stories.summary: The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.

stories.title: Govt plans colour-coded driving licence for Indians, foreigners
stories.summary: Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.

stories.title: Centre flags data gap, regulatory hurdles in curbing hospital mark-ups
stories.summary: The Union govt has told the SC in its affidavit that margins on hospital consumables can range from 100% to 1,000% or more, highlighting concerns over the high mark-ups patients often face on supplies used during treatment. However, a senior official told TOI that the govt does not have the data needed to assess margins across hospital supplies and determine whether wider controls are warranted.

stories.title: Movie glorifies violence, generalises graft in medical field: IMA
stories.summary: In a letter, dated Oct 22, to I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak sought an impartial review of the promo video for the upcoming film and appropriate corrective measures from its makers. It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of National Medical Commission.

stories.title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
stories.summary: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child “must be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort alone”.

stories.title: Sonia Gandhi makes Instagram debut, shares first look of her upcoming book
stories.summary: In her first post on Instagram, Sonia shared a video of her welcoming the first copies of her autobiography “Belonging: A journey of love” which is set to be released on Nov 10. The video showed her holding up the book and then sharing sweets with daughter and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. “It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” Sonia wrote on the post.

stories.title: Will decide on any notice to remove CEC according to rules: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla
stories.summary: Both the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha chairman had rejected previous notices from the opposition, saying their allegations “do not prima facie meet the high constitutional bar for removal proceedings”. Birla noted the process for removal of the chief election commissioner was the same as for removing a Supreme Court judge.

stories.title: Resignation by Justice Yashwant Varma may end Lok Sabha proceedings
stories.summary: Justice Yashwant Varma’s name still figuring on the list of judges on the HC website had bolstered the view. However, sources said legal opinion, backed by a court verdict, that an HC judge’s resignation comes into effect as soon as he resigns may prevail in what was earlier seen as a legal grey area.

stories.title: MEA calls out UN report for saying Dawood Ibrahim's D-company India-based
stories.summary: First secretary in India’s permanent mission to UN, Raghoo Puri, was responding to a report by Ben Saul, the special rapporteur on the ‘Promotion and Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms while Countering Terrorism’. He said this presented member-states with a fait accompli, an unfortunate situation for an organisation already facing challenges to its legitimacy.

stories.title: Karoline Leavitt says her previous job was obviously not for Katie Zacharia who survived as press secretary for 5 days
Hospitals ‘overcharging’ is a malpractice: Govt to Supreme Court
stories.summary: In an affidavit filed in SC on the issue of capping prices of all medicines and medical consumables, chemicals and fertilisers ministry said that patients have a very low bargaining position with respect to hospitals, resulting in various malpractices. The affidavit noted the irony of India being home to companies making cheap drugs but patients here having to pay way above the manufacturing price, as well as patients being subjected to overcharging by hospitals.

stories.title: After 2005 rat removal, three seabird species on a Pacific island grew up to tenfold over decades
stories.summary: The successful eradication of invasive rodents in 2005 has greatly influenced seabird populations on Surprise Island. Researchers closely monitored seven seabird species to document their recovery post-eradication. While some species thrived quickly, others needed more extended observation to show signs of improvement. Notably, noddies saw a significant increase in breeding pairs, whereas red-footed boobies showed a more gradual recovery.

stories.title: Kuwaiti H-1B doctor in Ohio poisoned girlfriend with abortion drug to terminate pregnancy, became US citizen lying on his Form N-400
Google India, Telegram executives appear before NCPCR over CSEAM
stories.summary: Meta has submitted its response following the appearance of Meta India chief Arun Srinivas and senior executives of the company before NCPCR last month over the inquiry instituted after it took cognisance of allegations concerning paid s on Instagram that allegedly facilitated access to Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM)/CSEAM. Meta’s response is under scrutiny, sources in NCPCR said.

stories.title: Vanessa Hudgens bought a 1922 LA home for $5 million; after renovation, she sold it for $6.7 million
stories.summary: In 2018, Vanessa Hudgens acquired a charming historic residence in Los Angeles from Gary Oldman for almost $5 million. She renovated and redesigned the space, ultimately selling it to Ronan Farrow and Jon Lovett in February 2022 for an impressive $6.725 million. The 1922-built house, fondly known as Little DeMille, boasted rich heritage, beautiful gardens, and artistic enhancements by Hudgens, showcasing her flair for style.

stories.title: Ellis Building Hotel Conversion: Aperture buys site for $10.3m; Marriott Tribute Portfolio rooms planned
stories.summary: The iconic Ellis Building, erected in 1922, is set to undergo a transformation into a chic boutique hotel, managed by Aperture Hotels and affiliated with Marriott's Tribute Portfolio. This revitalization aims to breathe new life into the historic space, following previous redevelopment failures. The project promises about 95 to 105 stylish guest rooms, complemented by a modern restaurant and bar, aligning with similar projects in downtown Phoenix.

stories.title: 21 years on, double life term for Jammu terror attack that killed baby, 2 others
stories.summary: In his order on Wednesday, principal sessions judge Ramban Ajay Kumar Gupta rejected defence arguments that the attack had taken place more than two decades ago when Sharief was young, his long incarceration and possibility of rehabilitation. Besides the life sentences, the court imposed two separate terms of 10 years on Sharief under various sections pertaining to murder and arms act offences.

stories.title: Govt defends cancellation of Wangchuk institute’s land allotment, alleges role in last year’s unrest
stories.summary: The claims have been made in an affidavit filed on Wednesday in which Wangchuk is also accused of inciting “violence in Leh on Sept 24, 2025” in which four people were killed and scores injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood and Sixth Schedule status for the Union territory (UT) of Ladakh.

stories.title: Engineer Builds Rental Business: Ohio couple turns cave into cash; social media drives bookings
stories.summary: Bryant Gingerich and his wife Amy turned a sprawling 34-acre land into a thriving hospitality destination known as Dunlap Hollow. This charming getaway features an array of unique accommodations, including a quaint cottage, an A-frame, and an adventurous cave stay. By leveraging social media marketing, they attracted a steady stream of guests, leading to impressive profits.

stories.title: Roe 8 Corridor Rehabilitation: 200,000 plants and 97 species return; ecosystem only 30% restored
stories.summary: Almost ten years post the controversial Roe 8 highway initiative, Western Australia is witnessing a promising wave of ecological recovery. Recent studies have reported a remarkable resurgence of local wildlife and native plant life. Rehabilitation efforts, which have culminated in planting over 280,000 seedlings, are welcoming back species such as Carnaby’s black cockatoos.

stories.title: Centre betrayed us, now want full statehood for Ladakh: Sonam Wangchuk
stories.summary: Wangchuk said the representatives of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) had come prepared for Oct 22 talks in Delhi as a follow up of the May 15 meeting in Leh, with the expectation that the MHA and Ladakh bodies' respective drafts on contours and powers of UT-level body and district councils, would be discussed.

stories.title: New norms to limit fuel leaks, protect EV batteries in rear-end crashes
stories.summary: In a notification, road transport ministry has also made the automotive standard, AIS-192, mandatory for Event Data Recorder (EDR) from Oct 2029 if it is installed in any car. The EDR feature is not mandatory for all cars, and it remains an optional feature. EDR records crash details, which help establish what happened immediately before and during a collision. It is similar in purpose to an aircraft’s flight-data recorder.

stories.title: DHS can't knock on the doors and ask people about their immigration status, rules federal judge
Olivia Wilde sells Studio City home for nearly $1m less than asking
stories.summary: Olivia Wilde recently offloaded her Studio City residence for $5.23 million, a price tag that fell short of her original purchase. Designed by architect Barbara Bestor, the home boasted a sleek modern-ranch aesthetic. Initially on the market for $6.2 million, the sale concluded in December, adding to her previous real estate transaction in Silver Lake, sold at $4.2 million. Meanwhile, rumors swirl about her relationship with art dealer Caspar Jopling.

stories.title: Amazon loses 240 million acres of forest, risking rainfall disruption
stories.summary: According to a recent report, the Amazon has lost 97 million hectares of primary forest by 2025. Most forest loss is attributed to human activity, particularly land clearing and fires. The disruptions to moisture pathways during dry seasons raise critical concerns for the ecosystem. A strong El Niño expected in late 2026 could exacerbate these issues and increase fire risks.

stories.title: PM Modi calls for stronger global institutions; takes ‘failed product’ jab at Congress
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the need for stronger global institutions during his address at the NDTV World Summit. He argued that the current global system struggles to address new challenges, particularly in international relations. Modi also criticized Congress leadership for failing to effectively launch their leader, calling it a burden on the party. Furthermore, he highlighted India's role in international cooperation, especially during the Covid-19 pandemic.

stories.title: North Dakota farmer to earn $5,250 a year for turning erosion-prone land into grassland
stories.summary: In North Dakota, a retired farmer is turning erosion-susceptible farmland into lush grassland to secure annual earnings. Through a state conservation program, he anticipates earning $5,250 over five years. This initiative encourages farmers to repurpose unproductive land, benefiting wildlife and soil health. With interest exceeding available funds, discussions are underway to seek federal assistance to enhance the program's impact on farm income and conservation.

stories.title: Hawaii coral study finds reef sounds help larvae settle on coated structures
CEC impeachment: Speaker Om Birla says fresh motion against Gyanesh Kumar will be examined as per rules
Man builds WWII-style bunker beneath his garden with 35ft tunnel and hidden beer lift
stories.summary: Dave Billings, a fabricator from Derbyshire, has dedicated 11 years to creating an underground garden project. His construction includes two bunkers connected by a long passage, which was inspired by World War II escape tunnels. Billings designed a lift disguised as a beer keg to facilitate drink delivery underground. He plans to connect the bunkers to his home through a concealed entrance leading to an old well.

stories.title: A Texas man turned 10 acres into a $100,000-a-year glamping business with just $12,000 down
stories.summary: Garrett Brown launched Cameron Ranch Glamping on a picturesque 10-acre plot in Houston, beginning with a minimal budget. He cleverly applied land hacking methods that streamlined utility connections while steering clear of complicated planning processes. The business flourished initially with a geodome, later evolving through zero-cost revenue-sharing arrangements. Rather than relying on third-party bookings, he focused on direct guest engagement, chronicling his experiences in his book, The Glamping Investor.

stories.title: Natco’s generic SMA drug approved; ‘clinical trial’ labels trigger Kerala row
stories.summary: CDSCO says no bioequivalence study required for oral solution; company says labels on free bottles were part of standard packaging protocol

stories.title: Indian diaspora could pay price for West’s immigration backlash, warns Sushant Sareen
stories.summary: As Trump blames France’s unrest on immigration and urges Macron to close borders, expert warns law-abiding Indians could get caught in the crossfire

stories.title: $34M Brookline mansion could set new record, surpassing Brady-Bündchen sale
Texas woman's home sold for $20,000 over unrelated debt; eight years later, court reopens dispute
stories.summary: A Texas woman whose home was auctioned for $20,000 in 2018 over an unrelated debt has been allowed to continue challenging the sale. Francine Lee Lankford claims the property was her permanent home and legally protected from such a sale. On October 21, 2026, an appeals court ruled that her claim required further examination, but did not restore her ownership.

stories.title: Dark side of glow-ups: The ugly truth of India's beauty trends and what you need to be aware of
Indiana lawmaker resigns after he was caught shoplifting from Walmart stores. He says he's under medical evaluation for cognitive decline
Netanyahu invites PM Modi to light Independence Day torch, hails decades-old ties
He left banking to revive a closed US wool mill; 12 years later, it supplies the military
stories.summary: A Connecticut wool mill that closed in 2013, leaving 85 workers jobless, has been revived by former investment banker Jacob Harrison Long. He bought the 475,000-square-foot factory in 2014 despite having no manufacturing experience. Twelve years later, the mill employs about 50 people and supplies fabric for US military uniforms. Long now hopes to expand textile manufacturing across New England.

stories.title: US accuses Canada of interference in midterm elections, Carney denies charges
Even sick leave needs approval here: Indian techie shares three months' experience of moving from US to India on the same job, same company
Mike Tyson earned $400 million, went bankrupt; now his perfumes are worth $50,000
Raihan Vadra’s protest photos spark political row, Congress alleges censorship, BJP hits back - all you need to know
Defence, space & nuclear energy: PM Modi, Poland's Tusk bat for deeper ties, doubling trade by 2030
US restaurant that offered free meals in protest against ICE to shut down permanently
Barbara Corcoran's $16M NYC penthouse becomes a beach house on Fifth Avenue
Michigan neighbours accuse each other of flooding their land; both awarded damages
stories.summary: A years-long dispute between neighbours in Michigan over flooding and water flowing across their properties resulted in both sides receiving compensation. A jury awarded $85,000 to William Michael Coan and Cindy Plant and $91,250 to Robert Ercolani. On October 20, 2026, the Michigan Court of Appeals upheld both awards and an independent drainage plan intended to address the flooding.

stories.title: France unrest: Macron vows ban on 'illegitimate' protests in coming days
stories.summary: In response to escalating unrest, French President Emmanuel Macron unveiled plans to prohibit unauthorized protests while ramping up security measures. Following extensive riots and vandalism, authorities brace for further gatherings this weekend. Trade unions and recognized groups will be directed to alternative protest paths to mitigate potential damage, with the initial disturbances rooted in student protests spurring broader demonstrations against rising living costs, just ahead of France's upcoming presidential election.

stories.title: London duplex once home to Keira Knightley lists for £11.5M
stories.summary: After an extensive two-year renovation, the Hyde Park Gardens duplex in London stands elegantly restored. Spanning 4,071 square feet, the lavish residence boasts three bedrooms and bathrooms, complemented by a private terrace overlooking four acres of communal greens. Available for £11.5 million, it’s perfect for those craving luxury and convenience, with nearby attractions including Connaught Village and accessible transport at Lancaster Gate and Paddington stations.

stories.title: ‘No permission needed to hoist national flag’: Neha Bora tells Delhi HC, challenges police notice
Yorkshire couple's straw-bale home, built in 2018, now listed for £2.75 million
Entrepreneur Rebuilds Beauty Brand: Nurse turns $500 into $100m; now backs Watch & Sea
stories.summary: Courtney Adeleye made a remarkable shift from nursing to entrepreneurship by founding The Mane Choice, a haircare brand that achieved impressive success. Initially starting with a few products, the overwhelming demand prompted the addition of supplements, accelerating the brand's growth. Ultimately, The Mane Choice surpassed $100 million in annual sales, culminating in its acquisition for $61.5 million in 2019.

stories.title: Indian-origin man, 24, killed in Canada highway crash days after permanent residency approval
'No political family faced as much injustice': Akhilesh meets jailed Azam Khan, targets BJP
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav met Azam Khan in Rampur district jail as the Samajwadi Party prepares for upcoming elections. Yadav accused the BJP government of targeting Khan's family with false cases and political vendetta. During their meeting, they discussed strategies for all 403 Assembly constituencies, gathering input from alliance partners. The SP leader emphasized the importance of justice and fairness in Rampur while planning to fulfill Khan's vision for education.

stories.title: Minnesota couple’s $27,000 neighbour dispute ends with $20,000 privacy award reversed
stories.summary: In Minnesota, a conflict brewed between two couples over a shared driveway and the removal of a tree. The Stahleys performed maintenance on the Rubys' land without consent, leading to a legal battle. Ultimately, the court awarded the Rubys $27,000, with $20,000 for invasion of privacy. However, the appeals court overturned the privacy ruling, necessitating further proceedings and adjusting the damages for tree removal.

stories.title: Oregon woman’s breast cancer diagnosis inspires husband’s gaming community to raise $1 million for research
stories.summary: When Jessica Conwell confronted the daunting challenge of triple-negative breast cancer, her husband Matt leaned on his gaming community for support. This passionate group rallied together, spearheading fundraising activities that amassed a remarkable $55,000 in their inaugural event. Inspired by early success, they continued their efforts, ultimately raising over $1 million for critical cancer research.

stories.title: In 1926, Frankfurt installed 10,000 modern fitted kitchens; today, volunteers are rescuing them
stories.summary: In the year 1926, Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky revolutionized domestic design by creating the Frankfurt Kitchen, aimed at maximizing cooking efficiency for urban dwellers. While around 10,000 of these iconic kitchens were initially integrated into Frankfurt residences, many have since succumbed to renovations. Today, preservationists are dedicated to conserving the remaining kitchens, adapting them with modern appliances while respecting their historical integrity.

stories.title: ‘Inconsistent with policy’: Bikaner House on removal of photos from Raihan Vadra’s exhibition
‘Not change regime, but break country’: BJP accuses Congress of colluding with foreign powers
Netanyahu denies report that Trump blocked planned Israeli strike on October 10
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel has refuted allegations that President Donald Trump interrupted a military mission planned against Iran. A Financial Times article suggested that Israel had intentions for airstrikes on Iran’s nuclear facilities, which were ultimately dropped due to Trump's disapproval, influenced by worries regarding economic fallout before the midterm elections, particularly concerning fuel prices.

stories.title: ‘Stand against hate’: Mamdani celebrates Navratri with Hindu New Yorkers after Illinois temple shooting plot
Sofía Vergara sold Beverly Hills villa for $13.7 million, had listed it for $19.6 million in 2022
stories.summary: Sofía Vergara has officially sold her stunning Tuscan-style estate in Beverly Hills for $13.7 million in April 2024. Initially listed at $19.6 million in July 2022, after significant renovations, the price was reduced. Vergara, who acquired the property in 2014 for $10.6 million with Joe Manganiello, achieved a $3.1 million profit before expenses, boasting seven bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, and luxurious amenities throughout.

stories.title: Meet Chaz, 13, who raised $4,000 for charity despite a herniated disc
After months of coyote complaints, LA toddler bitten; DNA confirms attack
‘Rahul Gandhi, Raihan Vadra’: BJP takes 'launch' jibe as photo exhibition row escalates
stories.summary: Political tensions have escalated following the removal of photographs from Raihan Vadra's exhibition at Bikaner House. BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia criticized the Gandhi family for allegedly promoting Raihan for political ambitions. Raihan Vadra expressed concerns about censorship and the impact on artistic expression following the objections from the venue management. Both Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Robert Vadra have expressed their support for Raihan in this matter.

stories.title: ‘Hope peace & normalcy return’: MEA condemns attacks on Saudi airport, oil field
How the High Museum of Art grew from one home to a cultural landmark
New York court reverses $400,000 mortgage foreclosure judgment after years of legal battle following husband’s death
stories.summary: A recent ruling by an appeals court has overturned a foreclosure decision related to a property in Babylon, New York. The court determined that Bank of America did not give the borrower adequate notice prior to starting foreclosure procedures and failed to show that it had the necessary standing in the case. Consequently, the court rejected the bank's request for a summary judgment against the estate of Alice McNamara.

stories.title: 'Congress spreading anarchy': BJP draws parallel between France and Delhi protests
CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka seek more time, skip Delhi Police questioning
'They have the right to protest, argue': Ex-BJP leader Annamalai questions govt's handling of CJP protests
'Beacon of hope': Polish PM Donald Tusk hails ties with India, calls PM Modi a 'friend'
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited India to strengthen bilateral cooperation between India and Poland. He highlighted the absence of conflicts of interest and shared values between the two nations. Both leaders discussed expanding economic opportunities through the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement. Tusk emphasized the positive economic developments achieved by Poland and India over the last 35 years.

stories.title: 1 Indian killed, 2 injured in Dammam airport attack in Saudi Arabia
'You want to protect infiltrators' votes': Amit Shah's sharp attack on Rahul Gandhi over 'vote theft' claims
'Told them to give it to me in writing': Raihan Vadra recounts how events unfolded before photos were taken down at Bikaner House exhibition
stories.summary: Raihan Vadra's photography exhibition, No Idea Is Fine, allegedly faced turmoil at Bikaner House when management objected hours before its start, claiming venue policy violations. While Vadra proposed removing select images, the officials demanded the removal of all 70 photographs, including those depicting the Indian national flag. This sparked outrage among Congress members, igniting debates about censorship and the value of artistic freedom.

stories.title: State by state, some SIR hurdles are falling
stories.summary: States in India are currently reforming voter registration processes by allowing broader document categories for eligibility. Booth-level officers are actively visiting homes to assist voters left out during revisions. Many regions report that discrepancies are being resolved with less bureaucratic procedures. Voter engagement has improved significantly compared to previous years through various initiatives. The overall aim is to facilitate a smoother registration process for all eligible citizens.

stories.title: Mariska Hargitay helped fund testing of 11,341 rape kits in Detroit; 263 convictions followed
stories.summary: American actress Mariska Hargitay helped support a project to test 11,341 sexual assault evidence kits discovered in a Detroit police warehouse in 2009. The kits had remained untested for years, with cases dating back to 1984. Led by Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy, the initiative had secured 263 convictions by April 2025, with investigations continuing across the United States.

stories.title: Lincoln’s 1864 signed photograph, found in an old desk, sells for $149,020
Pompeii’s grandest ancient residence gets €1.4 million restoration
stories.summary: Thanks to a private sponsor, the House of Marcus Fabius Rufus in Pompeii is set for restoration, with a portion expected to welcome guided groups by this Christmas. The renovation focuses on fresco restoration and improved visitor access, addressing the extensive damage the site suffered since its closure in 1980 due to a volcanic eruption.

stories.title: Scottish castle built in 1584 with original fireplaces and staircases listed for £120,000
stories.summary: Baltersan Castle, built in 1584 near Maybole, Ayrshire, is now available on the market for £120,000. This castle, which is roofless and Category A-listed, occupies 0.75 acres of land. Notable figures like Charles Rennie Mackintosh and poets Robert Burns and John Keats have been linked to the property. Although the building retains much of its original structure, planning consent for restoration has expired.

stories.title: EC announces bypoll for Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha seat vacated by L Murugan
‘Finding a place to belong’: Sonia Gandhi makes Instagram debut, shares first look of memoir
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi has joined Instagram to share the first look of her upcoming memoir titled 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'. The memoir will be released internationally on November 10 and recounts her personal journey from Italy to India. It includes reflections on her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi and family tragedies. Due to a publishing dispute in India, HarperCollins India will now publish the domestic edition.

stories.title: Georgia woman sues over neighbour's marijuana smoke despite smoking ban; court dismisses claim
stories.summary: A Georgia woman sued after claiming her neighbour’s marijuana smoke repeatedly entered her apartment despite a no-smoking lease, affecting her breathing and health. Bridget Francis alleged that the apartment management ignored her complaints. However, on October 19, 2026, a Georgia appeals court upheld the dismissal of her claims against a California teachers’ pension fund, ruling that it was legally protected from the lawsuit.

stories.title: INDIA bloc huddle: Leaders to meet virtually on CEC row; SIR irregularities on agenda
stories.summary: INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, will meet via video conferencing on Thursday. They will strategize regarding the Election Commission’s actions surrounding the electoral rolls. Opposition leaders have accused the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of irregularities and demanded his resignation. The bloc plans to continue its campaign against perceived threats to democratic institutions and has submitted a memorandum outlining its demands.

stories.title: California seventh-grader tests potential brain-injury treatment on 350 fruit flies
stories.summary: Alekha Goldberg from California has distinguished herself as a finalist in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. Her innovative research focuses on the neuroprotective properties of methylene blue for traumatic brain injury, utilizing fruit flies in her experiments. The results show enhanced climbing ability and survival rates post-injury.

stories.title: Maldives sinks two retired aircraft to create an unusual underwater reef; coral restoration begins in 2026
stories.summary: Two decommissioned Dornier 228 aircraft are submerged near Kudagiri Island to create a diving attraction. Conservation teams are working to establish an artificial reef by attaching coral fragments to underwater frames. The project aims to combine marine tourism with aviation history while promoting coral growth. Various organizations are collaborating to monitor the ecological impact of this initiative.

stories.title: 'Stand for what's true': Priyanka Gandhi's emotional message for son Raihan after over 70 images removed from exhibition
Texas appeals court upholds $880 refund in rental deposit dispute
'India-based' D-Company tag: New Delhi rebukes UN rapporteur, flags 'glaring inaccuracies'
Emma Stone’s 1926 LA home sells for $4.3 million after renovation, $305,000 above asking price
stories.summary: Emma Stone has beautifully transformed a historic home in Los Angeles, which she bought for $2.3 million back in 2019. After completing significant renovations, she listed the property for $3.995 million in January 2024. Boasting a guesthouse, a larger kitchen, and preserved architectural features, the home quickly sold for $4.3 million just ten days later, showcasing Stone’s savvy real estate acumen.

stories.title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka summoned by Delhi Police day after release
‘Anti-Indian hate is exploding’: US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi flags rising anti-Hindu hate online
US, Israel prepare for fresh Iran strikes as Tehran threatens with ‘Father of All Bombs’
stories.summary: The United States and Israel are preparing for potential military strikes against Iran after the upcoming midterm elections. Iran has announced it will reveal a new weapon called the 'Father of All Bombs' as tensions rise. US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discuss military options recently. Meanwhile, Iranian officials warn of severe responses if attacked, emphasizing improved missile capabilities.

stories.title: 'Successes in eliminating Maoism': PM Modi, EAM Jaishankar wish Amit Shah on birthday
'This evil man will be punished': Union minister Rijiju warns Delhi influencer over 'racial' abuse of Tripura youth
'Tricolor row': What happened at Priyanka Gandhi’s son Raihan’s exhibition at Bikaner House - controversy explained
Drones fall, strikes stall: How Musk's Starshield curbs hit Zelenskyy’s war against Russia
Kuwait-flagged tanker carrying 21 Indian seafarers hit by projectile in Strait of Hormuz; all safe
stories.summary: A Kuwait-flagged oil product tanker, M/T Al Dasma, was struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. All 21 Indian seafarers aboard the vessel were reported safe after the incident on October 21. This event follows previous attacks on vessels in the region, raising safety concerns for Indian mariners. The Indian government is in contact with ship management to ensure ongoing security measures.

stories.title: In Pakistan, Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu calls for early Saarc summit
stories.summary: The visit also saw the two sides signing 20 MoUs, including in areas like defence and maritime cooperation that will be of concern to India. This is not the first time though that Muizzu has called for revival of Saarc. In his independence day speech this year, Muizzu had also offered to act as a mediator between India and Pakistan to advance talks for an early leaders’ summit.

stories.title: British Indian stripped of OBE over rogue landlord allegations
stories.summary: Nirpal Singh Riat told TOI on Thursday that he disputes some of these allegations, which he says are “fabricated”. Regardless, a Hounslow councillor lobbied the honours forfeiture committee, which sits within the cabinet office, to get his honours withdrawn, he told TOI. Once notified, his lawyer wrote to the committee disputing the claims but never got a response.

stories.title: Congo Basin Journey: Ash Dykes loses contact for 16 hours; satellite link restores updates
stories.summary: Explorer Ash Dykes’ team raised concerns after losing contact with him for more than 16 hours during his 434-mile journey through the Congo Basin. The 35-year-old Welsh adventurer is travelling from Nola in the Central African Republic to Mossaka in the Republic of Congo. His team later re-established contact through a Garmin satellite device after Starlink and his power bank failed. Limited connectivity continues to restrict updates from the remote expedition.

stories.title: Texas Ranch State Park Purchase: Foundation buys 650 acres for new park; phased opening from 2027
stories.summary: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation has acquired a family-run ranch in East Texas for future park development. This historic land, held by the Pollard family since 1940 and boasting valuable lakefront access, is set to transition to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department by late 2027. The park will offer recreational opportunities while preserving the area’s ecological integrity, enabling the public to connect with nature.

stories.title: Subway co-founder’s relative buys Connecticut warehouse for $6.75 million, plans renovation
stories.summary: A member of the Buck family has purchased a Danbury warehouse previously owned by the Salame family. This transaction, completed for $6.75 million, signals a commitment to modernizing the site while preserving its industrial purpose. Plans include extensive renovations and the construction of an office building alongside the warehouse. The investment reflects confidence in the local economy and aims to maintain vibrant commercial use of the property.

stories.title: Why are uninsured vehicles not part of crash relief scheme? Supreme Court
stories.summary: Taking note that “Compensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026” has not been notified or publicised, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan directed the govt to publicise it to ensure awareness. People must be made aware of their right to seek interim compensation, it said. Union road transport ministry officials said the scheme will be notified as provided for under Central Motor Vehicle Act.

stories.title: Rosatom completes supply of engineered safety features actuation systems for Kudankulam N-plant units 3 and 4
stories.summary: In total, about 300 items of equipment were manufactured and delivered to the plant – four sets of ESFAS CS in accordance with the number of safety instrumentation and control trains, per each power unit featuring VVER-1000 reactors. ESFAS is the system that monitors the process parameters of a power unit when there is a deviation from normal operation conditions.

stories.title: New norms for DL: Driving tutorial pass mark may rise to 75%, select licence services to be free
stories.summary: Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes. The higher qualifying score of 70% is aimed at making the assessment more stringent. The draft also proposes a defined procedure for online applications to change driving licence particulars, including name and address. Licencing authorities would have to approve or reject applications for changes within 15 days, giving reasons for rejection.

stories.title: Cincinnati’s vacant Terrace Plaza Hotel faces fresh redevelopment hurdles over tax dispute
stories.summary: Cincinnati's iconic Terrace Plaza Hotel has stood vacant since 2008, currently tied up in redevelopment plans. A contentious property tax valuation dispute between the owner and the city's school district has caused delays. This $160 million project seeks to honor the hotel's historical significance while also requiring a resolution of tax issues to proceed with construction, maintaining its vital role in the city’s architectural legacy.

stories.title: Sienna Miller’s £1.75m thatched cottage gets a £200k price cut
stories.summary: Sienna Miller's thatched cottage, known as Thatch, is currently listed for £1.75 million. The cottage, located in Buckinghamshire, offers a blend of historical charm and modern amenities. Originally purchased by Miller in 2008, it features four bedrooms and a stylish country kitchen. It embraces its 16th-century character while providing a peaceful rural lifestyle. The property is presented with a reduced asking price after being initially listed at £1.95 million.

stories.title: Cars to brake on their own: Centre plans AEBS mandate from Oct 2030
stories.summary: As for pre-2030 still-in production models, AEBS would mandatory from Oct 2032. The draft notification, with timelines for different ADAS safety features for cars, would be out soon, people aware of the development said, adding that focus would be more on taxis. They said the proposed timelines take into account the lead time that industry and users would need.

stories.title: SC stays probe against Vijayan & kin for a week to enable him to move high court
stories.summary: Referring to Section 175(4) of BNSS, which requires a report from the public servant’s superior officer before ordering an investigation into a complaint against the public servant for acts done in discharge of official duties, the bench said, “The single judge not only directed registration of FIR, which is the mandate in SC ruling in Vijay Madanlal case, but ordered commencement of investigation and submission of final report.”

stories.title: PM Modi has failed ‘abysmally’ on Manipur, says Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge
stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi what has happened to the Peace Committee which was announced by home minister Amit Shah in June 2023 and what action has been taken on the Supreme Court-appointed Justice Gita Mittal Committee’s recommendations. He also asked what concrete measures have been taken to restore peace, protect citizens and address the continuing security challenges in the sensitive border state.

stories.title: Drug menace next target, says Union home minister Amit Shah; eyes 2029 deadline
stories.summary: Stating that an environment conducive to development has emerged in Kashmir, Northeast and LWE-hit regions, Shah particularly thanked CRPF and its CoBRA battalion as well as Chhattisgarh Police for their role in the decisive fight against LWE. The home ministry will dedicate the remaining part of 2026 and three years after that to freeing the country from the drug menace, Shah said.

stories.title: Tiger shooters got weapons via ‘dead drop’; couriers delivered guns a day earlier
stories.summary: Kunal, who has also been arrested, has emerged as a key character who had been in touch with gangsters Anil Pandit and Randeep Malik for over two months. He had also figured as the source of the weapon used for the murder of a forex-hawala trader in Sonipat last year, sources said.

stories.title: At Jamnagar refinery, Rubio and Ambanis discuss energy, digital infra, giga factories
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump had earlier announced the setting up of a $300 billion refinery in US, with RIL being part of his plank to revive industry in the country and bring back jobs that were offshored. The Mukesh Ambani-led company has, however, not outlined any details. The importance of Reliance has since increased because the Jamnagar complex is where hard Venezuelan crude can be refined.

stories.title: Delhi protests India’s internal matter, won’t comment: Rubio; calls UN experts an ‘oxymoron'
stories.summary: On Tuesday, more than 20 UN human rights experts in Geneva had expressed alarm over what they described as a “repeatedly heavy-handed police response” to peaceful youth-led demonstrations in the national capital. United States secretary of state Marco Rubio brushed aside criticism by “UN experts” of the Indian crackdown as he called them an “oxymoron”.

stories.title: NMC denotifies medical education rules; annual disclosures risk lacking verification
stories.summary: The 2019 Act also states that MARB may conduct evaluation of any institute at any time without prior notice. However, with the denotification, the aspects that need to be included in the evaluation report, such as verification of physical infrastructure, availability of the required number of faculty and review of feedback from students, have also been removed.

stories.title: Jeff Gordon’s foundation helped open Rwanda cancer centre; it treated 18,000+ patients by 2025
stories.summary: In 2012, Rwanda launched the Butaro Cancer Center of Excellence to fill the gap in cancer care services. Since then, it has treated over 18,000 individuals, greatly enhancing local healthcare. The center plays a crucial role by establishing vital diagnostic programs and training healthcare staff. However, challenges such as high drug costs and a lack of specialists remain, affecting survival rates.

stories.title: Florida homeowners sue HOA, alleging a $232,000 roof deposit was paid before the public vote
stories.summary: Homeowners in The Vistas at Phillips Commons have initiated a lawsuit against their homeowners association. They allege that a roofing contract worth $2.1 million was approved secretly before an official vote. The residents claim that a significant deposit was made before the meeting took place, indicating potential financial misconduct. An active criminal investigation is examining alleged irregularities involving both the association and the management company.

stories.title: India deal pretty close, will be different: Trump; pact to exclude unresolved sectors
stories.summary: There has been speculation in certain quarters that the much-awaited deal may not be comprehensive, covering all sectors, and the two sides may like to leave aside the issues which have been particularly nettlesome to have an understanding on those for which they have been able to hammer out agreements.

stories.title: Confidence in poll process key for democracy, halt list of candidates: SC to AP SEC
stories.summary: Senior advocate Maninder Singh, who appeared for YSRCP, said in 19 of the 100 urban local bodies — 13 municipal corporations and 87 municipalities/nagar panchayats — more than 63% of YSRCP candidates were prevented from filing nominations or their nomination papers were torn. Senior advocate Sidharth Luthra, for AP govt, said YSRCP was importing criminal elements from as far as Punjab and fomenting violence only to cry wolf later.

stories.title: RSS-affiliated labour organisation opens first Kashmir office in Pulwama
stories.summary: BMS has been actively working in Kashmir since 2020 after the abrogation of Article 370 and currently has 20 registered affiliated labour unions in the region, Khuchay said. Initially, there were a lot of misconceptions about RSS, he said. However, the BMS functionary claimed that over the years, he had succeeded in convincing the people that RSS was not anti-Muslim, but pro-labour and pro-people.

stories.title: Manhattan townhouse with 41-foot pool gets $1 million price cut
stories.summary: Nestled at 238 West 74th Street, this pristine townhouse dating back 140 years is available for $10.45 million. Spanning around 6,460 square feet, it boasts six bedrooms and six-and-a-half bathrooms. Unique features include a splendid 41-foot heated indoor pool and lush outdoor spaces, combining modern conveniences with historic charm. Its recent renovations enhance the classic aesthetics, and it has seen several price reductions from an initial $14.945 million.

stories.title: Connecticut tenant wins $1.6 million after fall, but landlord's appeal leaves him unpaid
stories.summary: Michael Criscuolo, a resident of Connecticut, faced a life-changing injury after stumbling over construction debris near his apartment. A court ruled in his favor, granting him $1.6 million due to the landlord's clear negligence. Yet, Sim Levenhartz has failed to pay the awarded sum, with an appeal still in progress, prolonging Criscuolo's wait for justice. Meanwhile, the property deteriorates further, racking up municipal fines.

stories.title: Drone-linked narco-terror module busted in Jammu; 804 gm heroin; 1.1 kg opium seized
stories.summary: “Preliminary investigation has indicated a cross-border nexus. Inquiry is underway to identify the source of the consignment, its intended recipients, and persons involved in the network,” police said. The network came to light during the questioning of a 26-year-old man arrested for consuming drugs in RS Pura on Wednesday. Police said, “The arrested man, Sunny Kumar, a resident of Kotli Mirdian, Suchetgarh, revealed about the smuggling module.”

stories.title: Who are the terrorists? J&K and Ladakh high court questions ‘vague’ detention order
stories.summary: A single bench of Justice Wasim Nargal said preventive detention, which allows authorities to deprive a person of liberty without a regular criminal trial, demands the “highest degree of constitutional responsibility and procedural diligence”. The court directed the DC to appear with the detention order, police dossier, material placed before him and records showing his consideration of the case and subjective satisfaction before ordering detention under PSA.

stories.title: Pennsylvania turned fire-damaged land bought for as little as 18 cents an acre into a million-tree park
stories.summary: Promised Land State Park in Pennsylvania originated from the acquisition of fire-damaged land between 1902 and 1904. Through dedicated efforts by the Civilian Conservation Corps, over a million trees were planted, transforming the landscape into a beautiful forested area. Recreation facilities were developed to enhance visitors' enjoyment, although the park faced hurdles like a tornado in 1998.

stories.title: Eva Marcille faces $22,000 HOA lawsuit over unpaid fees and property violations at her Georgia home
stories.summary: Eva Marcille, known for her reality TV fame, is embroiled in a legal battle with her Georgia homeowners association due to claims of unpaid dues and property upkeep issues. The association alleges that Eva has failed to respond to multiple warnings concerning her property's state. Her attorney, Michael T. Sterling, has pledged to vigorously defend her, underscoring potential ramifications for homeowner rights in Georgia.

stories.title: Congress pulls up SBI over data breach, seeks accountability; experts call leak 'no ordinary incident'
stories.summary: Congress has raised concerns regarding a significant data exposure involving 3,897 customer records from State Bank of India. The bank confirmed the leak following alerts from its cybersecurity providers and has since initiated an investigation. Experts warned that the leaked data may pose risks to national security due to the bank's prominence. Meanwhile, SBI assured that customer balances remain safe and are implementing security measures.

stories.title: 7,000 people from 126 districts once hit by Naxalism to attend Ekta Diwas parade in Kevadia
Ankita Bhandari case: CBI serves notice to actress Urmila Sanawar for narco test
'I'm killing this…': Kansas man arrested for threatening to shoot Donald Trump
‘Remain vigilant’: India urges citizens in France to avoid protest sites ahead of fresh demonstrations
stories.summary: The Indian Embassy in France has raised an alert for Indian nationals amid ongoing protests in the nation. Citizens are advised to avoid large gatherings and comply with directives from local officials. With violent outbreaks and curfews emerging in reaction to increasing living expenses, the French government braces for more unrest. Indians living in France should closely follow news updates and keep emergency contacts easily available.

stories.title: Trump's son 'opposed' Iran war, believed US should avoid another Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Donald Trump Jr expressed private opposition to the war with Iran, differing from his father's military approach. Despite sharing his views with close associates, he has avoided public disagreements with his father. The conflict has revealed divisions within the MAGA movement on foreign intervention. Domestic challenges, like rising fuel prices, have affected Trump's approval ratings amid the ongoing war.

stories.title: Man buys $30 drawing at estate sale, later linked to Renaissance master Dürer and valued at $10 million
stories.summary: A drawing bought for $30 at an estate sale in Massachusetts is confirmed to be by Albrecht Dürer. Experts attribute the ink sketch to 1503 and estimate its value between $10 million and $50 million. The anonymous buyer initially believed it to be a modern reproduction, showcasing his artistic instincts. Extensive analysis confirmed the drawing's authenticity and its links to Dürer’s other works.

stories.title: Hilary Duff’s $3.85M Beverly Hills home gets playful family makeover
India sees a drop in GHG emissions in 2025, even as UNEP flags huge gap in global reduction efforts
US top court nixes Trump admin's bid to restrict medical care for transgender inmates
52-acre California vineyard once part of Hollywood star Fred MacMurray’s ranch lists for $22 million
stories.summary: Part of Hollywood actor Fred MacMurray’s 1,750-acre California ranch, the 52-acre Flax Estate and Vineyard in Healdsburg has hit the market for $22 million. Owned by philanthropists Jeffrey and Laurie Ubben, who bought the property for $21 million in 2016, the estate features 26 acres of organically farmed Pinot Noir vineyards and three residences.

stories.title: Minnesota tribe reduces casino land request by nearly 75% after locals raise concerns
stories.summary: The White Earth Nation in Minnesota has reduced its proposed casino land-trust request from nearly 300 acres to 80 following concerns about drinking water, traffic, infrastructure costs, and property taxes. The project, planned for Clay County, has not yet received federal approval and also requires concurrence from Minnesota's governor. Tribal representatives say a decision could come by late 2028 under the most favourable circumstances.

stories.title: San Francisco co-op born after Black displacement gets $23 million boost for 2,400-home redevelopment
stories.summary: Freedom West Homes has acquired crucial funding to embark on an ambitious redevelopment initiative that will yield 2,400 new homes. This project prioritizes the needs of existing cooperative shareholders, ensuring they remain in place rather than face displacement. Notably, it focuses on replacing dilapidated structures while maintaining ownership for Black and immigrant families.

stories.title: Australia’s endangered palm cockatoos get artificial nests; first chick fledges in world-first
stories.summary: A palm cockatoo chick has recently fledged from an artificial hollow in the Cape York Peninsula, marking a positive step for conservationists. They installed 29 artificial nesting hollows to combat the lack of natural breeding sites. This first successful breeding event is a pivotal achievement in palm cockatoo conservation. Ongoing monitoring will assess how well these new hollows can facilitate nesting and chick growth for this endangered species.

stories.title: Rs 50k bond, no Jantar Mantar protest call: What are the conditions of CJP leaders' release
AAIB asks Alliance Air to ‘strengthen simulator training’ for pilots in serious incident probe report
stories.summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau has recommended enhanced simulator training for Alliance Air pilots after a serious incident. On October 8, 2024, an Alliance ATR undershot the runway at Bhubaneswar due to severe rain. Pilots struggled with communication and situational awareness, leading to complications during landing. The investigation noted contributing weather factors such as turbulence and low visibility.

stories.title: Glacier Cliffs Retreat And Stabilise: Study tracks rapid ice loss; long-term collapse less certain
stories.summary: Recent research reveals that Antarctica's glaciers are retreating at a faster pace than earlier predictions had estimated. By analyzing over 15,000 satellite images, scientists focused on the stability of ice cliffs. While some cliffs showed signs of quick retreat, they later stabilized instead of collapsing completely. Factors like water depth and the shape of the underlying bedrock significantly influence glacier stability.

stories.title: Rhode Island Home Price Cut: landmark Reading Room gets $1.2m trim; now listed at $9.75m
stories.summary: The Reading Room, a stunning waterfront residence dating back to 1880, is now available for $9.75 million, down from its original listing of $10.95 million. This beautifully restored Victorian property boasts incredible views of Narragansett Bay, allowing future owners to enjoy a unique slice of coastal heritage. Its charm and character make it an exceptional opportunity for buyers seeking a historic home.

stories.title: Tyler Perry cuts Wyoming mansion price by $3.5 million after $30 million Puerto Rico home purchase
stories.summary: Tyler Perry has reduced the asking price of his Wyoming mansion by $3.5 million, bringing it down to $36 million after reportedly buying a $30 million home in Puerto Rico. Built in 2019, the 37-acre estate features nine bedrooms, 8.5 bathrooms, a home theatre, a cowboy-themed bar, a swimming pool and a guesthouse.

stories.title: 'Shouldn't have come if unwell': Subodh Uniyal defends public reprimand of Daler Mehndi
Sacramento jury awards $33.3 million to physics student injured by a falling tree branch in 2020
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, a jury in Sacramento awarded Michael Flynn $33.3 million after he sustained a brain injury from a dead branch falling during his jog in McKinley Park. The city was found wholly negligent in their tree maintenance and safety checks. Despite the injury, Flynn persevered through rehabilitation to earn his doctorate in physics, advocating for greater accountability in public infrastructure safety.

stories.title: Kirsten Dunst’s former LA home sells for $4.55 million in just nine days
Louisiana’s historic Lincoln Theater set to reopen after years of restoration
In Southern California, five rival supercolonies of Argentine ants are engaged in a war that has led to 15 million deaths already
stories.summary: A tumultuous and deadly rivalry unfolds among five Argentine ant supercolonies in San Diego, resulting in an alarming number of fatalities. These strongly territorial ants engage in relentless battles, disregarding the 'dear enemy effect' common in territorial animals. Surprisingly, studies reveal that these colonies have reached an impasse, maintaining fixed borders even amid continuous aggression, indicating a lengthy conflict without an end in sight.

stories.title: 2 Indian-origin pharmacists jailed in UK over £1.3m NHS cancer drug fraud

stories.summary: Advisory flags violations of Programme Code; asks broadcasters to curb inflammatory debates, strengthen editorial checks

Reba McEntire-backed Texas charity has welcomed over 35,000 families since 1992
stories.summary: Established in 1992 by Reba McEntire, Reba's Ranch House serves as a sanctuary for families of hospitalized patients, having provided aid to over 35,000 families. The house offers not just accommodation and meals but also emotional and spiritual support through initiatives like Room for Hope. Many guests have experienced marked improvements in sleep and anxiety during their stay, reflecting the house's responsive growth to community needs.

stories.title: All India Kisan Sabha threatens govt of 'militant resistance' if it goes ahead with US trade deal
Dallas’ historic theater to relight its tower after $45 million redevelopment
stories.summary: On November 1, Dallas's iconic Forest Theater is poised to make its grand return following significant restoration efforts. With a staggering $45 million injection aimed at modernizing its cultural offerings, the reopening promises live performances and food vendors to engage the community. The relighting of the Tower and marquee heralds a rejuvenated era, fostering support for local artists and revitalizing the South Dallas cultural scene.

stories.title: London residents may keep homes after 12-year fight against estate demolition
stories.summary: In a pivotal decision, Lambeth Council has announced plans to halt the demolition of the Central Hill and Cressingham Gardens housing estates. The focus will shift toward improving existing homes and fostering community ties, sparing residents from the threat of eviction. This significant turnaround, subject to Cabinet approval on October 21, marks a commitment to preserve community integrity and architectural character.

stories.title: Alabama farmer secretly paid strangers’ medicine bills for a decade before his death
Delhi court orders release of CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
stories.summary: A special executive magistrate court in Delhi reserved its order regarding the custody of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. The police sought an extension of three days for their custody following a protest at Jantar Mantar. During the proceedings, Das and Ranka challenged the custody extension in the Delhi high court. The high court advised them to await the SEM's decision before seeking further legal remedies.

London taxi driver’s £40 painting linked to 19th-century Amritsar sells for £75,000 at auction
stories.summary: In a remarkable twist of fate, a British taxi driver's modest £40 purchase at a car boot sale has turned into a windfall, as the artwork, featuring the iconic Golden Temple in Amritsar, fetched an astonishing £75,000 at auction. Thought to be the work of artist Baba Bishan Singh, this event highlights the pivotal role of expert appraisals in unveiling the true worth of hidden treasures in art.

stories.title: Dragons’ Den investor called her idea “pathetic”; she built a £10 million firm
‘Next big challenge is drugs’: Amit Shah sets 2029 target after Naxalism crackdown
OpenAI to train government employees in AI through Mission Karmayogi platform
Delaware marked its state parks' 75th anniversary by planting its 75,000th tree, completing a five-year goal across 17 parks
stories.summary: Delaware celebrates the planting of its 75,000th tree in state parks, coinciding with the park system's 75th anniversary. This achievement contributes to a larger goal of planting one million trees by 2030. The initiative features diverse tree species, driven by the support of community volunteers. Notable trees like the American holly were chosen to improve environmental quality and provide inviting spaces for the public.

stories.title: Lonnie Mack’s iconic Flying V guitar and amplifier sell for $550,000 at auction
stories.summary: The legendary 1958 Gibson Flying V guitar, famously owned by Lonnie Mack and dubbed 'Number 7', fetched an impressive $550,000 at auction. This auction also featured Mack's 1962 Magnatone Custom 440 amplifier, which was crucial to his distinct sound. Mack's guitar, tailored for his innovative techniques, has had a profound influence on blues-rock music for many years.

stories.title: After son’s death, mother’s support group now helps 7,000 men weekly
Monsoon's gone, El Niño isn't: Why India's weather worries are far from over
stories.summary: El Niño is increasingly influencing global weather patterns including agriculture and temperatures in India. Current forecasts predict a warmer winter as El Niño intensifies, which could affect agriculture adversely. Recent monsoon rainfall deficits raise concerns regarding water resources and crop yields moving forward. Different regions may experience varying extremes from drought to flooding in the coming months due to this phenomenon.

stories.title: ‘I'm not a travel agent’: Shashi Tharoor when asked about Rahul Gandhi's foreign trip

Virginia is turning 100,000 tons of demolished bridge concrete into fish habitat; 951 tons already underwater
stories.summary: The Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel expansion project involves dismantling an old bridge and using the concrete for artificial reefs. This initiative helps divert demolition waste from landfills while enhancing underwater habitats. Approximately 100,000 tons of concrete is expected to be repurposed for marine life by 2027. The Virginia Marine Resources Commission manages the artificial reefs that support local fisheries and marine ecosystems. This innovative approach connects infrastructure development with environmental sustainability.

stories.title: Swiss brothers spend £10,000 creating a Greek village in their garden
Mike Tyson’s firm seeks $10 million from Hulk Hogan’s estate over beer deal
stories.summary: Carma HoldCo, which Mike Tyson co-founded, has filed a lawsuit in Florida against Hulk Hogan's estate, claiming a breach of contract worth $10 million. The lawsuit alleges that Hogan's team used Carma's ideas for Real American Beer without permission. Previously, Carma accused Hogan's former executives of poaching, though the defendants assert that no enforceable contract exists. With Hogan's estate valued at around $5 million, this claim could have substantial consequences.

stories.title: Ukraine peace, prisoner release & Trump meeting: What was discussed in Putin's meeting with US envoy Witkoff
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin met with US special envoy Steve Witkoff to discuss potential solutions to the Ukraine conflict. Witkoff presented proposals aimed at reviving negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, emphasizing the need for trilateral talks. During the meeting, they addressed the release of Stephen Hubbard, an American prisoner in Russia, and issues related to economic cooperation.

stories.summary: During a hearing, the Delhi High Court engaged in a light-hearted exchange about Generation Z with Cockroach Janta Party leaders. Concerns were raised about possible violations of prohibitory orders related to protests as well.
